title: Industrial Designer
description:
About Hark

Hark is an artificial intelligence company building advanced, personalized intelligence. One that is proactive, multimodal, and capable of interacting with the world through speech, text, vision, and persistent memory.

We're pairing that intelligence with next-generation hardware to create a universal interface between humans and machines. While today's AI largely operates through chat boxes and decade-old devices, Hark is focused on what comes next: agentic systems that interact naturally with people and the real world.

To get there, we're developing multimodal models and next-generation AI hardware together - designed from the ground up as a single, unified interface for a new era of intelligent systems.

About the Role

We're hiring an Industrial Designer to join Hark's design team, reporting to our Head of Design. You'll help bring the look, feel, and physical experience of our devices to life, taking concepts from sketch to production within the design direction set by the team. You'll work hands-on every day, sketching, modeling, prototyping, and partnering closely with product design, electrical, and acoustic engineers to make sure what ships matches the design intent.

This role sits where design meets engineering: you'll spend as much time with engineers at the bench and at builds as you do at your desk, turning concepts into products that can actually be made.

Responsibilities

  • Develop industrial design concepts for Hark hardware and accessories through sketches, renderings, 3D surface models, and physical mockups
  • Carry design direction from the Head of Design into detailed, production-ready surfaces and design specifications
  • Build rapid prototypes in-house (foam, 3D print, CNC) to test scale, ergonomics, feel, and proportion
  • Support color, material, and finish (CMF) development, including researching materials and reviewing supplier samples
  • Design physical interaction details: buttons, haptics, light, charging, and how devices are held, worn, or placed
  • Work side by side with Product Design, Mechanical, Electrical, Acoustics, and Thermals engineers from first concept through mass production, co-owning the trade-offs that turn a design into a manufacturable product
  • Prepare clear design presentations, renderings, and documentation for team and leadership reviews
  • Travel to suppliers and manufacturing partners as needed to review builds and cosmetic quality
  • Contribute to Hark's evolving hardware design language across a growing family of products

Requirements

  • Bachelor's in Industrial Design or a related field
  • 3+ years of industrial design experience in consumer products, with hands-on involvement in at least one hardware product that reached production
  • A track record of partnering closely with mechanical and electrical engineers to take designs through engineering builds and into mass production
  • A portfolio that shows strong form, detail, and craft, plus the thinking behind your decisions
  • Strong 3D surfacing skills (Alias, Rhino, or similar) and fluency in rendering tools (KeyShot or similar)
  • Fast, expressive sketching and visual communication skills
  • Working knowledge of high-volume manufacturing processes (injection molding, die casting, CNC, finishing) and how they shape design
  • Comfortable taking direction and feedback, iterating quickly, and working through ambiguity
  • Collaborative and low-ego, with a high bar for detail

Bonus Qualifications

  • Experience designing wearables, audio products, or other compact devices with integrated sensors, microphones, cameras, or displays
  • Experience with CMF development and supplier sampling
  • Experience with lighting, haptics, or other physical feedback as part of a product's interaction design
  • Familiarity with mechanical CAD (NX, Creo, or SolidWorks) for working handoffs with engineering
  • Experience designing packaging, accessories, or the unboxing experience

Compensation

The US base salary range for this full-time position is between $150,000 - $350,000 annually.

The pay offered for this position may vary based on several individual factors, including job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. The total compensation package may also include additional components/benefits depending on the specific role. This information will be shared if an employment offer is extended.

title: Network Security Engineer
description:
We are seeking a senior technical leader for the Network Security Engineer. You will define the strategy, architecture, engineering, automation, and lifecycle management of Ford’s global network security platforms. Your work will advance Zero Trust and SASE, strengthen cloud and enterprise connectivity, and help ensure network services are secure, resilient, and highly available.

This role combines deep network security expertise with architecture leadership, automation, operational discipline, and collaboration across global teams. You will partner with engineering and operations teams, business stakeholders, and technology providers to modernize network security and support Ford’s enterprise, manufacturing, cloud, supplier, dealer, and partner environments.

Network Security Strategy, Architecture & Modernization

  • Define the enterprise network security architecture and technology roadmap.
  • Lead strategy for Zero Trust, Secure Access Service Edge (SASE), Prisma Access, firewalls, proxies, Cisco ISE, SD-WAN, wireless, DNS/DHCP/IPAM, and F5 technologies.
  • Design secure, reliable connectivity for Ford’s enterprise, manufacturing, cloud, supplier, dealer, and partner environments.
  • Modernize legacy VPN and DMZ architectures by advancing Zero Trust access models.
  • Establish and maintain security standards, governance practices, and compliance approaches for network security platforms.
  • Partner with technical teams and technology providers—including Cisco, Palo Alto Networks, and F5—to evaluate capabilities, guide implementation, and plan platform lifecycles.

Security Engineering, Automation & Risk Reduction

  • Drive network security engineering and platform improvements in partnership with development and infrastructure teams.
  • Advance network automation and Infrastructure as Code practices to improve consistency, efficiency, and reliability.
  • Lead or coordinate remediation of security vulnerabilities, including urgent and zero-day risks.
  • Apply Agentic AI automation where appropriate to improve security operations and engineering workflows.
  • Champion Full Stack Observability (FSO) and Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) practices to strengthen service health and operational insight.

Operations, Availability & Incident Leadership

  • Support major incidents, change management, technical escalations, and enterprise network security operations.
  • Help ensure 24x7 availability of global network security services through Follow-the-Sun operations.
  • Collaborate with global operations teams to maintain secure, resilient, and highly available platforms.
  • Provide technical direction during complex troubleshooting and network security issues.

Technical Leadership & Collaboration

  • Provide technical leadership and mentorship to network security engineers.
  • Build strong working relationships across network, cloud, security, infrastructure, manufacturing, and operations teams.
  • Coordinate with internal teams and technology partners to align architecture, engineering, and operational practices.
  • Communicate technical strategies, risks, dependencies, and recommendations clearly to technical and business stakeholders.

We recognize that no one person will embody every quality or skill listed below. If you bring deep network security experience and are motivated to modernize and protect complex enterprise environments, we encourage you to apply.

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field—or equivalent relevant experience.
  • Preferred degree: Bachelor of Technology.

Experience

  • 12+ years of enterprise IT experience.
  • 6+ years of network security engineering experience.
  • Experience defining or implementing enterprise network security architecture, technology strategy, or platform roadmaps.
  • Experience supporting enterprise-scale network environments and operational processes.
  • Experience with network automation, incident management, problem management, and change management.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead technical initiatives, troubleshoot complex issues, and collaborate across engineering and operations teams.
  • Experience mentoring engineers or providing technical direction in a complex environment.

Required Technical Experience

  • Strong expertise in Palo Alto firewalls, Prisma Access, Cisco Umbrella, Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA), SASE, and intrusion prevention/detection systems (IPS/IDS).
  • Hands-on experience with Cisco ISE, SD-WAN/SDN, F5 load balancers, and DNS/DHCP/IP address management (IPAM), including TCPWave.
  • Strong knowledge of routing, switching, LAN/WAN, MPLS, IPsec VPN, and DMZ architecture.
  • Proficiency with Wireshark and network packet analysis.
  • Experience with enterprise network operations, technical escalations, incident response, and change management.
  • Experience with network automation and Infrastructure as Code practices.
  • Ability to assess network security risks and vulnerabilities, prioritize remediation, and communicate technical impact.

  • Relevant certifications, such as Cisco CCNA, CCNP, or CCIE and Palo Alto certifications such as PCNSE, PCSE, or PCSP.

Preferred Experience

  • Experience with Agentic AI automation for network security engineering or operations.
  • Experience with Full Stack Observability and Site Reliability Engineering practices.
  • Experience modernizing legacy network access and security architectures.
  • Experience supporting global, 24x7 enterprise environments and Follow-the-Sun operations.
  • Experience working with technology partners such as Cisco, Palo Alto Networks, and F5.

title: Insider Threat Analyst
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

INSIDER THREAT ANALYST

SpaceX is seeking a dynamic and driven individual with a demonstrated ability to work independently and as a member of a team in a fast-paced, high-tech environment. Our goal is to protect some of the world’s most advanced technologies including rockets, Dragon capsules for human transport, inter-planetary transport vehicles, the world's largest satellite communications network, etc. As an industry leader, we are a target of adversaries, both foreign and domestic, focused on slowing us down and accessing our proprietary technology. The work we do will literally safeguard mankind becoming an interplanetary species.

You will be responsible for the research, analysis, production, and dissemination of information relevant to protecting the safety and security of personnel, brand, global assets, intellectual property, and operations at SpaceX. This role will triage anomalous event data and analyze insider threat program datasets to respond to threats posed to SpaceX. You will use comprehensive understanding of various collection methods and platforms to explore new data sources, build effective queries, and combine information from disparate sources.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Conduct comprehensive investigations and analysis in support of SpaceX intellectual property and security
  • Uphold investigation and analytic tradecraft standards including confidentiality, objectivity, lawfulness, timeliness, and use of all available sources of information
  • Collect and analyze available program data to evaluate insider threat risk to SpaceX infrastructure, programs, and operations
  • Triage anomalous event data associated with indicators of data exfiltration, data destruction and other key indicators of concern
  • Conduct internal investigations working with Information Security, HR, Legal, Government Security, Physical Security, and external partners based on information derived from internal and external sources
  • Utilize network monitoring, data analytic, and other tools (DLP/SIEM/UEBA) to identify anomalous activity, initiate investigations and decipher underlying trends
  • Extract and organize insider threat program data to build metrics, reports and case studies addressing mission requirements and timelines
  • Communicate findings in a timely and accurate manner to team members, management, and relevant stakeholders
  • Support employee training and briefings for internal and external audiences
  • Liaise with external industry and government partners to benchmark insider threat program, share threat intelligence, and further investigations
  • Continuously identify and help implement program improvement methods
  • Manage and safeguard sensitive information, including case files, employee PII, and intelligence reports

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor's degree and 2+ years of professional experience in internal investigations, information security, or counterintelligence; OR 4+ years professional experience in information security, internal investigations, or counterintelligence in lieu of a degree

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • 1+ year using a SIEM and/or conducting digital forensic investigations in a government or corporate environment
  • Working level understanding of insider threat program missions, internal stakeholders, and manifestations of insider threats
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Purview for eDiscovery
  • Experience performing business process automation or constructing data pipelines
  • Familiarity with risk-based alerting, detection, and tuning concepts for insider risk
  • Experience conducting preliminary assessments, determining scope, investigation planning, evidence collection/handling, interviewing and reporting findings to internal and external stakeholders
  • Ability to conduct interviews on short notice according to established internal guidelines.
  • Excellent written and oral communication skills, with the ability to produce clear and concise reports
  • Highly organized with a strong attention to detail
  • Ability to adapt to changing priorities and deadlines
  • Can swiftly adapt to new technical environments and workflows
  • Ability to exercise discretion when conducting confidential investigations

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Must be able to work extended hours and weekends as needed to support critical efforts and operations
  • Must be willing to travel ad hoc
  • Active TS/SCI clearance, or ability to obtain one. With an active clearance, candidates will be subject to pre-employment screening including background check and drug/alcohol test as well as random drug and alcohol testing during employment

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

Pay Range:
Level 1: $85,000 - $110,000
Level 2: $100,000 - $135,000

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package at SpaceX. You may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of company stock or long-term cash awards, as well as potential discretionary bonuses and the ability to purchase additional stock at a discount through an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, paid parental leave, and various other discounts and perks. You may also accrue 3 weeks of paid vacation and will be eligible for 10 or more paid holidays per year. Employees accrue paid sick leave pursuant to Company policy which satisfies or exceeds the accrual, carryover, and use requirements of the law.

Those with an active clearance will receive a 10% differential, up to an additional $20,000 annually, once officially briefed into a classified program.

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

  • To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.

Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to EEOCompliance@spacex.com.

title: Director, Development
description:
Copia Power (“Copia”) is a Carlyle-backed energy and digital infrastructure platform that develops, constructs, and operates large-scale assets across the U.S. to accelerate the electrification and growth of the digital economy. Copia Power has over 2,600 MW of energy generation and storage assets in operation or under construction and is actively developing over 15 GW of grid-connected data centers supported by Copia’s portfolio of gigawatt-scale energy campuses comprising more than 25 GW of solar and storage and 7 GW of natural gas generation assets.

At Copia, we pride ourselves on a culture where sustainability is at the heart of everything we do. We are dedicated to making a meaningful impact on the environment, and we believe that achieving this goal requires not just hard work but also enjoying the journey. Our team thrives on connectivity, fostering strong relationships across all levels of the organization. Together, we combine passion and playfulness to drive progress and make a difference.

Job Description:

Copia is seeking a Director, Development to lead the development of Copia's renewable energy and data center project portfolio, guiding projects from early-stage site identification through late-stage commercialization, financing, and handoff to construction. This role sits at the intersection of power and digital infrastructure, requiring creative solutions to deliver energy for both traditional solar and storage projects and large-scale AI and hyperscale data centers in constrained markets.

The ideal candidate will be responsible for leading site identification and evaluation, land negotiations and real estate agreements, permitting and entitlements, power and interconnection strategy, utility engagement, and energy markets across a portfolio of projects ranging from utility-scale generation to 100MW to 300MW+ data center loads by phase. This role requires 10+ years of experience in renewable energy and/or large-scale data center infrastructure development, deep expertise navigating land, permitting, interconnection, and energy markets, and exceptional decision-making, communication, and influencing skills to align cross-functional teams and external partners toward successful outcomes.

The Director, Development will report directly to the EVP, Chief Development Officer, working closely with Copia’s asset management, energy markets, legal, and finance teams in an individual contributor capacity.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Lead a team of subject matter experts to advance early and late-stage renewable energy and data center projects from site selection through commercial contracting, construction handoff, and project financing
  • Manage the development of a portfolio of projects, including budgeting and finances, project timing and planning, risk assessment, and defining priorities based on development metrics and offtake potential
  • Coordinate and manage interdisciplinary teams across land negotiations, real estate, engineering, permitting, interconnection, and legal through construction commencement
  • Facilitate project discretionary permitting, including permit strategy, stakeholder engagement, and representation with local authorities and public meetings
  • Engage with utilities on interconnection, transmission, and power delivery, aligning with Copia's internal generation strategy across solar, storage, and gas
  • Support negotiation of critical project agreements, including site control, PPAs, interconnection and load agreements, EPC contracts, and O&M agreements
  • Manage due diligence on individual or portfolio acquisitions, partnering with the business development and M&A team to assess project risk, complete valuations, and inform transaction structuring

What We Look For:

  • Ability to communicate effectively in verbal and written correspondence.
  • Highly driven with problem-solving abilities, integrity, and strong work ethic.
  • Proactive mindset with the ability to thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.
  • Ability to work effectively within a rapidly changing organization.
  • Demonstrated collaborative partnerships with peers, management, and vendors.
  • Resourcefulness and polite persistence.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • 10+ years professional experience in renewable energy and/or large-scale data center infrastructure development, including exposure to utilities, interconnection, permitting, contracting, and financing
  • Bachelor's degree preferred in finance, engineering, environmental studies, renewable energy, project/construction management, or similar discipline
  • Proven experience with Microsoft Office, including advanced proficiency in PowerPoint and Excel
  • Experience with project management software and a CRM system
  • Ability to work in the Phoenix, AZ office a minimum of 3 days per week
  • Ability to travel up to 30%
  • Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States without employer sponsorship
We are partnering with select search firms for this role and are not accepting inquiries or candidates from additional third-party agencies or recruiters.

Compensation:

At Copia, we carefully consider a wide range of factors when determining compensation, including your skills, qualifications, location, and experience. This role may also be eligible for benefits, performance bonuses, and other perks. We encourage all interested candidates to apply.

Our Benefits:

At Copia, we prioritize diversity and inclusion, fostering an environment where everyone can be their true selves every day. Our commitment extends to providing comprehensive benefits to all employees, such as:

  • Medical, Dental & Vision Coverage (with no premiums)
  • Company contribution to 401(k) plans
  • Annual bonus eligibility
  • Flexible work hours
  • Unlimited paid time off for a healthy work-life balance
  • Paid holidays to celebrate and recharge
  • Wellness and cell phone credits to support personal well-being
  • Life and AD&D insurance for peace of mind
  • Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) for community and support
  • Opportunities for professional development to grow and thrive within the company

We believe that by fostering a culture of inclusivity and offering these benefits, we empower our employees to thrive both personally and professionally.

About Copia:

Copia Power (“Copia”), is a wholly owned portfolio company of the global investment firm, The Carlyle Group. Copia’s platform is focused on developing, owning, and operating utility-scale sustainable infrastructure in the United States. We value diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. For more information, visit .

title: Online Data Analyst - French (CA)
description:
TELUS Digital AI Community

Our global AI Community is a vibrant network of more than one million contributors from diverse backgrounds who help customers collect, enhance, train, translate, and localize content to build better AI models. Become part of our growing community and contribute to the development of innovative AI technologies used by some of the world's largest brands.

Millions of people rely on digital maps every day to navigate, to discover, to find their way. But maps are only as accurate as the data behind them, and data is only as trustworthy as the people who verify it. Your knowledge of Canada's geography, local landmarks, and how people actually navigate your region is something no algorithm can fully replicate. That local intelligence is what makes maps genuinely useful.

A Day in the Life of an Online Data Analyst

In this role, you will conduct structured quality audits on spatial and mapping datasets. Your role is to verify, evaluate, and validate complex geographic and business information using advanced mapping tools and detailed reference materials.

  • Conduct structured quality audits on spatial datasets using mapping platforms, search directories, and GIS-standard evaluation tools
  • Evaluate and cross-reference complex business, geographic, and cultural data entries against multiple authoritative sources
  • Perform root-cause analysis when spatial data points conflict across sources, documenting the discrepancy with precise reasoning
  • Apply detailed evaluation frameworks with consistency and rigor across dozens of geographic, business, and cultural data variations
  • Be open to work across a diverse set of Task Types (e.g. Maps, News, Audio tasks, Relevance)
  • Provide structured feedback that helps refine mapping algorithms and improve geographic intelligence

Why this matters: Accurately verified mapping data prevents real-world navigation errors. Your verification work ensures people can reliably find critical services, reach trusted businesses, and navigate with confidence. At scale, this is infrastructure work that is foundational to how billions of people interact with geographic information.

Why join the project:

  • Fully remote flexibility: Complete work from anywhere with stable internet, structuring your schedule around academic research, consulting, or other professional commitments
  • Structured onboarding: Access comprehensive evaluation guidelines, detailed reference materials, and practical examples before your first live assessment
  • Direct feedback and growth: Receive performance assessments tied to quality metrics so you can refine your evaluation precision
  • Intellectually rigorous work: Each evaluation requires methodical reasoning, framework interpretation, and structured discrepancy analysis.
  • Responsive support team: Contact dedicated contributor operations staff for clarification on guidelines, technical issues, or administrative questions

Qualification path

Requirements:

  • Professional fluency in English and French (native or near-native proficiency required)
  • Residency in Canada for the last 5 consecutive years
  • Being open to work across a diverse set of Task Types (e.g. Maps, News, Audio tasks, Relevance)
  • Advanced analytical thinking and methodical problem-solving ability
  • Deep regional, cultural, and geographic knowledge of Canada
  • Comfort with rigorous guideline interpretation and consistent framework application
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience in analytical, technical, or research disciplines (strongly preferred)
  • Stable internet connection and access to a personal computer

Qualification path

  • Complete your contributor profile and submit a brief background overview
  • Verify your identity through our secure identity verification process
  • Review the open-book study guide and evaluation framework (provided in your welcome materials)
  • Complete an open-book qualification assessment at your own pace within the time given
  • Receive your project assignment and access credentials

title: Medical Coding Auditor
description:
Optum is a global organization that delivers care, aided by technology to help millions of people live healthier lives. The work you do with our team will directly improve health outcomes by connecting people with the care, pharmacy benefits, data and resources they need to feel their best. Here, you will find a culture guided by inclusion, talented peers, comprehensive benefits and career development opportunities. Come make an impact on the communities we serve as you help us advance health optimization on a global scale. Join us to start Caring. Connecting. Growing together.

The Medical Coding Auditor is required to determine the accuracy of claims submitted by a provider to UnitedHealth Group by comparing it to the medical record(s) submitted for the date(s) of service being reviewed. This position supports the identification of suspected Waste & Error of health insurance claims and ensures claims are accurately documented. Candidates must be able to exercise judgement/decision making on complex payment decisions that directly impacts the provider and client by following state and government compliance guidelines, coding requirements and policies. They must confidently analyze and interpret data and medical records/documentation daily to understand historical claims activity, determine validity and demonstrate their ability to provide written communication to the provider. They are responsible to investigate, review and provide clinical and/or coding expertise in a review of claims. They need to effectively manage their caseload and monthly metrics in a production driven environment and ensure they are meeting all compliance turnaround times mandated by the client. The Medical Coding Auditor must be proficient in computer skills and able to navigate multiple systems at one time with varying levels of complexity. They must have the ability to research and work independently on making decisions on complex cases.

You'll enjoy the flexibility to telecommute* from anywhere within the U.S. as you take on some tough challenges.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Performs clinical review of CPT, HCPCS, and modifiers assigned to codes on claims in a telecommuting work environment
  • Determines accuracy of medical coding/billing and payment recommendation for claims
  • This could include Medical Director/physician consultations, interpretation of state and federal mandates, applicable benefit language, medical and reimbursement policies, and consideration of relevant clinical information
  • Determines appropriate level of service utilizing Evaluation and Management coding principles
  • Provides detailed clinical narratives on case outcomes
  • Ensures adherence to state and federal compliance policies, reimbursement policies and contract compliance
  • Identifies aberrant billing patterns and trends, evidence of fraud, waste, or abuse, and recommends providers to be flagged for review
  • Maintains and manages daily case review assignments, with accountability to quality, utilization, and productivity standards
  • Provides clinical support and expertise to the other investigative and analytical areas
  • Participates in team and department meetings
  • Engages in a collaborative work environment when applicable but is also able to work independently
  • Serves as a clinical resource to other areas within the clinical investigative team
  • Work with applicable business partners to obtain additional information relevant to the clinical review

You'll be rewarded and recognized for your performance in an environment that will challenge you and give you clear direction on what it takes to succeed in your role as well as provide development for other roles you may be interested in.

Required Qualifications:

  • Certified Coder AHIMA (CCA, CCS, CCS-P) or AAPC Certified coder (CPC, CPC-I)
  • 2+ years of experience as an AHIMA or AAPC Certified coder
  • 2+ years of CPT/HCPCS/Modifiers coding experience
  • 2+ years strong medical record review experience
  • 1+ year of working in a team atmosphere in a metric driven environment including daily production standards and quality standards

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience in the health insurance business, using industry terminology and regulatory guidelines
  • Experience in Waste & Error principles
  • Healthcare claims experience/processing experience
  • Experience with Fraud Waste & Abuse or Payment Integrity
  • [Internal Posting Only] 1+ year experience of UHC platforms - COSMOS, Facets, CPW, NICE, ISET, UNET
  • Proficient and able to navigate and maneuver multiple systems at one time with varying levels of complexity
  • Strong computer skills with the ability to troubleshoot problems
  • Intermediate experience with Microsoft & Adobe applications (Outlook, Power Point, Word, Excel, OneNote, Teams, PDF)

Soft Skills:

  • Highly organized with effective and persuasive communication skills
  • Strong written communication skills
  • Open to change and new information; ability to adapt in changing environments and integrate best practices
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to interpret data
  • Strong analytical mindset working with medical terminology and/or coding

*All Telecommuters will be required to adhere to UnitedHealth Group's Telecommuter Policy.

Pay is based on several factors including but not limited to local labor markets, education, work experience, certifications, etc. In addition to your salary, we offer benefits such as, a comprehensive benefits package, incentive and recognition programs, equity stock purchase and 401k contribution (all benefits are subject to eligibility requirements). No matter where or when you begin a career with us, you'll find a far-reaching choice of benefits and incentives. The hourly pay for this role will range from $24.00 to $43.00 per hour based on full-time employment. We comply with all minimum wage laws as applicable.

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

Application Deadline: This will be posted for a minimum of 2 business days or until a sufficient candidate pool has been collected. Job posting may come down early due to volume of applicants.

title: Research Data Analyst I
description:
Job Function Summary

Involves gathering, analyzing, and interpreting a wide variety of research data. Designs and conducts research including selecting data samples, developing research instruments, analyzing collected information according to established statistical methods, and developing recommendations based on research findings. Prepares reports, charts, tables, and other visual aids to interpret and communicate data and results.

Generic Scope

Entry-level professional with limited prior experience; learns to use professional concepts to resolve problems of limited scope and complexity; works on assignments that are initially routine in nature, requiring limited judgment and decision making. Employees at this level are expected to acquire the skills and knowledge to perform more advanced work following an agreed upon time in position, through defined training and development planning.

Custom Scope

Under direct supervision, acquires skills and knowledge of professional concepts in research data analysis. Works on small projects or segments of projects with limited scope and complexity.

Department Overview

The Department of Radiology & Biomedical Imaging is one of the largest departments within the School of Medicine, generating more than $40 million in professional fee revenues each year, and submitting grant proposals resulting in $30-40 million of awards each year. More than 90% of the MD faculty in Radiology is based at the Parnassus Campus, including nine of the ten clinical sections and their chiefs, and five of the seven vice chairs. The department has significant clinical and research operations at China Basin, Mission Bay, the VAMC, ZSFG, and Mount Zion. It includes more than 150 academic personnel and approximately 225 staff FTE. In addition, there are more than 90 resident, fellow, and graduate student trainees.

The Research Data Anl 1 position is focused on the collection of clinical data focused on patients treated with PSMA radioligand therapy and peptide receptor radionuclide therapy. A multicenter database is being created to collect data on these patients to understand toxicity, efficacy and see how these drugs are used clinically. The candidate will work under the general supervision and guidance from the supervisor Dr. Thomas Hope. They will also work with Dr. Abuzar Tuchayi Moradi.

Statistical and Data Analysis

  • Under direct supervision, performs basic statistical and data analysis.

Research Data Collection and Preparation

Collects research data and prepares it for analysis.

  • Entering clinical data from the medical record system into the REDcap database.
  • Interpreting imaging reports and converting them to binary data entry format.
  • Determining progressing free survival dates based on imaging and reports.

Study Design

  • Assists with study design proposals and survey instruments.

Report Preparation and Analysis

Assists with report preparation and / or analysis for internal constituents.

  • Reviewing pathology reports and determining appropriate Ki-67 and other variables.

Clinical Data Storage and Documentation

Develops knowledge in areas of storage, documentation and dissemination of computerized data.

  • Collect data on patients to understand toxicity, efficacy and see how these drugs are used clinically.
  • Collection of clinical data focused on patients treated with PSMA radioligand therapy and peptide receptor radionuclide therapy.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training.
  • Acquiring knowledge of research function. Acquiring ability to perform research analysis duties.
  • Acquiring statistical analysis, systems programming, and database design skills to perform research analysis duties.
  • Ability to effectively manage time and see assigned parts of projects through to completion on deadline.
  • Basic consultation and communication skills.
  • Attention to Details.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Previous exposure to Medical Care.

Licenses

None listed.

Certifications

With over 100 locations, the company focuses on delivering high-quality, end-to-end solutions throughout the entire lifecycle of infrastructure projects, from concept to completion, by leveraging industry expertise and a strong commitment to client value.

Role Overview:

This role is the finance point person for the people who fund us: our sponsor and our lender group. Reporting to the Director of Strategic Finance, the successful candidate will own lender and private equity requests, run the cash flow and liquidity forecast, and build and defend the pro forma EBITDA addbacks that our leverage and covenant calculations depend on.

We are looking for someone from a consulting background (transaction advisory, restructuring or similar) who has sat across the table from PE firms and banks, knows what they will ask next, and answers with numbers that tie. The role is also expected to set the standard for how Finance uses AI: this person should already work with AI tools every day and be able to show us how.

What We’re Looking For:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics or a related field. MBA, CPA or CFA a plus.

  • Consulting background required: transaction advisory / financial due diligence (Big 4 or national firm), restructuring or turnaround advisory, or comparable advisory work. Investment banking or leveraged finance experience also considered.

  • Direct experience working with private equity sponsors and banks or private credit lenders: DDQs, lender reporting, QoE and addback support, covenant calculations, refinancings or amendments.

  • Proven track record building and running integrated three-statement and cash flow models, including 13-week cash flow forecasts.

  • Expert-level Excel: complex model architecture, dynamic scenarios, lookups and array formulas, Power Query, and models others can audit.

  • SQL or equivalent data skills strongly preferred; experience with Databricks, Power BI or similar tools a plus.

  • Demonstrated, hands-on use of AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot or similar) in finance work. Candidates should be ready to walk through specific workflows they built and the time they saved.

  • Working knowledge of credit agreement mechanics: EBITDA definitions and addback caps, leverage and liquidity tests, reporting covenants and cure provisions.

  • Preferred: experience in engineering consulting, professional services or AEC; project-based accounting (WIP, unbilled, change orders); Deltek Vantagepoint.

Key Competencies:

  • Precision under pressure: foots every total, bridges every change and flags anything stale before it goes out.

  • Credibility with sponsors and lenders: direct, calm and prepared; knows the difference between a model output and a commitment.

  • Ownership: runs a request from intake to answer without being chased.

  • Builder’s mindset: automates the second time a task comes up, and leaves tools behind that others can use.

  • Clear communication: turns complex analysis into short, defensible answers for the CFO, the sponsor and the lender group.



What You’ll Be Working On:

Lender & Private Equity Requests

  • Own the request queue from our PE sponsor and lender group end to end: intake, owner assignment, due dates, drafting, review and release. Nothing leaves Atlas without a named owner and a tie-out.

  • Prepare responses to lender and sponsor DDQs, follow-up question lists, investment committee (IC) support materials and board reporting inputs, written so they hold up against every document the reader already has.

  • Produce the recurring lender reporting package, including the monthly financials, the rolling 13-week cash flow forecast with variance to prior forecast, and quarterly compliance certificates and covenant calculations.

  • Assemble data rooms and underwriting packages for refinancings, amendments, letters of credit and other credit facilities; act as the day-to-day finance contact for sponsor deal teams, lenders and their advisors.

  • Read and apply the credit agreement: defined terms (Consolidated EBITDA, Liquidity, Net Leverage), reporting deadlines, cure periods and draw conditions, so every figure states the basis it is measured on.

Cash Flow & Liquidity

  • Run the integrated EBITDA-to-cash-flow model (monthly, 18 to 24 months forward): working capital drivers (DSO, DPO, unbilled/WIP), capex, leases, debt service, interest rate swaps, severance and one-time items.

  • Own scenario and sensitivity analysis on collections, payables paydown, revenue growth and cost actions; show clearly where liquidity is tight and what closes the gap.

  • Maintain model discipline: version control, a change log that matches the live inputs, a bridge between every version, and tie-out checks that actually return zero.

  • Partner with Treasury on the weekly cash forecast, revolver availability and letter-of-credit capacity; reconcile the model to actual cash every month.

Pro Forma EBITDA & Addbacks

  • Build and defend the bridge from GAAP EBITDA to Adjusted and Pro Forma EBITDA, with a documented, auditable support file for every addback (restructuring, severance, cost-to-achieve, run-rate savings, acquisition pro formas, non-recurring items).

  • Test each addback against the credit agreement definition and caps and against quality-of-earnings standards before it goes to the sponsor or lenders.

  • Track run-rate savings and synergies against actuals so the addbacks we claim are the savings we deliver.

  • Work with outside advisors and QoE providers on diligence, sell-side or buy-side, and support the VP, Corporate Development with deal models, valuation and post-close integration tracking.

AI, Data & Automation

  • Use AI as a daily tool, not a side project: build and maintain AI-enabled workflows (for example Claude and Microsoft Copilot) that draft DDQ answers, review models, check files before they are sent and answer recurring requests.

  • Pull and shape data directly from source systems (Deltek Vantagepoint, ADP, Databricks, Power BI) using SQL or equivalent, instead of waiting on manual extracts.

  • Turn one-off analyses into repeatable, documented tools that others on the Finance team can run; train colleagues on them.

  • Hold AI-assisted work to the same standard as any other work: every number traced to source, every output reviewed before release.


Ready to take your career to the next level? Join us and be part of a team that values your growth, celebrates your achievements, and empowers you to make a real impact. Apply today and start shaping your future with a company that invests in your success every step of the way!

title: Social Services Specialist
description:
Social Services Specialist

Revision Date: 9/16/2022

Department: Social Services

Employment Status: Full-Time

Program: Family and Social Services

FLSA Status: Non-Exempt

Reports To: Social Services Supervisor

Supervises: N/A

Preference: TERO Ordinance 201-01, P.L. 93-638

Job Summary

The Social Services Specialist is responsible for welcoming clients (un'inas) in need of services to do an intake. The Social Services Specialist will have basic knowledge of all functions within the Na'ini Social Services Programs including but not limited to: Bureau of Indian Affairs (BIA) Welfare, Burial and Emergency Assistance, State of Alaska - Community Initiatives Matching Grant (SOA CIMG) Administration for Children and Families: Child Care Development Fund (ACF CCDF) & Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (ACF - LIHEAP), Community Services Block Grant (ACF - CSBG), Cook Inlet Tribal Council Child Care and Food Cache. A function will be designated to each specialist and it is the specialist's responsibility to follow grant requirements.

Essential Functions

  • Collaborate with Social Services Intake Technician in completing intakes, scheduling, case management, prevention, advocacy and providing referrals internally and externally, answering the phone, maintaining un'ina/family confidentiality and conducting home visits
  • Maintain un'ina records in accordance with the Tribe's standards, local, state and federal guidelines or regulations and comply with internal process for filing (i.e. title pages, sections, archiving), electronic data management system, designated program software and documenting case notes
  • Assist in determining eligibility, completing applications and processing applications in a timely manner, writing pending approval or denial letters, notifying un'ina verbally or in writing of status
  • Responsible for the day to day operation of designated function
  • Develop and provide group presentations internally and externally representing Kenaitze Indian Tribe and Family and Social Services
  • Adhere to grants, reports and budget requirements, timelines and compliance
  • Assist the Social Services Supervisor in strategic planning, interviewing, presentations internally and externally, community outreach, marketing plans, developing policies and procedures and be an active participant
  • Responsible for staying informed in social service program trends and recommending changes in service delivery to the Social Services Supervisor
  • Participate in other administrative duties: such as facilitating/attending regular social services meetings, creating agendas and minutes, finalizing dashboards; developing self-sufficiency plans, case plans and/or safety plans assist in staffing to best meet the needs of the un'ina(s)
  • Cross training is essential, and each specialist will be able to cover other designated functions, be familiar with each subspecialty within Na'ini Social Services to ensure all un'ina needs are met
  • All specialists will assist in shopping/fishing/cleaning/unloading for the food cache, to include but not limited to packing, sweeping, mopping, cleaning freezers
  • Consistently aware and updating internal/external resources and sharing with internal/external agencies
  • As a mandated reporter do reports of harm to the appropriate agency and follow through as needed
  • Facilitate/participate in community agency meetings, meet with other service providers, colleges, etc
  • Be available and able at a moment's notice to change work in a different program, work evenings, weekends and do schedule adjustments, or respond immediately to a crisis/emergency or need
  • Improve the accessibility of other social services programs
  • Ensures compliance with Tribal, federal, state, and local employment laws and regulations, Tribal policies and TERO ordinance

It is the intent of this job description to highlight the essential functions of the position; however, it is not an all-inclusive list. The incumbent may be called upon and required to follow or perform other duties and tasks requested by his/her supervisor, consistent with the purpose of the position, department and/or the Kenaitze Indian Tribe's objectives.

Working Conditions

Lifting Requirements

  • Light work - Exerting up to 20 pounds of force frequently, and/or a negligible amount of force constantly to move objects. If the use of arm and/or leg control requires exertion of forces greater than that of sedentary work and if the worker sits most of the time, the job is considered light work.

Physical Requirements

  • Stand or Sit (Stationary position)
  • Walk (Move, Traverse)
  • Use hands/fingers to handle or feel (Operate, Activate, Use, Prepare, Inspect, Place, Detect, Position)
  • Stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl (Position self (to), Move)
  • Talk/hear (Communicate, Detect, Converse with, Discern, Convey, Express oneself, Exchange information)
  • See (Detect, Determine, Perceive, Identify, Recognize, Judge, Observe, Inspect, Estimate, Assess)
  • Pushing or Pulling
  • Repetitive Motion

Hazards and Atmospheric Conditions

  • Exposure to Dust
  • Wet
  • Noise
  • Vibration
  • Mists or Gases
  • Mechanical Hazards

OSHA Categories

  • Category I - Duties performed routinely require exposure to blood, body fluid and tissue

Equipment and Tools

List Equipment used for job: Computer, Fax, Copier, Scanner and other office equipment

Drives KIT or Personal Vehicle: Both

Travel

  • Local
  • In-State
  • Out-of-State

Qualifications

Education

  • High School Diploma or a combination of education and experience in a related field may be substituted for a degree
  • Bachelor's in Human Services related fields preferred, although year for year experience in lieu of BS or BA

Experience

  • Three (3) years of experience in social and community based programs
  • Experience working with Department of Public Assistance and other State and Federal agencies
  • Experience in the development of community program strategies
  • Experience managing private, state and federal grants; and grant compliance
  • Experience in budget management
  • Experience in policy and procedure development & implementation
  • Experience in public speaking
  • Understanding of public education and health and social services regulations
  • Knowledge and experience working with Alaska Native/American Indian people

Preferred

  • Knowledge and experience working with cultural diversities

License/Certification

  • Must have a valid Alaska State driver's license and must remain insurable under the Tribe's policy, or obtain within 90 days of hire, or, with approval of the hiring manager, sign a *Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) in lieu of having a driver's license to perform the required duties of the position (If Applicable)

Special Skills

In addition to meeting education and experience requirements, Social Services Specialists must possess, or develop before providing program services, the knowledge base and skills necessary to carry out the following:

The knowledge base must include:

  • The terminology commonly used in human services fields or settings
  • The resources available to meet the needs of recipient
  • Knowledge of drug and alcohol abuse treatment options
  • Excellent interpersonal communication skills, including public speaking and presentations
  • Critical Incident Reporting, Adult Protective Services, Office of Children's Services reporting
  • Ability to work with vulnerable populations, child abuse, homelessness, substance abuse, poverty and domestic violence and sexual assault clients/perpetrators
  • The ability to evaluate needs assessments to meet the needs of the population to be served
  • The ability to organize, evaluate, and present information orally and in writing
  • The ability to work with professional and support staff
  • Ability to work independently as well as collaboratively

Conducts business in a service-oriented manner that is attentive, pleasant, respectful and kind when dealing with un'ina, visitors, co-workers and othersThis position is a Covered Position subject to all requirements of the Alaska Barrier Crimes Act (ABCA) and to the Indian Child Protection and Family Violence Prevention Act, (ICPA). ABCA and ICPA requirements apply and must be complied with at all times in order to remain in the position.

*Memorandum of Understanding: Serves as documented evidence that the Kenaitze Indian Tribe has expressed the ineligibility of an employee to operate motor vehicles owned, leased or rented by the Kenaitze Indian Tribe, or to operate a personal vehicle on behalf of the Kenaitze Indian Tribe

title: Retail Technology Quality Analyst
description:
Location: Hybrid in Lawrence, MA (Tuesday-Thursday onsite, Monday & Friday remote)

Job Type: 1-year contract (possibility of extension, however, this is not guaranteed)

Company: The name of our partner organization will be disclosed during the interview process. This is not a direct role with LaunchCode; it is a position through LaunchCode, working with one of our partner companies.

Disclaimer: We are unable to provide work sponsorship for this role. We are unable to consider candidates for this role who have a current or future work sponsorship need (this includes those holding extended OPT Visas).

Our company partner is looking for a Retail Technology Quality Analyst who understands how retail systems support real business operations and is excited to bring that knowledge into the world of AI-driven software testing. In this role, you’ll be primarily responsible for testing POS systems, including Aptos Store 6 and newer point-of-sale platforms, with business-journey testing that may also involve connected retail applications such as Aptos WebIM, Sales Audit, Merchandising, and Retail Analytics. This testing is less about checking individual screens and more about proving that critical store selling, payment, returns, inventory, reconciliation, and operational handoffs work correctly across the broader retail technology ecosystem.

If you’re energized by retail operations, business-process testing, emerging technology, and AI, and want to help shape the future of retail systems, this is your opportunity.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Serve as a primary tester for POS systems, including Aptos Store 6 and newer point-of-sale platforms, validating store selling, payment, returns, exchange, discount, tax, receipt, and end-of-day workflows.
  • Execute business-journey testing that may span connected systems such as Aptos WebIM, Sales Audit, Merchandising, Retail Analytics, and payment platforms, while keeping POS quality as the primary day-to-day responsibility.
  • Test retail operations workflows such as sales transactions, returns, exchanges, tender types, promotions, loyalty interactions, tax behavior, receipts, inventory updates, and downstream impacts across store, ERP, finance, fulfillment, and reporting processes.
  • Collaborate with Quality Engineers, Product Owners, business stakeholders, and vendor partners to execute process-based testing that spans store operations, ERP, inventory, finance, fulfillment, and reporting platforms.
  • Use AI tools to accelerate test design, exploratory testing, defect analysis, documentation, and test reporting.
  • Learn and apply modern test automation tools and scripting languages to support test execution and reporting.
  • Configure and troubleshoot retail hardware setups including POS terminals, scanners, printers, mobile devices, and payment systems.
  • Participate in agile ceremonies and contribute to quality discussions within a Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe) environment.
  • Act as a retail subject matter expert, bringing frontline and back-office retail operations insights into the testing process to ensure software meets the needs of store associates, retail operations teams, inventory and fulfillment teams, finance and reconciliation teams, and customers.

Qualifications:

  • 3+ years of experience working in a retail store environment, preferably in a role involving technology, operations, or omni-channel workflows.
  • Familiarity with retail back-office processes such as inventory management, WebIM workflows, receiving, transfers, fulfillment, reconciliation, merchandising updates, reporting, or exception handling.
  • Ability to think like an end user, identify edge cases, document defects clearly, and communicate risk to technical and non-technical partners.
  • Technically curious and comfortable working with retail hardware, mobile devices, and connected peripherals.
  • Basic scripting experience (e.g., PowerShell, Python, or shell scripting); VBScript experience is a plus.
  • Passion for AI and emerging retail technologies, with a desire to learn and apply AI tools to testing and quality assurance.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills, especially when working with cross-functional teams.
  • Experience using or testing POS, retail store operations, payment, inventory management, or ERP-connected systems is highly desirable; direct Aptos Store 6 or Aptos WebIM experience is a plus.
  • (Bonus) Exposure to robotic arm testing or automation hardware used in retail or logistics environments.

title: Visual Inspection Associate – Sterile Compounding
description:
Thirty Madison is now part of Remedy! You can read more about the acquisition here. We are excited to join forces and continue to revolutionize healthcare accessibility!

As a Visual Inspection Associate, you will be responsible for performing detailed visual inspections of sterile compounded pharmaceutical preparations to ensure products meet established quality standards, inspection criteria, and patient safety requirements. You will identify visible defects, maintain accurate inspection documentation, and support compliance with USP <797>, applicable state Board of Pharmacy regulations, and facility standard operating procedures.

Reporting to QA Compliance, you will work closely with pharmacy operations and quality teams to ensure consistent inspection practices, accurate documentation, and timely escalation of product quality concerns. This role offers the opportunity to contribute directly to patient safety while supporting an expanding sterile compounding operation and its readiness for ACHC/PCAB accreditation.

Comp | Perks | Benefits

  • This is an onsite position located in Missouri City, TX
  • Robust and affordable Medical, Dental, and Vision plan options
  • Vacation time off policy - up to 10 vacation days accrued your first year. Vacation time begins accruing immediately

**Base pay offered may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.

What you get to do every day

Sterile Product Visual Inspection

  • Perform visual inspections of sterile compounded pharmaceutical preparations, including injectable medications packaged in vials, syringes, and other sterile containers, as applicable
  • Inspect products for visible particulate matter, discoloration, cloudiness, clarity issues, and other observable product defects
  • Examine containers for visible cracks, leaks, damaged closures, compromised seals, and other observable container integrity concerns
  • Follow approved inspection procedures, established acceptance criteria, and standard operating procedures (SOPs) to ensure consistent inspection practices
  • Utilize designated inspection stations, lighting, contrasting backgrounds, and other approved visual inspection equipment
  • Identify and appropriately segregate products that fail established visual inspection acceptance criteria
  • Promptly escalate suspected defects, inspection discrepancies, and product quality concerns to QA Compliance
  • Maintain consistent inspection accuracy and attention to detail while performing repetitive inspection activities
  • Complete required visual inspection training, qualification assessments, and periodic competency evaluations

Quality & Compliance

  • Perform inspection activities in accordance with USP <797>, applicable state Board of Pharmacy regulations, and facility SOPs
  • Follow established procedures for product handling, inspection, segregation, and escalation of nonconforming products
  • Ensure inspection activities support product quality, patient safety, and established regulatory requirements
  • Maintain clean, organized, and compliant visual inspection workstations
  • Follow approved procedures for the proper handling and protection of sterile compounded preparations
  • Report observed defects, discrepancies, equipment concerns, and deviations promptly to QA Compliance
  • Support internal audits, regulatory inspections, and ACHC/PCAB accreditation readiness through accurate inspection practices and documentation
  • Participate in ongoing training and continuous improvement initiatives related to visual inspection accuracy, consistency, and compliance

Inspection Documentation & Traceability

  • Accurately complete visual inspection records, including product identification, lot or batch information, inspection results, and identified defects
  • Document inspection outcomes in accordance with established procedures and good documentation practices
  • Maintain complete and traceable records of inspected, accepted, rejected, and segregated products
  • Ensure inspection documentation is completed accurately and contemporaneously
  • Record and escalate recurring defects, inspection discrepancies, or unusual product observations to QA Compliance
  • Support the maintenance of inspection logs, equipment records, and qualification documentation
  • Assist QA Compliance with inspection record retrieval and documentation reviews during audits or regulatory inspections

What you bring to the role

  • High school diploma or equivalent required
  • Previous experience in pharmaceutical manufacturing, sterile compounding, visual inspection, or a regulated production environment preferred
  • Experience performing visual inspections of sterile pharmaceutical products, including injectable preparations, vials, or syringes, strongly preferred
  • Familiarity with visible particulate inspection, pharmaceutical container defects, and established inspection acceptance criteria
  • Understanding of USP <797>, pharmaceutical quality standards, or regulated pharmacy operations preferred
  • Exceptional attention to detail and ability to identify subtle visual defects and product abnormalities
  • Ability to consistently perform repetitive, detail-oriented inspection tasks while maintaining accuracy and focus
  • Strong organizational skills and ability to maintain accurate inspection records and documentation
  • Ability to follow detailed written procedures, inspection criteria, and SOPs without deviation
  • Strong communication skills and ability to promptly escalate product quality concerns
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating with QA Compliance and pharmacy operations
  • Ability to successfully complete required visual inspection training and qualification assessments

Bonus Points

  • Experience performing manual visual inspection of sterile injectable pharmaceutical products
  • Experience in a 503A compounding pharmacy, FDA-registered 503B outsourcing facility, or sterile pharmaceutical manufacturing environment
  • Familiarity with USP <797> requirements and sterile compounding quality standards
  • Experience using visual inspection booths, specialized lighting, contrasting backgrounds, or semi-automated inspection equipment
  • Knowledge of visible particulate identification, container closure defects, and inspection acceptance criteria
  • Experience documenting inspection results, defect classifications, and rejected product dispositions
  • Familiarity with ACHC/PCAB accreditation standards and pharmacy quality documentation requirements
  • Knowledge of good documentation practices (GDP) and applicable cGMP principles
  • Previous experience working closely with Quality Assurance or QA Compliance teams

Physical Requirements

  • Extended periods of sitting or standing while performing detailed visual inspection activities
  • Ability to perform repetitive fine-motor tasks and handle pharmaceutical containers with precision
  • Visual acuity, with or without corrective lenses, sufficient to meet established inspection qualification requirements
  • Ability to maintain sustained visual concentration and attention to detail throughout inspection activities
  • Ability to safely handle sterile pharmaceutical containers and operate designated inspection equipment
  • Work in a controlled pharmaceutical environment requiring appropriate protective clothing and personal protective equipment (PPE)
  • Ability to follow applicable hygiene, gowning, and safety requirements
  • Ability to lift up to 35 lbs

All Company policies and procedures are subject to change without notice based on business needs. This includes, but is not limited to, the locations where we hire remote, hybrid, or onsite employees.



U.S. Applicants Only

The safety and integrity of those seeking employment with us is of the utmost importance and we actively work with our legal and security teams to prevent future incidents.

title: Product Manager
description:
Are you motivated by the opportunity to have a big impact?


The Opportunity

We are seeking a stellar individual for a high-impact role focused on defining monetization strategy within Adobe’s Creativity and Productivity business segment (historically referred to as Digital Media and home to such premier products as Creative Cloud, Acrobat, Photoshop, Illustrator and Firefly). We are a highly visible team responsible for making strategic recommendations that have a significant financial impact.

Our team leads development and refinement of Adobe’s monetization strategy, including monetization of GenAI and emerging agentic capabilities across segments and routes-to-market. We do this by driving initiatives that optimize new and existing offerings via product innovation, product line determination, business model refinement, and changes to offering and pricing strategy.

As such, the right candidate will find this to be a strong foundation for growth and an outstanding opportunity to have a material impact on the business.

What You’ll Do

Our team’s role is to influence the product roadmap to drive significant growth in customer acquisition, product usage, revenues, and profits. This may involve the following activities:

  • Define and optimize the pricing and packaging strategy for offers within the Creativity and Productivity business segment.
  • Collect, synthesize and analyze industry and competitor data.
  • Develop and conduct qualitative customer research.
  • Design and complete quantitative market research including one or more of the following research methods: Build-Your-Own Conjoint, Discrete Choice Conjoint, Gabor-Granger.
  • Perform statistical analysis on empirical data (sales, usage, etc.)
  • Develop financial models that simulate customer behavior and project costs to complete scenario analysis that estimates the impact of proposals on market penetration, company revenues and margin.
  • Develop and present arguments that articulate the strategy and return-on-investment in order to acquire and incorporate cross-functional feedback and ultimately achieve executive approval.

We also ensure smooth execution of our proposals.

  • Engage with engineering, finance, and operational teams to ensure that proposed monetization strategies can be implemented within existing quote-to-cash systems, balancing proposals between ideal monetization potential vs. operationalization
  • Collaborate with Product Management and Product Marketing teams to define product roadmaps to better support monetization goals
  • Set guidelines for direct sales, develop sales plays and training as appropriate.
  • Complete post-mortems to ensure proposals are successful and/or refine.

What You’ll Need to Succeed

We are looking for an analytical wiz with high initiative, a strategic approach and quantitative talent.

  • Proven experience developing pricing and packaging strategies and successfully bringing them to market in a complex matrixed organization.
  • Understanding of emerging GenAI capabilities and their practical application across business processes, customer experiences and operational workflows.
  • The ability to simplify the complex, quickly define the core problem and frame the solution approach.
  • Attention to detail balanced by comfort with ambiguity.
  • Excellent deck-writing, communication, and upward-influencing skills.
  • Strong EQ and leadership ability.
  • Intellectual curiosity.
  • Experience driving consensus in a large matrixed organization.
  • A background in strategy consulting, product marketing, and/or change-management, ideally in software/technology, are all big pluses.
  • Familiarity with creativity and document management solutions and workflows is a plus.
  • MBA or equivalent experience.

About Adobe

Adobe empowers everyone to create through innovative platforms and tools that unleash creativity, productivity and personalized customer experiences. Adobe’s industry-leading offerings including Adobe Acrobat Studio, Adobe Express, Adobe Firefly, Creative Cloud, Adobe Experience Platform, Adobe Experience Manager, and GenStudio enable people and businesses to turn ideas into impact, powered by AI and driven by human ingenuity.


Our 30,000+ employees worldwide are creating the future and raising the bar as we drive the next decade of growth. We’re on a mission to hire the very best and believe in creating a company culture where all employees are empowered to make an impact. At Adobe, we believe that great ideas can come from anywhere in the organization. The next big idea could be yours.


Let’s Adobe together

At Adobe, we believe in creating a company culture where all employees are empowered to make an impact. Learn more about Adobe life, including our values and culture, focus on people, purpose and community, Adobe for All, comprehensive benefits programs, the stories we tell, the customers we serve, and how you can help us advance our mission of empowering everyone to create.


Adobe is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based on gender, race or color, ethnicity or national origin, age, disability, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic. Learn more.

title: Environmental Technician I

title: Executive Director Software Engineering
description:
Calling All Esteemed Leaders! Are you a software engineering leader who excels at solution architecture, technical strategy, engineering quality, and team development? Do you thrive in complex environments where innovation, data, and cross-functional collaboration come together to deliver meaningful value for caregivers? If so, we invite you to explore this leadership opportunity with Providence.

The Role

The Executive Director will shape how Providence uses enterprise application data to inform decisions, improve operations, and create value. As the leader of the data and reporting strategy for Enterprise Business Applications and Technologies, this individual will serve Providence Shared Services and users across the organization by strengthening the data and reporting capabilities supporting Human Capital, Finance, Supply Chain, workforce management, and related enterprise platforms.

The leader will bring business stakeholders, executives, architects, engineers, analytics teams, and service partners together around a unified strategy and operating model. The mandate is to transform fragmented data and reporting capabilities into an integrated, governed, and trusted enterprise ecosystem that reduces duplication, establishes authoritative data sources, accelerates insights through self-service reporting, protects sensitive information, and enables predictive and proactive decision-making.

Beyond defining the strategy, the Executive Director will lead its execution. This includes establishing the roadmap and engineering standards, guiding architecture and delivery, developing organizational capabilities, managing cross-functional dependencies, and ensuring solutions are secure, reliable, supportable, adopted, and continuously improved. The successful leader will balance immediate stakeholder needs with the foundational investments required to create lasting enterprise value.

What You'll Do

  • Responsible for all software solution, architecture strategy, software design and engineering deliverables for the portfolio that they support.
  • Leads the group to design technical solutions that deliver the expected value to the partner, and business objectives to PSJH. Ensures that the technical vision and designs are iterative and well-positioned for successive releases.
  • Anticipates industry and market trends, advises business leaders on new solutions, and consistently defines successful technical solutions that succeed in the marketplace.
  • Guides the creation of conceptual models for new solutions and the future solution direction that incorporate market, technology, and business trends.
  • Advises business leaders on needed capabilities and technologies, and how to build or acquire them to realize the future solution vision, over multiple releases.
