title: Patient Records Abstractor 2
description:
Location: Fully Remote

Employment Duration: 3 months

Patient Record Abstractor fulfills a role as a Medical Coder for UCSF’s physician practices. They review patient records, discharge summaries, operative reports, and other clinical documentation to assign standardized codes for diagnoses, procedures, and services. They apply national and international coding classifications to ensure records reflect the care delivered, supporting accurate reimbursement and reliable clinical data. They have knowledge of Current Procedural Terminology (CPT), International Classification of Diseases, 10th Edition, Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM), and Healthcare Common Procedural Coding System (HCPCS).

The role operates within a healthcare records or billing team and requires close liaison with clinicians, clinical coders, and administrative staff to resolve documentation queries. Coders must maintain currency with coding updates, compliance requirements, and professional standards, and participate in regular audits to monitor coding quality. Expectations include timely processing of case volumes while maintaining high accuracy, adherence to confidentiality and information governance standards, and contribution to process improvements that enhance data quality and coding efficiency.

The Faculty Practice Revenue Management Operations (FPRMO) department is responsible for physician-based coding for UCSF faculty. The team ensures accurate code assignment for professional services delivered across UCSF locations, affiliated community hospitals, off-license practices, and ambulatory clinics.

FPRMO supports a diverse group of providers, including physicians, nurse practitioners, and advanced practice providers, across a wide spectrum of specialties within an academic medical center environment. These specialties include Neurosurgery, Cardiovascular Services, OB/GYN, Gender Reassignment, Rheumatology, and Plastic Surgery.

FPRMO plays a critical role in the revenue cycle by delivering precise and compliant coding for approximately 1.6 million patient encounters annually, supporting both regulatory requirements and optimal reimbursement.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Work in moderate work queues daily as defined by UCSF leadership.
  • Work in simple work queues as needed.
  • Work RFI and edit work queues as needed.
  • Maintain or exceed a 95% accuracy rate.
  • Maintain productivity standards as defined by UCSF leadership.
  • Work proactively with divisions in areas of specialization to assure appropriate revenue cycle practices and compliance with internal and external regulations.
  • Code intermediate procedures/accounts requiring advanced knowledge in charge capture, workflow, hospital operations, authorizations, and the revenue cycle.
  • Resolve Claims Manager and Epic edits to ensure correct coding of services provided, including review of documentation for correct coding, evaluation and management (E/M) leveling, diagnosis coding, bundling issues, and modifier usage.
  • Apply dashboards and processes for continuous analysis of moderate revenue cycle functions of diverse scope.
  • Audit data input to support revenue cycle management.
  • Complete coding work reports, reconcile charge lists, create charge sessions, update DEPs, follow up on credential requests, and perform related coding activities.
  • Verify and correct statistical data abstracted and compiled by lower-level staff, reconcile output statistics, and perform medical coding.
  • Review APeX PB Charge Edit and RFI work queues daily or as assigned, address payor inquiries requiring department review, and resolve claim edits to ensure timely billing.
  • Proactively review assigned work queues and collaborate with faculty and ancillary providers regarding required documentation changes and updates.
  • Run reports related to assigned charges, including missing charge reports, error reports, and other reports supporting charge capture, error resolution, and throughput.
  • Under supervision, analyze charge integrity, reconciliation, and charge linkages from ancillary charging systems for the medical center/health system.

N/A

Required Qualifications

  • 2–5 years of revenue cycle professional fee coding experience or equivalent experience/training.
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to interpret and convey complex clinical finance information in a clear, concise manner.
  • Ability to prepare informative reports and presentations.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to evaluate workflows and systems and propose solutions.
  • Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to collaborate effectively on complex projects in a team environment with staff from a wide variety of business and clinical areas.
  • Ability to pass all classes related to UCSF Medical Center computer systems and UCSF coding and billing applications, which may include off-site billing systems from partner hospitals.
  • Demonstrated intermediate knowledge of medical terminology, CPT, ICD-10 coding conventions, and clinical documentation requirements.
  • Prior experience in a healthcare-related setting.
  • Knowledge of federal, state, and commercial carrier coding and billing standards.
  • One of the following certifications or an equivalent licensure as evaluated by FPRMO management:
    • Certified Professional Coder (CPC)
    • Certified Coding Specialist–Physician Based (CCS-P)
    • Certified Coding Associate (CCA)

title: Staff Software Engineer - Host & Secure Compute Software - Cork, Ireland
description:
Job Description

Company

QT Technologies Ireland Limited

Job Area

Engineering Group, Engineering Group > Software Engineering

General Summary

Qualcomm Cloud Edge in Cork is seeking a Staff Software Engineer to lead development of Linux-based system software for next‑generation datacenter and secure compute platforms. This role focuses on host‑side software, drivers, and system integration for Qualcomm’s high‑performance inference accelerators and secure compute solutions.

As a Staff Engineer, you will own complex subsystems end‑to‑end, drive architectural decisions, and provide technical leadership across software, hardware, and platform teams. Your work will span driver development, test infrastructure, performance optimization, security enablement, and product commercialization, with a strong emphasis on robust, production‑ready system software.

Key Responsibilities Host & System Software Development
  • Design, implement, and optimize Linux user‑space and kernel‑adjacent drivers and libraries in modern C++.
  • Lead development of host software stacks supporting high‑performance AI inference and secure compute workloads.
  • Drive API design, multi‑threaded systems, and scalable software architectures.
  • Own feature development, integration, and bring‑up across hardware and software boundaries.
Testing, Quality & CI
  • Architect and develop unit, integration, and system‑level tests for CI environments.
  • Lead functional and performance validation of host software and drivers.
  • Establish best practices for testability, automation, and long‑term maintainability.
Secure Compute & Virtualization (Differentiating Scope)
  • Integrate host software with Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) including Secure VMs (CVM) and Software‑Isolated VMs (SIVM).
  • Enable secure PCIe device assignment, SR‑IOV, and container/VM‑based workloads.
  • Implement and support device attestation, lifecycle management, and secure interface configuration.
  • Collaborate on PCIe firewall, memory protection, and register isolation features.
Performance, Debug & Bring‑Up
  • Debug complex host‑side issues including boot flows, PCIe link behavior, log transfer, and overflow handling.
  • Optimize host software for AI inference performance and low‑latency workloads.
  • Use advanced debugging, tracing, and profiling tools on Linux platforms.
Technical Leadership & Collaboration
  • Provide technical leadership across mixed hardware/software teams.
  • Drive design reviews, influence system architecture, and mentor senior engineers.
  • Work closely with hardware, firmware, hypervisor, security, and cloud teams to deliver end‑to‑end solutions.
  • Support customer deployments and resolve complex system‑level issues.
Required Skills And Experience
  • Extensive experience with Linux system software development in modern C/C++.
  • Strong background in Linux user‑space development, API design, and multi‑threading / synchronization.
  • Solid understanding of Linux internals, kernel concepts, drivers, and system bring‑up.
  • Experience with UML, OO design, and large‑scale software architecture.
  • Strong knowledge of SoC architecture (cores, caches, memory hierarchy, interconnects, I/O).
  • Experience with source code and configuration management (git required).
  • Proven ability to work at low‑level implementation detail while maintaining system‑level perspective.
  • Excellent written and verbal English communication skills.
  • Comfortable operating in a high‑caliber, cross‑disciplinary engineering environment.
Staff‑Level Expectations

title: Staff Frontend Engineer - Commerce
description:
About HighLevel:
HighLevel is an AI-powered business operating system that gives agencies, entrepreneurs and SMBs the infrastructure to build, automate and scale. Today, HighLevel supports SMBs across 150+ countries, fueling community-driven growth rooted in real customer outcomes.
To date, businesses operating on HighLevel have generated over $7 billion in ecosystem value, demonstrating the impact of shared infrastructure at scale. By centralizing conversations, automation and intelligence into one system, we help businesses move faster, reduce complexity and execute efficiently.
Behind the platform, HighLevel powers more than 4 billion API hits and 2.5 billion message events daily. With 250 terabytes of distributed data, 250+ microservices and over 1 million domain names supported, our architecture is built for performance, resilience and long-term scalability.

Our People
With over 2,000 team members across 10+ countries, HighLevel operates as a global, remote-first organization built for speed and ownership. We value initiative, clarity and execution, creating space for ambitious people to build systems that support millions of businesses worldwide. Here, innovation thrives, ideas are celebrated and people come first, no matter where they call home.

Our Impact
Every month, HighLevel enables more than 1.5 billion messages, 200 million leads and 20 million conversations for the more than 1 million businesses we support. Behind those numbers are real people building independence, expanding opportunity and creating measurable impact. We’re proud to be a part of that.
Learn more about us on our YouTube Channel or Blog Posts.

About the Role:

    You are the technical owner of every pixel a Commerce merchant or shopper sees. You also raise the frontend bar for all of HighLevel. The role has two horizons.

    Commerce first. You set the architecture. You write the standards. You review the code. You hire the team. You hold the line on performance, accessibility, and quality while engineers and their coding agents ship into Commerce every day.

    Then HighLevel. Commerce is greenfield. That makes it the place to prove what excellent frontend engineering looks like at HighLevel. What works in Commerce becomes a shared capability, so every organization benefits.

    The central frontend platform team is your closest partner on both horizons. They own the shared foundation. You are their most demanding customer and one of their strongest contributors. You bring Commerce requirements early. You co-design solutions with them. You upstream what Commerce builds, so HighLevel keeps one foundation.

    This is an individual contributor role at staff level. You lead through design documents, code, reviews, and the people you grow. You will write production code every week.

    The bar is high. A storefront that loads in six seconds loses the sale. A checkout a screen reader cannot use excludes a customer and breaks the law in some markets. An architecture that couples every team slows every one of them. A pattern that stays inside one organization helps only that organization. You own all four problems.

Responsibilities:

    First 90 days

    • Publish the Commerce frontend standard: architecture, state, data fetching, testing, accessibility, and performance. Every Commerce team adopts it.
    • Instrument real-user monitoring on every Commerce surface. Publish field metrics for LCP, INP, and CLS per surface, with an owning team for each.
    • Review frontend pull requests across Commerce. Raise the quality of every one you touch, and write down the patterns so reviews scale beyond you.
    • Map the central frontend platform roadmap against Commerce needs. Agree a working contract with that team: what the platform provides, what Commerce builds, and how requests and contributions flow both ways.
    • Set up a standing design review with the central platform team, so Commerce decisions and platform decisions stay aligned.
    • Produce a frontend hiring plan: how many engineers, at what levels, and in what order.

    First 6 months

    • Ship the architecture that lets every Commerce team build and deploy its surfaces independently, with enforced module boundaries. Build it on the central platform's foundation wherever one exists, and close gaps jointly with that team.
    • Put performance and bundle budgets in CI for every Commerce route. A regression fails the build.
    • Make accessibility a gate: automated checks in CI and manual audits on checkout and storefront flows against WCAG 2.2 AA.
    • Land typed, generated API clients end to end, so a backend contract change breaks at compile time.
    • Contribute at least one Commerce-built capability to the central platform, adopted by another organization.
    • Hire and onboard the first Commerce frontend engineers.

    First 12 months

    • Commerce storefronts meet "good" Core Web Vitals at the 75th percentile in field data, on mid-range mobile devices.
    • Checkout and storefront pass a WCAG 2.2 AA audit.
    • Backend engineers ship frontend features that meet the standard without your direct involvement.
    • Coding agents across Commerce follow the frontend standard by default, through shared instructions, skills, and review gates you designed.
    • Commerce is HighLevel's reference implementation for frontend excellence. Its standards, performance budgets, and agent guidance reach other organizations through the central platform.
    • You lead or co-lead HighLevel-wide frontend decisions with the central platform team, written as RFCs other organizations build on.
    • The Commerce frontend team runs on its own. You spend your time on the next hardest problem at HighLevel.

Requirements:

    • You have 9+ years of experience in building frontend systems
    • You have built commerce surfaces at scale: storefronts, checkout, or point of sale.
    • You have built or led a design system consumed by many teams, and shipped breaking changes through it safely.
    • You have used ConnectRPC, gRPC-Web, or protocol buffers from the browser.
    • You can read and write Go well enough to build or review a backend-for-frontend.
    • You contribute to open source, web standards discussions, or the frontend community.
    • You have taught backend engineers to ship good frontend code.
    • You have contributed to a shared frontend platform or design system used by several product organizations.

Our Stack & Direction

    Frontend. Vue.js across HighLevel. TanStack Query for server state. Webpack and Rspack for builds, with micro-frontends where teams need independent deploys.
    Contracts. ConnectRPC with protocol buffers from the browser to the backend. The client calls typed functions and receives typed responses. No hand-written REST clients.
    Backend. Go services on Kubernetes, with Postgres as the primary store. Backend-for-frontend layers run inside the cluster, close to the services they call.
    Rendering. Static generation where content allows it, client-side rendering for interactive surfaces, and a backend-for-frontend to aggregate data. You will challenge and refine this direction with evidence.
    Engineering practice. Every engineer works with coding agents. Standards live as written documents, shared agent instructions, and review gates.

What you bring on day one:

    Scope. You have owned frontend architecture across several teams for a multi-quarter effort. Other teams still build on decisions you made. You can show us the before and after.
    Platform partnership. You have worked with a central platform team as both a consumer and a contributor. You influence roadmaps you do not own. You negotiate scope with evidence. You land changes in shared code that many organizations depend on, without breaking them. You have taken a standard from one team and made it company-wide.
    The browser platform. You know the rendering pipeline, the event loop, and what makes a long task. You follow new platform features through Baseline and MDN, and you have shipped some of them. You reach for the platform before a library, and you have deleted dependencies because the browser made them unnecessary.
    Performance. You diagnose with field data, performance traces, and network waterfalls. You have moved Core Web Vitals in production and kept them there with budgets and ownership. You can explain where every millisecond of a page load goes, from DNS to interaction.
    Architecture for many teams. You have designed systems where many teams deploy independently into one product. You know module federation, native ES modules, import maps, monorepos, and when each one fits. You know what each costs: duplicate dependencies, runtime integration bugs, build infrastructure. You pick deliberately.
    Data and contracts. You design how the client talks to the server: backend-for-frontend layers, typed RPC contracts, caching, and invalidation. You understand why twenty sequential calls over the public internet cost seconds, and how to collapse them.
    Accessibility. You build with semantic HTML first and add ARIA only where semantics fall short. You know WCAG 2.2, colour contrast requirements, and keyboard and screen reader behaviour. You have led an accessibility audit and fixed what it found.
    Security. You treat user-generated content as hostile. You know XSS, content security policy, sandboxed rendering, and supply chain risk in the npm ecosystem.
    Code review. Your reviews make engineers better. You find the race condition before the naming nit. You turn repeated feedback into lint rules, patterns, and documentation.
    AI-assisted engineering. You use coding agents every day with discipline. You write the context, specs, and skills that make agent output match the standard. You verify generated code with tests and review. You have a view on how teams keep a codebase understandable when everyone generates three times more code.
    Writing. You write design documents and decision records that other engineers can act on without a meeting.

Providing this information is voluntary and refusal to do so will not affect your application status. title: Streetcar Operator
description:
Streetcar Operator OKC

Salary $23.57 hourly

Job Summary

A Streetcar Operator is responsible for operating a streetcar on a 4.6-mile route safely and efficiently within city limits, ensuring passengers' comfort, safety, and adherence to operational schedules. The route will include 22 stops linking major employers, businesses, attractions, and residences in the downtown area. The operator must possess operating skills, knowledge of traffic laws, and demonstrate professionalism while interacting with passengers. Operators provide operation of the battery/overhead wire-powered streetcar in mixed use traffic typically in the Downtown area. This position plays a critical role in providing public transportation services and contributing to the community's mobility.

Duties And responsibilities:

*This is a non-exhaustive overview of the job duties for this position.

  • This position is responsible for the operation of the streetcar in a safe and efficient manner within established rules, schedules, regulations, procedures and providing professional and courteous customer service.

  • Reports for duty at the Streetcar Maintenance Facility or any other designated location along the system in the prescribed uniform with a neat and well-groomed appearance.

  • New hires should expect to work late nights, weekends and holidays exclusively as seniority dictates.

  • Maybe required to work on an “on-call” basis.

  • New hires must successfully complete provided training programs for operating rules, track access, standard operating procedures, safety, vehicle operations, minor-troubleshooting and basic customer service.

  • May work with maintenance of manufacturers to provide movement of the Streetcars within the yard and shop area and on the mainline or mainline extension(s) for vehicle testing and operations training.

  • Act as incident commander as needed until relieved.

  • Informs Dispatchers or Route Supervisors of operating status of equipment and any observed defects.

  • Perform pre-departure inspection in accordance with established procedures for streetcar preparation for service and reports to supervisory staff all operational hazards.

  • Observes and immediately report reports to supervisory staff all operational hazards.

  • Observes and reports any defects along the alignment.

  • Receives and transmits messages through handheld or Streetcar onboard messaging system.

  • Prepares trip reports and defect reports upon completion of duty.

  • Regular and predictable attendance and punctuality are a requirement for this position.

  • Other duties as assigned.

Job Requirements

  • High School diploma or Ged.

  • Must have a valid driver’s license and with a good driving record for the past 5 years.

  • Ability to read, write and communicate proficiently in English.

  • Ability to obtain and maintain a Streetcar Operation certification

  • Preference: Previous Rail Transit Operator and/or Public Transit Operator experience.

Pre- Employment Requirements

  • Subject to pre-employment background check and motor vehicle report review.

  • No criminal record within the last 7 years

  • Less than 2 points on your driving record, and no infractions in the past 12 months

  • Must have a valid driver license

  • Subject to pre-employment physical, medical evaluation, and drug screen due to the safety sensitive nature of this position.

  • Successfully complete and maintain any required safety certification and testing on an annual basis.

  • Must be 21 years of age or older

  • Must have a high school diploma or GED

  • Must have a valid DOT medical card

Any major moving violations, previous convictions or pending misdemeanor or felony charges for distribution of illegal substances, violent crimes or lewd acts are reviewed by management for approval.

Physical Requirements:

The physical demands described below must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential job functions of this role. This position will be physically demanding at times. This is a non-exhaustive overview of the physical requirements of this job.

  • Able to walk on uneven surfaces up to one-half mile.
  • Maintain balance for an extended period while train is in motion.
  • Must be able to be aware of surroundings and follow verbal commands while being exposed to moderately loud noises on a daily basis.
  • Must be able to work in a confined access/space environment with a width of 24 inches.
  • Must be able to adapt to various temperature extremes including but not limited to heat, cold, moisture and wind.
  • Regularly sit and stand for an extended period of time.
  • Regularly push/pull up to 25 pounds.
  • Regularly ascend and descend a platform with a height of up to 18 inches from the floor.
  • Able to tolerate repetitive movements: bending and overhead reaching.
  • Must successfully pass color/vision examinations as required by the position.
  • Must be able to hear and distinguish auditory signals as required by the position.
  • Must be able to work in a safety sensitive work environment.

Working Conditions

  • Occasionally working in a confined access/space environment with a width of 24 inches.
  • Inside and outside regularly, and exposed to heat, cold, humidity, and rain.
  • The possibility of falls from working on and around slippery surfaces.
  • Possibility of body injuries such as sprains, fractures, deep cuts, or loss of body members.
  • Possibility of injury to the body caused by burns or electrical shock.
  • Will work near moving machinery and power tools.
  • Exposed to intermittent or continued loud noises caused by machinery and other workers.
  • Occasionally exposed to infections caused by microorganisms.
  • Will work eight to 10 hour shifts and may be required to work holidays and overtime.

Evaluation Criteria

Interpersonal Relations: Employees work closely with customers, community members, security staff and supervisors. Frequently working with radio communications with other staff and supervisors. Occasionally talk with Techs and other staff to determine what problems may be experiencing with equipment or vehicle.

Supervision Given and Received: Receives route details and detailed oral instructions from a Route Supervisor/Dispatch and/or supervisor(s). Work is continually reviewed by supervisor.

Other Duties and Responsibilities
This is a summary of the duties and responsibilities commonly found within this classification. It is not meant to be all-inclusive; thus, other related activities or tasks may be assigned.

title: VIDIGERM61
description:

Vidispine GmbH is a leading solutions integrator with decades of successful delivery across broadcast, media, and sports industries. Our media asset management and broadcast solutions are deployed globally, supporting some of the most demanding content workflows.

We are looking for a Solution Architect to own the end-to-end technical design of VidiNet solutions for our customers across Europe and beyond.

This role combines architecture with hands-on delivery. You will shape solutions with customers before contract, define the target architecture, and then implement the complex parts of it together with the project team through testing and Go-Live.

What You'll Do

  • Own the solution architecture for VidiNet Media Asset Management engagements, from first customer workshop through Go-Live

  • Design end-to-end media workflows (ingest, processing, metadata, storage, distribution) that are scalable, secure, and maintainable

  • Review designs and implementations for alignment with the agreed architecture and VidiNet best practices
  • Deliver customer workshops, knowledge transfer sessions, and training
  • Work closely with product and engineering teams to feed customer requirements into the roadmap and validate fit with platform capabilities
  • Contribute to reference architectures, reusable patterns, and continuous improvement of delivery methodologies

What You Bring

Experience & Background

  • 7+ years of experience in Professional Services, Solutions Engineering, or System Integration, including at least 3 years in a solution or technical architect role
  • Proven track record designing and delivering complex IT or media workflow solutions for enterprise customers
  • Experience supporting pre-sales: scoping, estimation, and contributing to commercial proposals
  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or equivalent practical experience

Technical Skills

  • Deep understanding of broadcast and media workflows and media asset management concepts

  • OpenSearch / observability stacks
  • GitHub and CI/CD pipelines
  • Infrastructure as code and configuration management (Terraform, Ansible, Chef)
  • Familiarity with architecture modelling approaches (e.g. C4, UML)

What Makes You Successful

  • Strong communication skills, with the confidence to lead technical discussions with customer architects, engineers, and senior stakeholders
  • Ability to translate business needs into technical designs, and technical trade-offs into business-relevant terms
  • Sound judgement on scope: you can tell what the platform does out of the box, what needs configuration, and what needs custom work
  • Structured, pragmatic, and comfortable moving between architecture decisions and hands-on implementation
  • Collaborative mentor who raises the technical level of the delivery team
  • Customer-focused mindset with a commitment to high-quality solutions
  • Fluent in English and German (written and spoken)

Additional Information

  • Willingness to travel occasionally (approx. 10%) for customer workshops and key project milestones (Europe and international)
  • Work in a dynamic, international environment with high-impact projects

Why Join Vidispine

  • Shape state-of-the-art media technology solutions for customers worldwide
  • Work in a highly skilled, collaborative team environment
  • Own the technical direction of complex, large-scale media workflows and integrations
  • Grow your career in a delivery-focused, innovation-driven organization

title: Senior Product Manager (Bridging)
description:
About Us 🚀

Bridgit is a leading non-bank lender transforming the way Australians access property equity. Purpose-built to make property transactions faster and easier, we pioneered the Buy Now, Sell Later solution - empowering homeowners to unlock their property equity and move on their terms. With a simple digital application, fast approvals, and flexible loan options, we're making property finance seamless and stress-free.

We're now five years old and making huge strides. We've accredited over three-quarters of Australia's broker network, and launched white label solutions with Australia's largest aggregators - Connective, Aussie Home Loans, Finsure, and Loan Market Group - and we're just getting started.

Our momentum has been recognised with awards including Best Growth Story at the 2025 Fintech Awards, the 2025 Finder People's Choice Award for Lending Innovation, Deloitte's Tech Fast 50 2025, and a place among LinkedIn's Top 20 Startups in Australia 2025.

The Role

We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to own Buy Now, Sell Later, the bridging finance product Bridgit was built on. Reporting to the Product Director - Mortgages, you'll own the product's roadmap and performance end to end. That runs from understanding what brokers and customers need through to shipping improvements that make bridging faster, simpler and more competitive.

What you’ll do:

  • Own the product strategy, roadmap and performance for bridging finance, with clear success metrics across conversion, time to approval, customer outcomes and commercial performance.

  • Build a deep understanding of our brokers and customers, using research, feedback and data to find the problems most worth solving.

  • Use competitor insight across price, policy and product to identify where bridging needs to evolve, and bring clear recommendations to the Product Director - Mortgages.

  • Partner with Credit to understand how policy shapes the bridging experience, including peak debt, end debt, serviceability and valuations. Identify where changes to product and policy can improve approval speed and quality.

  • Get hands-on with solution design, including process flows, wireframes, prototypes and user stories, to turn concepts into developer-ready features.

  • Break large initiatives into smaller releases that each deliver value and build towards the longer-term roadmap.

  • Work closely with Engineering, Design, Platform, Operations, Credit, Distribution and Compliance to deliver on time and to a high standard.

  • Lead testing and rollout, then measure results after launch and feed what you learn back into the roadmap.

  • Build business cases for significant bridging initiatives, with success measures defined before work begins.

What we’re looking for:

  • 6+ years' experience in product management, including ownership of a product or major product area.

  • Experience in lending, ideally residential mortgages or bridging finance, with a working understanding of credit policy and the broker distribution model.

  • A track record of using data and customer insight to make product decisions and measure outcomes.

  • Strong commercial judgement: you understand how price, policy and product combine to win in market.

  • Comfort working closely with engineering teams and getting into technical detail.

  • Clear, confident communication with everyone from brokers to executives.

  • A proactive approach and comfort with ambiguity.

Bonus points for:

  • Experience with bridging, equity release or specialist lending products.

  • Any exposure to tools like Jira, Trello, Notion, or similar.

  • Startup or scaleup experience.

Why Join Us?

Bridgit values its team, they are the heart of how we build this business. Along with competitive remuneration, slick offices and the chance to be part of an innovative, agile fintech, we also offer:

  • Extra Leave – we offer birthday leave + an additional day of paid leave to be used for life events, celebrations or just a mental health reset.

  • Two weeks from anywhere – we encourage employees to work remotely from a location of their choice for two weeks each year.

  • Learning and Development – all employees are encouraged and empowered to engage in professional development including a number of learning initiatives run internally.

  • Social events – we have a jam-packed social scene, with events throughout the year.

Ready to Make an Impact? 🙌

If you’re excited about reshaping the lending industry and want to be part of a company that values authenticity and innovation, we’d love to chat. Apply now and let’s build the future of finance together!

A heads-up that because we operate in the financial services space, any offer made will be subject to successful pre-employment screening, including reference checks and a standard police check.

description:

title: Senior Manager, Visual Merchandising & Store Design Operations (ANZ & APAC)
description:
HOURGLASS COSMETICS —Senior Manager, Visual Merchandising & Store Design Operations (ANZ & APAC) (Hybrid Role)

Connected by creativity and driven by purpose. Hourglass Cosmetics is a vegan and cruelty-free beauty brand, redefining luxury cosmetics with high-performance products, innovative formulas, and award-winning franchises. Recognized by Forbes, Fast Company and Time Magazine as one of the most inventive beauty companies, Hourglass leads the industry with its breakthrough products and its commitment to animal welfare. Founded in 2004, Hourglass is globally available in 32 markets and over 4,600 doors including Sephora, Ulta, Neiman Marcus, Selfridges, Space NK and more. Hourglass became part of the Unilever Prestige division in 2017. Discover more about the Hourglass brand story and mission on our website hourglasscosmetics.com.

The Senior Manager, Visual Merchandising & Store Design (VMSD) Operations, ANZ & APAC will lead the planning and execution of visual merchandising and store design programs across Australia, New Zealand and the wider Asia Pacific region. The role drives the development, execution and ongoing maintenance of seasonal updates, secondary activations, shop-in-shops (SIS), Travel Retail (TR) locations, new door openings and brand expansion across the region, ensuring consistent alignment with global brand standards across all retail channels. This role is the regional point of contact between Global HQ (VMSD Operations, 3D/2D Design and Trade Marketing) and APAC commercial teams, retail partners and vendors. This role partners with regional and global VMSD teams, using shared processes and tools to keep ANZ & APAC aligned with the global business.

WHAT YOU’LL DO:

  • Regional Alignment & HQ Communication:
    • Act as the single point of contact between global HQ, ANZ, and all APAC markets, bringing market requests and priorities together into one regional view.
    • Lead weekly ANZ & APAC status meetings with global VMSD and Design teams, with clear agendas and actionable recaps.
    • Lead meetings with APAC local teams to understand their requirements and communicate with global teams.
    • Manage all ANZ & APAC projects in Asana, using shared global processes so work is visible across regions.
    • Partner with global teams on secondary programs, including Sephora ANZ & APAC placements in department stores and travel retail, and own regional execution and reporting.
    • Share learnings, vendor insights and best practices with regional counterparts to keep ways of working consistent.
    • Adapt globally approved design and merchandising strategies for each market, getting HQ approval before any local changes.
    • Work across ANZ, APAC, and US time zones through scheduled calls and clear written updates.
    • Flag timeline, budget and brand-standard risks early, with recommended solutions.
  • Project Management:
    • Own timelines and deliverables for seasonal updates, secondary activations, new doors, expansions and closures across ANZ and APAC, tracked in ASANA.
    • Lead regional status meetings with global teams, commercial partners, retailers and vendors; issue clear recaps and escalate risks early.
    • Consolidate market inputs (retailer requirements, door lists, launch dates, space constraints) into global project requests and briefing documents to give 3D/2D teams clear, complete briefs.
    • Communicate shipping, delivery and installation timelines and key dates to retailers, vendors, market teams and field teams, and ensure timely delivery of VM guidelines and final production artwork.
  • Seasonal & Secondary Execution:
    • Oversee seasonal updates for regional gondolas, counters and TR/SIS, recommending fixture and space solutions that meet commercial goals and brand standards. Lead secondary fixture programs with key partners, including Sephora, from vendor bidding through installation.
    • Support the end-to-end artwork process with Global 2D Design, from project request to final vendor delivery, including localized artwork and in-market language review for each market.
    • Translate global design standards to local retailer and market requirements, reviewing drawings, samples and final installs for brand quality.
    • Conduct regular store visits to assess execution, shopability and the competitive landscape.
  • Operations & Vendors:
    • Project manage new door openings, refits and closures, working with commercial teams to plan fixture inventory for changes in door counts and distribution. Build and manage regional vendor and installer network, making sure pricing is competitive and work meets Hourglass standards.
    • Maintain the regional fixture library, installation photo records and vendor list, along with SOPs that follow global processes.
    • Serve as the primary point of contact for ANZ & APAC fixture replacement and maintenance support.
    • Help drive process improvement between global and regional teams, including evolving project request and briefing templates.
  • Finance:
    • Manage the regional VMSD opex and capex budget with the Global Executive Director, including forecasts, spend tracking and YTD reporting.
    • Manage vendor quotes, POs and invoices across markets and currencies; value engineer solutions within budget.

YOU’LL LOVE THIS JOB IF:

  • You are DETAIL ORIENTED: You appreciate the importance of having detailed and precise information.
  • You are a strong COMMUNICATOR: You align stakeholders across regions and time zones with a confident presence and drive clear, decisive outcomes.
  • You are extremely ORGANIZED: You are not overwhelmed by the thought of tackling multiple tasks and markets at a time.
  • You are AGILE: You adapt well to changing needs and priorities and are able to pivot easily to achieve goals and deadlines.
  • You are highly STRATEGIC: You are able to develop creative concepts and vision that support brand and business goals.

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • 6+ years of experience in Visual Merchandising, Store Design Operations, Retail Operations or related field, including ANZ and/or APAC markets.
  • Experience in a regional role reporting into a global headquarters, including adapting global guidelines for local markets.
  • Proven experience with seasonal updates, launches and new door openings for a beauty or luxury brand; strong planogram skills.
  • Experience managing multi-market vendors, installers and budgets across currencies.
  • Proficiency in MS Office, Asana or Smartsheet; Adobe Creative Suite a plus.
  • Strong communicator, able to lead meetings across time zones with flexibility for US and UK calls.
  • Highly organized and detail-oriented; able to manage multiple projects in a fast-paced environment.
  • Willingness to travel within ANZ and APAC as required.
  • Role based in Sydney and must be able to work from the Sydney office 60% of the time on mandatory office days.

Reporting to Manager, HR Services, you will lead the strategy and evolution of HR’s digital ecosystem, from intuitive intranet experiences to seamless self‑service content and knowledge resources, ensuring employees can easily find what they need, when they need it. Working closely with HR leaders, technology partners, and enterprise communicators, you’ll establish standards and governance that ensure consistency and quality across every HR touchpoint.

This is a unique opportunity for an innovative, analytical and collaborative professional to help accelerate HR’s shift toward a modern, integrated, self‑service model that empowers employees and enhances their everyday experience.

Why should I join?

If you are a high achieving, experienced, motivated HR trailblazer who thrives in a fast-paced environment and has the credibility to be a trusted HR partner; have the confidence to challenge the status quo and the ability to handle multiple priorities at the same time, then this amazing opportunity is for you!

Metrolinx is committed to helping our leaders achieve their goals through continuous learning, professional development, and support.

This includes organizing content for easy retrieval, tagging, user-friendly structure and machine-readability.

title: Teamleder til Salg Privat

title: Power Systems Engineer - Level 1/2
description:
Idaho National Laboratory is hiring an Electrical Engineer to work on our Electrical Controls and Structural Engineering team. Our team works a 4x10 schedule located out of our Materials and Fuels Complex (MFC) with every Friday off.

This position is located at our Materials and Fuels Complex, which hosts the core of the U.S. nuclear research and development capabilities with a diverse array of facilities designed for remote work on highly irradiated fuels and materials. A new fuel idea can be designed, fabricated, tested, and analyzed at MFC to better understand the effects of irradiation. Many groups, such as universities, industry partners, other national laboratories, international research organizations, and other federal agencies are working at MFC.

You will apply engineering principles to electrical systems and electrical power transmission and distribution. Apply electrical engineering theories and principles to explore research opportunities associated with electrical energy generation, storage, transmission, distribution, management, and use. Collaborate with associated engineering professions to ensure the development of integrated systems to enable safe, resilient, reliable delivery of power to the end user.

Essential Job Functions:

  • Perform detailed analyses on current power transmission and distribution systems to inform development and design decisions
  • Apply electrical engineering theories and principles to pursue solutions resulting in secure, sustainable, resilient, robust, reliable electrical power systems, including all aspects of energy generation, storage, transmission, distribution, management, and use.
  • Apply sound engineering principles in the design, development, and installation of industrial electrical power systems.
  • Collaborate with customers in developing system alternatives and analyze alternatives to ensure program requirements are met, including evaluating risks, costs, and other performance measures.
  • Provide technical reviews of design output (design change packages, installation procedures, and testing procedures, etc.) and obtain appropriate approvals for design output.
  • Ensure design modifications meet technical baseline requirements.
  • Establish and maintain configuration management of assigned system(s) while maintaining existing drawings and databases. Develop functional and operation requirements, system design descriptions, and test procedures for equipment.
  • Coordinate and collaborate with other engineers, planners, operations personnel, and other stakeholders to ensure the proper execution of testing activities.
  • Provide first order data analysis and report test status to appropriate stakeholders.
  • Provide input on the functionality of test equipment and support procurement activities in acquiring equipment, spare parts, or other systems for plant modifications and/or research systems.
  • Evaluate and assess system/equipment performance and history to improve efficiency and reliability.
  • May be responsible for all electrical engineering aspects of project work, including identifying the equipment, services, space, personnel, work controls, etc., required to execute given projects.
  • May oversee the design and maintenance of assigned high-risk electrical systems operations.
  • May direct others or work directly with equipment vendors to diagnose and repair malfunctions and/or design and specify new equipment to meet customer requirements.
  • May direct and execute the application design, set-up, and basic operation of complex high power and high voltage equipment and systems.
  • Other duties as assigned

Required:

  • Level 1: Bachelor’s in power engineering, electrical engineering or other related field from an ABET accredited institution and 0 years experience.
  • Level 2: Bachelor's in power engineering, electrical engineering or other related field from an ABET accredited institution and 2 years of experience. Master's and 0 years of experience. PhD and 0 years of experience.
  • This position requires the ability to obtain and maintain a Department of Energy "L" clearance, which requires US Citizenship.

Ideal Candidate Requirements:

  • Completed hands-on coursework, lab work, or a senior capstone project involving the operation or analysis of industrial electrical equipment such as motors, transformers, switchgear, or distribution systems including work involving load analysis, power quality, or system protection
  • Applied National Electrical Code (NEC) or Electrical Safety in the Workplace (NFPA 70E) requirements or electrical safety concepts such as fault current analysis, overcurrent protection, or arc flash hazard assessment through academic coursework, a lab, or design project
  • Completed coursework or project work involving backup power systems such as generators or uninterruptible power supplies (UPS) as well as the creation or interpretation of electrical drawings, schematics, or single line diagrams related to power distribution or facility electrical systems


Job Information:

  • The pay range for this position is: Level 1 ($66,504 - $136,356)/ Level 2 ($79,344 - $162,732). At Idaho National Laboratory compensation decisions are determined using factors such as education, relevant experience, and other credentials.
  • TDP: This is a testing designated position; you will be required to submit to a pre-employment drug screen and periodic drug testing throughout the term of your employment.
  • Multi-Level: This is a multi-level posting and you will be placed at the appropriate level dependent on depth and breadth of proven experience and skills.

Physical Requirements:

While performing the duties of this classification, the employee is frequently required to stand, walk, sit, stoop, kneel, bend, and work in an office and laboratory environment. The job requires hand/finger dexterity to keyboard or type, handle materials, manipulate tools, and reach with hands and arms. The job may require operation of job-related equipment and driving a vehicle. Sufficient visual acuity and hearing capacity to perform the essential functions and interact with the public is required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

title: Technician (23151)

title: Binance Accelerator Program - QA (Content)
description:
Binance is a leading global blockchain ecosystem behind the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange by trading volume and registered users. We are trusted by 300+ million people in 100+ countries for our industry-leading security, user fund transparency, trading engine speed, deep liquidity, and an unmatched portfolio of digital-asset products.     Able to use Chrome DevTools to inspect network requests and console logs, with a basic understanding of HTTP and JSON

title: Backstage & Automation Trainer, Entertainment Technical
description:
The Backstage & Automation Trainer oversees and delivers comprehensive Entertainment Technical training programs aligned with a specialized backstage and automation curriculum, under limited supervision. They collaborate with management to set training objectives, design tiered course curricula, and develop materials like handouts, tests, and practical exercises. Responsibilities include lecturing on safety, project planning, installation, maintenance, and repair of automation systems, theatrical sets, props, and stage equipment. The trainer administers evaluations, maintains trainee performance records, and refines training programs, incorporating feedback and recommending enhancements such as multimedia aids. Additionally, they manage inventory and maintenance of sets and props, coordinate with production teams for new show setups, and integrate operational improvements into the curriculum. They provide trainings for shipboard staff, offer technical support via ticketing systems, and assist in recruiting Entertainment Technicians in collaboration with the Casting & Booking Department, ensuring alignment with best practices in the field. The Backstage & Automation Trainer conducts Entertainment Technical training programs based on a comprehensive Backstage & Automation curriculum, under limited supervision. They determine training objectives in coordination with management, write and review training programs including tiered course curricula, handouts, and tests, and design practical exercises. They lecture on safety, project planning, installation, preventative maintenance, and repairs of automation systems, theatrical sets, props, flying apparatuses, and stage flooring. Additionally, the trainer administers written and practical examinations and authors performance reports to evaluate and document trainee progress and performance during their time at Carnival Studios.

Essential Functions:

Program, Operations & Innovation

  • Training Development and Delivery: Designs and delivers comprehensive training programs for Stage & Automation Technicians, focusing on TAIT & Mechatronics systems, stage maintenance, and scenic repair. Training includes group and individual instruction, hands-on workshops, and covers safety protocols, production show operations, preventative maintenance, and repairs.

  • Training Program Development: Create, update, and review training programs to align with trainee needs and industry advancements. Continuously evaluate the effectiveness of training programs through feedback from trainees and stakeholders, making necessary adjustments to enhance learning outcomes.

  • Training: Conduct both group and one-on-one training sessions to address specific learning needs and ensure comprehensive skill development. Utilize a variety of teaching methods and materials, including hands-on activities, demonstrations, and theoretical discussions. Lectures on safety, project planning, installation, preventative maintenance, and repairs of Automation Systems, theatrical sets, props, Flying apparatuses, stage flooring

  • Examinations and Performance Evaluation: Administer written and practical exams to assess trainees’ knowledge and technical skills. Evaluate trainee performance, provide constructive feedback, and identify areas for improvement. Track progress over time and recommend further training or development opportunities as needed during their tour in Carnival Studios

  • Administrative: Maintain accurate and up-to-date records for each trainee, tracking progress, exam results, and overall performance. Generate reports and provide detailed feedback to trainees, department leaders, and other stakeholders.

  • Equipment Inventory and Maintenance: Manage the inventory of all audio equipment, ensuring proper storage, tracking, and maintenance. Oversee regular maintenance and repairs of audio equipment to ensure optimal working condition. Coordinate the purchase of new equipment or replacement parts as needed, based on equipment wear and technological advancement

Team Leadership and Development

  • Cultural Essentials: Uphold and promote Carnival’s core behaviors, such as speaking up, respecting and protecting, improving, communicating, listening and learning, and empowering. Encourage team members to share their insights, challenges, and suggestions to enhance collaboration and operational success, while proactively resolving conflicts. Organize and execute monthly “Studio Star” which highlights outstanding team members with in a month for their outstanding work.

  • Team Environment: Actively engage in team meetings, projects, and brainstorming sessions to foster collaboration and idea sharing. Support a positive team environment by recognizing individual contributions and promoting mutual respect and support among team members.

Collaborate

  • Interdepartmental: Work alongside the Operations, Production & Music teams to identify areas for improvement in general production processes. Offer expert advice on the technical aspects of new or existing productions, contributing valuable insights into audio-related issues and solutions. Help integrate new technologies and best practices into productions, ensuring high-quality audio outcomes.

  • Teamwork with Shoreside and Shipboard Teams: Foster strong communication and teamwork between Shoreside and Shipboard teams, ensuring that audio systems, training, and technical support are aligned across locations. Work collaboratively to troubleshoot and resolve issues that may arise during live performances or training activities, ensuring consistency in delivery.

  • Continuous Improvement: Participate in meetings with other departments within Carnival Studios to discuss opportunities for process improvement, production quality, and technical support. Act as a resource for ongoing learning and development for both technical staff and trainees, helping to create a culture of continuous improvement within the organization.

Safety and Compliance

  • Safety Practices: Develop and enforce safety practices and training programs to ensure guest and crew safety while maintaining operational integrity. Prepare teams for onboard safety duties and coordinate regular drills and tests for safe execution of show stops during live performances.

  • Regulatory Compliance: The Backstage & Automation Trainer must ensure that all training and technical practices meet industry standards and regulatory requirements. This includes staying updated with safety regulations related to backstage and automation equipment, as well as ensuring compliance with any maritime or aviation safety protocols (for operations involving vessels). This could include adhering to electrical safety codes, fire prevention protocols, and sound exposure guidelines. Hazard Identification and Mitigation: During technical rehearsals, the trainer must also be vigilant in identifying potential safety hazards related to backstage and automation equipment (e.g., wires in walkways, excessive sound levels, electrical safety) and take immediate action to mitigate these risks. Additionally, ensuring that all equipment is inspected for functionality and safety before use is a key responsibility.

Since inception, Oportun has provided more than $22.7 billion in responsible and affordable credit, saved its members more than $2.5 billion in interest and fees, and helped its members set aside an average of more than $1,800 annually.

Oportun is currently seeking qualified candidates with customer service, cashier, sales, or hospitality experience to work Full-Time. Our Member Loyalty Representatives are passionate about listening, helping, and connecting with people at all touchpoints, such as in our stores and in the communities around our stores through personal outreach activities. title: 1st Shift Security Officer
description:
The Opportunity:

As a Security Officer you play an important role in protecting Mattel’s employees, guest (s), product(s) and brands. The ideal candidate is flexible, collaborative, detail oriented, has strong communication skills, and prioritization skills. This position is located at Mattel’s global headquarters in El Segundo Ca. This is an on-site position and includes weekend and holiday work. Schedules may vary based on business needs.

What Your Impact Will Be:

  • Support Mattel’s GlobalSecurity Strategy to protect people, assets, and Mattel’s reputation by providing exceptional customer service and consistently applying policies and practices.
  • Enforce Mattel Global Security policies and practices to create a safe and secure environment for all employees and visitors.
  • Completes security duties and related tasks as defined in the Contingency Operations and SOP manuals under the direction of the Security Leader/Shift Supervisor and Security Manager.
  • Completes security patrols on foot patrols, in a vehicle and digitally to monitor the Mattel campuses for physical security, safety and facilities-related concerns. Effectively monitors the access control system, CCTV system, and the “guard tour” management system.
  • Monitors the fire control panel for alarms and any problems with equipment. Reports any service/maintenance issues to Facilities personnel.
  • Perform administrative data entry duties as assigned by the Shift Supervisors, for incident documentation and communications via the Microsoft suite.
  • Ensure adherence to access control standards including the employee badge policy, visitor registration, temporary or contract worker check ins and intern badging along with other visitor types.
  • Ensures parking lot safety by conducting traffic control, enforcing parking rules, accident investigations and response to emergency call box activations.
  • Support IP (Intellectual Property) process surrounding confidentiality and controlled destruction of IP per Mattel standards.
  • Additional responsibilities as assigned by supervisor or manager.
  • Flexibility to work on multiple shifts and or shift times to support business needs.
  • This is an onsite position and does not allow for remote work.

What We’re Looking For:

  • One+ years of Security, Asset Protection, Loss Prevention, Law Enforcement, or military background preferred.
  • High school diploma or GED, required.

  • Must be able to work varying shifts including nights, holidays, and weekends.
  • Ability to read, analyze and interpret general business policies, professional journals, technical procedures, or governmental regulations.
  • Ability to write reports, and business correspondence, including detailed incident reports writing.
  • Display exceptional customer service and communication skills.
  • Ability to stand and walk, go up/downstairs and stand for extended periods of time.
  • Ability to lift and/or move up to 50 pounds.
  • Outdoor post assignments (where applicable) may require an individual to withstand extreme heat, humidity, cold, and/or severe weather (e.g. snow, sleet, rain, hail, wind).
  • Ability to use post-security equipment (handheld and walk-thru metal detectors, handheld radios, access control systems, CCTV).

We are a purpose driven company aiming to empower the next generation to explore the wonder of childhood and reach their full potential. We live up to our purpose employing the following behaviors:

  • We innovate: At Mattel we always aim to find new and better ways to create innovative products and experiences. No matter where you work in the organization, you can always make a difference and have real impact. We welcome new ideas and value new initiatives that challenge conventional thinking.
  • We execute: We are a performance driven company. We strive for excellence and are focused on pursuing best in class outcomes. We believe in accountability and ownership and know that our people are at their best when they are empowered to create and deliver results.

Who We Are:

Mattel is a leading global toy company and owner of one of the strongest catalogs of children’s and family entertainment franchises in the world. We create innovative products and experiences that inspire, entertain and develop children through play. We engage consumers through our portfolio of iconic brands, including Barbie, Hot Wheels, Fisher-Price, American Girl, Thomas & Friends, UNO and MEGA, as well as other popular intellectual properties that we own or license in partnership with global entertainment companies. Our offerings include film and television content, gaming, music and live events. We operate in 35 locations and our products are available in more than 150 countries in collaboration with the world’s leading retail and ecommerce companies. Since its founding in 1945, Mattel is proud to be a trusted partner in empowering children to explore the wonder of childhood and reach their full potential.

title: Senior Application Security Architect

title: QA/DevOps Intern
description:
Are you creative, innovative and enthusiastic about new technologies? Do you enjoy programming and problem solving? We are looking for interns who are passionate about a career in quality assurance (QA) and DevOps to join our team in Sophia Antipolis.

Arm’s Sophia Antipolis design centre is in one of the most appealing parts of France, the French Riviera, at the heart of Europe’s largest and most dynamic technology park. Surrounded by mountains and the Mediterranean Sea, this outstanding design centre has delivered leading products from Arm’s Cortex(TM) CPU family. These CPUs power some of the world’s best-selling smartphones, tablets and gaming systems, using technology that has taken user experience and performance to another level.

Job Overview:

This internship position is in the Engineering Support and Quality Assurance, an international and diverse team. Work in the Central Engineering – Productivity Engineering and be involved in the quality assurance of workflows for any hardware IP products made by Arm. Those workflows embrace the realms of Front End, DFT, Back End and Machine-Readable Specification.

We are offering a variety of internships that will be discussed during the interviews, depending on your profile and development wishes. All selected subjects are highly challenging projects, requiring deep interest in advanced technologies, DevOps, strong analytical skills, and a high degree of autonomy and creativity.

The internship topics are updated regularly, and can vary from:

  • Migrate existing QA flows of MRS, Front-End, DFT teams to Cloudbees
  • Implement QA flow from scratch for Back-End team
  • Audit on Security, software vulnerabilities for each team

Interested by the challenge? Join our team! We look forward to receiving your application!

What you could be doing as a QA/DevOps Intern:

  • The aim of our internships is to develop your potential and expand the opportunities on offer, providing an incredible variety of potential career paths. We will support with continuous learning and development, whilst encouraging you to achieve professional chartered status.
  • We want to make sure that every intern learns about different aspects of our work and grows their knowledge, so you will work in a team on real projects from day one, with guidance from expert engineers, and also have dedicated time for personal development.

We are looking for individuals who:

  • Are students in their last year of Masters (BAC+5 or equivalent) and available for a 5-month to 6-month internship
  • Have knowledge of DevOps/Jenkins/Groovy
  • Have experience of UNIX and Python and shell programming
  • Are fluent in written and oral English

Qualities that will help your application stand out:

Depending on the selected internship subject, other desirable skills might include:

  • git
  • Docker

Additional Information

We encourage early applications as we review them on a first come/first served basis.

Arm Internships require you to be enrolled in a higher education degree.

The internship duration is 6 months, starting in 2027.

French Law requires students to complete an internship agreement (Convention de Stage). This is a tripartite agreement signed by the student, their home university and host organization, that facilitates an internship in France. It is the contract defining all the essential points of the internship: duration, missions, remuneration and benefits, insurance in the event of an accident, etc.

It is preferable that Arm's own template of the agreement is used. Successful applicants will be required to provide contact details of the appropriate university representatives in order to have the agreement signed.

Please note we are unable to provide visa sponsorship for this role. Applicants must have the right to work in the country where the internship is based, without relying on sponsorship by Arm, for the full duration of the internship.

In Return:

Working on interesting new projects with leaders in the field is exciting, but we also know how important it is to receive support. That's why throughout your internship, you can expect regular feedback and development opportunities, social activities to connect with your peers, an end of internship celebration, plus the opportunity to be *considered for future Graduate positions (*subject to performance). #getreadytogrow

The Principal, Retirement Product is accountable for leading the development, management and continuous improvement of the Fund's retirement products. The role will drive innovation and continuous improvement across new product development, product performance, governance and risk management.


This senior position comes at a very exciting point in time. With more members approaching retirement and living longer than ever before, you can be part of the retirement team in largest super fund in the country, helping to directly improve the retirement outcomes for members. This is a rare and important opportunity to drive change and make a very tangible difference the lives of millions of Australians.

  • Build and lead a high-performing team, providing direction, coaching and development to foster innovation, accountability and succession capability.
  • Maintain strong product governance and reporting, representing retirement at internal Executive and Board committees and providing subject matter expertise input as required.
  • Drive stakeholder alignment across the Fund and promote effective prioritisation and decision making to support retirement and broader Member Domain growth objectives.


What You’ll Need

  • Extensive senior leadership experience within financial services, with a strong track record leading product portfolios in superannuation, retirement or other highly regulated environments.
  • Deep product management expertise, including strategy, pricing, new product development, product enhancement and end-to-end product lifecycle management.
  • Strong strategic, commercial and change leadership capability, with the proven ability to set direction, influence outcomes and lead complex cross-functional initiatives.
  • Comprehensive understanding of the retirement market, including member needs, competitive dynamics and relevant regulatory, governance and risk requirements.
  • Exceptional stakeholder and people leadership skills, with a proven ability to influence senior leaders, navigate ambiguity, build high-performing teams and deliver results in a changing environment.

Life at AustralianSuper

AustralianSuper is committed to colleague development, and we support our people with ongoing learning, coaching and training, as well as career opportunities across our expanding global organisation. We offer generous leave entitlements and promote a blended working environment in which all roles can flex, and we’re happy to discuss what this looks like for you.

We cultivate a workplace that champions safety, respect, inclusiveness and diversity. We are committed to supporting our diverse workforce in a way that is inclusive and embraces diversity in all its forms. What’s Next

Apply now, if you share our values of Energy, Integrity, Generosity of Spirit and Excellent Outcomes and would like the opportunity to work in a challenging, growing and rapidly evolving team to deliver outstanding results.

title: CSW Intern
description:
About Hope Christian Health Center: Hope Christian Health Center (HCHC) is a nonprofit, faith-based organization dedicated to serving the Las Vegas community through compassionate, high-quality healthcare. Our services include primary care, behavioral health, community health worker programs, street outreach services, and recuperative care. We are committed to addressing the physical, emotional, and social needs of the individuals and families we serve. Our mission is to glorify God by demonstrating Christ's love to the Las Vegas community through the delivery of excellent, affordable healthcare to all, regardless of their ability to pay.


JOB SUMMARY: The Clinical Social Worker (CSW) Intern plays a vital role in delivering compassionate, client-centered care within a fast-paced Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) behavioral health clinic. Under the supervision of a Nevada Board-approved LCSW supervisor, the intern provides therapeutic support to individuals experiencing mental health, emotional, and behavioral challenges. Responsibilities include conducting assessments, developing treatment plans, facilitating individual and group therapy sessions, and collaborating with multidisciplinary teams to ensure integrated care.


This position is part of an NBESW-approved internship program under NAC 641B.150. The intern will be supervised by a Nevada Board-approved LCSW with a minimum of three years of post-licensure clinical experience and current practice in psychotherapeutic methods. Weekly individual supervision (at least one hour) is required, with documentation of all supervision and accrued hours. The intern must display their Nevada CSW Intern Certificate at their primary practice location, as required by NAC 641B. All clients served are considered clients of the agency, and clinical records are agency-owned. Services must be provided exclusively within approved agency settings in Nevada. Independent or out-of-state practice is not permitted under this internship.


DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Perform biopsychosocial evaluations to identify client needs, strengths, diagnoses, and treatment goals.
  • Deliver psychotherapeutic interventions using evidence-based modalities tailored to culturally diverse populations.
  • Respond to urgent mental health situations with de-escalation, safety planning, and referral strategies.
  • Support clients in developing coping mechanisms, emotional regulation, and problem-solving strategies.
  • Deliver psychoeducation on mental health topics, treatment options, and wellness strategies.
  • Collaborate with primary care providers, case managers, and external agencies to ensure integrated care and continuity of services.
  • Develop and revise individualized care plans in partnership with clients, focusing on measurable outcomes.
  • Collaborate with collateral contacts as needed to support client progress and provide resources.


Administrative Duties

  • Maintain accurate and timely records of assessments, treatment plans, progress notes, and discharge summaries
  • Assist with appointment scheduling, reminder calls, and follow-up coordination to support client engagement.
  • Participate in tracking service outcomes, client satisfaction, and program metrics for quality improvement initiatives.
  • Attend staff meetings, case conferences, and supervision sessions to contribute to clinical discussions and receive guidance.
  • Complete mandatory trainings, maintain HIPAA compliance, and follow all internal and external regulations, policies, and procedures.


Other Duties:

  • Promotes and demonstrates Hope values of: Gospel motivation, Prayer, Excellence, Stewardship, Patience, Thankfulness, Humility, Service, Dignity through Relationship and Hospitality and Joy
  • Always maintains a courteous and professional demeanor.
  • Always maintains the confidentiality of Hope Christian Health Center finances and patient-related information.
  • Complies with HIPAA and protects patient information.
  • The CSW Intern ensures compliance with all 19 Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) Health Center Program Requirements.
  • The CSW Intern is also expected to actively participate in and support quality improvement activities and the clinical practice team efforts emphasizing the importance of the individual patient and putting the patient’s needs first.
  • Other duties as assigned.

title: Print Production Lead
description:
Some of what you will do:

The Print Production Controller coordinates print work through Staples Canada’s national production network. The role validates production readiness, applies approved routing standards, monitors job progress, resolves routine issues, and escalates service or completion risks. Working across retail, eCommerce, B2B, print fulfilment partners, production facilities, and approved vendor-supported work, the Controller provides clear ownership, visibility, and workflow discipline from intake through completion.

Specifically, You Will:

  • Review production-ready work to confirm files, specifications, timelines, quantities, finishing, delivery details, and supporting information are complete before release.

  • Work with Sales, Print Support, Print Estimating, production facilities, print fulfilment partners, approved vendors, and operational partners to resolve missing, unclear, or conflicting production information.

  • Interpret approved estimates, costing, sourcing, and production requirements to move work into the appropriate workflow.

  • Apply approved routing standards and workload visibility to coordinate the appropriate production path, including production facility or approved vendor production.

  • Proactively monitor job activity, intake quality, handoff points, routing constraints, and emerging red flags to identify risks before they affect service or committed completion dates. Take early action where possible and escalate as required to the Manager, hub managers, or other operational leaders.

  • Respond to escalations from intake, sales, customer-facing, and operational channels by assessing the issue, taking prompt action to resolve where possible, engaging the appropriate partners, and ensuring the resolution is documented and communicated in a timely manner.

  • Maintain accurate documentation of routing decisions, job status, exceptions, ownership changes, escalations, and resolution steps using approved workflow and ticketing processes.

  • Reinforce standard intake, routing, documentation, escalation, and communication practices across the Print Control Center.

  • Identify recurring issues, process gaps, handoff challenges, routing constraints, and improvement opportunities; share findings with Production Control leadership; and escalate issues as needed to support timely, documented, and communicated resolution.

Some of what you need:

  • College or technical diploma in graphic communications, print production, business, operations, or a related discipline preferred.

  • Strong understanding of production readiness, intake quality, print specifications, file readiness, finishing options, routing, job movement, documentation requirements, and common production risks.

  • Ability to interpret approved estimates, job specifications, sourcing decisions, costing information, and production requirements within defined decision rights and escalation criteria.

  • Ability to collaborate with Print Estimating and operational partners to support complete handoffs, accurate routing, workflow control, and production execution.

  • Strong proactive monitoring, prioritization, issue resolution, workload visibility, and early risk identification skills.

  • Sound judgment to resolve routine production issues and recognize when decisions, exceptions, or risks require escalation to Production Control leadership.

  • Strong attention to detail, organization, documentation discipline, follow-through, and comfort with production systems, workflow tools, ticketing logic, CRM, order management, quoting tools, and Microsoft Office.

  • 2–4 years of experience in print production, production coordination, print support, sales support, estimating, customer service operations, or a related operational role.

  • Experience with print specifications, production workflows, job routing, intake, escalations, approved vendor coordination, or production facility environments preferred.

  • Experience supporting B2B print, print fulfilment partners, retail print, eCommerce print, commercial print, centralized production, or multi-site production networks is an asset.

  • Experience with workflow, ServiceNow, CRM, order management, or production tracking tools is an asset.

Physical demands/working conditions:

  • Remote environment.

  • Requires a high-speed, stable internet connection.

  • Occasional travel to corporate offices, production facilities, approved vendor sites, or Staples locations may be required.

Some of what you will get:

  • Associate discount

  • Health and Dental benefits

  • RRSP/DPSP

  • Performance bonuses

  • Learning & Development programs

  • And more...
