  • Develop and maintain backend functionality and server-side integrations.
  • Manage database changes, investigate data-related issues, and maintain reliable migration, backup, and recovery processes.
  • Build and improve CI/CD workflows using GitHub Actions.
  • Configure, maintain, and troubleshoot GitHub runners, including self-hosted runners.
  • Improve build reliability, automated testing, deployment processes, and development environments.
  • Manage server-side application deployments, configuration, monitoring, and troubleshooting.
  • Establish effective AI-assisted and agentic coding workflows across the team.
  • Review AI-generated code and ensure that changes are tested, understandable, secure, and maintainable.
  • Help developers and junior team members use AI tools effectively through practical demonstrations and knowledge sharing.
  • Where appropriate, act as technical team lead: coordinate dependencies, guide implementation, review technical decisions, and help the team resolve blockers.

Required Qualifications

  • Demonstrated senior-level experience in mobile software development.
  • Strong Kotlin and Android development experience, together with practical Swift and iOS development experience.
  • Solid hands-on experience with Kotlin Multiplatform and integrating shared code into both mobile platforms.
  • The ability to investigate problems across mobile clients, APIs, backend services, databases, and infrastructure.
  • Practical backend development experience and a sound understanding of API design, authentication, and application security.
  • Strong SQL and relational database experience, including schema changes, migrations, and performance troubleshooting.
  • Hands-on DevOps experience with Linux servers, application deployment, configuration, and operational troubleshooting.
  • Excellent Git and GitHub knowledge, including pull requests, code reviews, branch workflows, and repository configuration.
  • Strong experience with GitHub Actions and configuring and maintaining GitHub runners.
  • Substantial experience using AI coding assistants and coding agents to deliver working software.
  • The ability to establish development workflows that combine coding agents, automated checks, and human review.
  • Clear communication, practical documentation skills, and a willingness to share knowledge.
  • The ability to work independently while supporting other developers constructively.
  • Interest in a long-term, full-time position and availability to start promptly after an agreement is reached.

Especially Valuable Experience

  • Previous experience as a technical lead or senior engineer supporting a mobile development team.
  • GPS, BLE, UWB, NFC, or other location and proximity technologies.
  • Testing mobile applications on real devices and investigating platform-specific behavior.
  • Container-based application deployment and reproducible development environments.
  • Monitoring, incident diagnosis, and maintaining reliable backend services.
  • Coordinating changes that affect mobile applications, backend APIs, and database structures together.

Potential Technical Team Lead Responsibilities

For a suitable candidate, the role can include technical leadership of our Android and iOS developers.

This would involve helping the team make consistent technical decisions, breaking down implementation work, coordinating shared dependencies, and maintaining the quality of delivered changes. You should be comfortable mentoring developers and taking responsibility for the technical direction while remaining actively involved in engineering.

What We Offer

  • A fully remote, full-time role with a long-term perspective.
  • Compensation based on your experience, expertise, and responsibilities.
  • A central role supporting our mobile development team.
  • The opportunity to shape our architecture, infrastructure, and agentic development workflows.
  • Potential technical teamlead responsibility, depending on suitability.
  • Close collaboration with a team that values practical knowledge sharing.

Remote Working Arrangement

Our remote working setup includes a time-tracking tool that records mouse-click and keyboard-activity metrics and captures screenshots of the screen. This monitoring is part of the working arrangement and will be explained during the recruitment process.

Applicants should be comfortable working with this setup.

How to Apply

Please submit your CV and a short overview of relevant projects.

Include:

  • Your experience developing for both Android and iOS, including Kotlin Multiplatform.
  • Your backend, database, and server infrastructure responsibilities.
  • Examples of GitHub Actions workflows and runner environments you have configured or maintained.
  • The AI coding tools and agentic workflows you use, with examples of delivered results.
  • Your experience supporting developers, mentoring colleagues, or leading a technical team.
  • Your earliest start date and salary expectations.

Public portfolio links, GitHub repositories, and released application references are welcome where available.

title: Law Clerk for the Honorable Lisa Janzen, Fourth Judicial District
description:

title: Senior Director of Operations
description:
Company Overview
About Virtium is a Rancho Santa Margarita, California–based designer and manufacturer of high-reliability industrial embedded solutions for customers whose systems must operate consistently in demanding, long-life environments. For more than 25 years, Virtium has supported global OEMs with industrial-grade SSDs, DRAM memory modules, compute and system-on-module solutions, AI accelerator modules, connectivity modules, and supporting software. Our solutions are used in applications across networking and telecommunications, industrial automation, aerospace and defense, medical, transportation, rugged computing, Industrial IoT, and other mission-critical embedded markets where reliability, lifecycle stability, qualification, and supply continuity matter.

About the Role
Virtium is seeking a strategic, hands-on Senior Director of Operations with deep Surface Mount Technology (SMT) and electronics manufacturing experience to directly lead Manufacturing Operations, Supply Chain, and Quality. This leader will own end-to-end customer fulfillment, from demand planning, sales forecasts, and customer orders through supplier readiness, materials, production planning, SMT/electronics manufacturing, quality, shipment, and delivery. Reporting to the Vice President of Operations, this leader will oversee teams and operating processes across the U.S. and Vietnam, serve as the primary operational owner of customer delivery commitments, and communicate regularly with customers, suppliers, executives, and occasionally the Board of Directors. The Senior Director of Operations will strengthen operational discipline, improve visibility and execution, and build the people, processes, equipment, quality systems, supplier performance, and scalable operating rhythms needed to support growth in a fast-paced electronics manufacturing environment.

What You’ll Do
• Own customer delivery and execution. Translate sales forecasts and customer orders into material commitments, capacity plans, production schedules, and shipments; proactively identify shortages, constraints, and delivery risks and drive recovery plans and escalations.
• Directly lead Manufacturing Operations, Supply Chain, and Quality. Own SMT/electronics manufacturing, materials planning, purchasing, supplier management, inventory, production, quality systems, customer service, order entry, and customer program management across U.S. and Vietnam operations, ensuring these functions operate as one integrated organization.
• Coordinate multi-site performance. Align facilities and manufacturing partners to optimize delivery, quality, capacity, cost, and customer responsiveness, with clear accountabilities and operating processes across locations.
• Establish a disciplined operating rhythm. Run weekly production meetings covering orders, materials, schedules, capacity, quality, and shipments, and lead executive operations reviews focused on KPIs, risks, actions, and customer commitments.
• Communicate and resolve issues. Lead customer, supplier, and cross-functional meetings; provide clear updates on operational performance, capacity, risks, and plans to executives and occasionally the Board.
• Lead supply chain performance. Directly manage the supply chain function, including procurement, supplier performance, material availability, inventory accuracy, working capital, E&O exposure, escalation management, and cross-functional alignment between demand, supply, production, and customer commitments.
• Lead quality performance and corrective action. Directly manage the quality function, ensuring effective quality systems, traceability, corrective and preventive actions, customer quality responsiveness, internal yield improvement, and consistent adherence to customer and regulatory requirements.
• Plan for growth. Develop operating budgets, staffing plans, capacity plans, and resource requirements, and prepare for volume increases through scalable people, processes, equipment, and systems.
• Drive measurable improvement. Improve productivity, cost, schedule attainment, inventory turns, quality, yield, and delivery through Lean practices, data-driven problem solving, and operational discipline.
• Develop leaders and teams. Coach functional leaders, set clear performance expectations, and build a culture of accountability, collaboration, and execution.

How You’ll Make an Impact
• Establish reliable ownership of customer commitments and improve on-time delivery and production schedule attainment.
• Increase forecast-to-delivery visibility across demand, materials, inventory, capacity, production, quality, and shipments.
• Strengthen U.S.–Vietnam coordination and create a consistent weekly operating cadence for addressing risks and actions.
• Improve supplier delivery, material availability, inventory turns, working capital, yield, returns, productivity, and cost performance.
• Build capable leaders and scalable operating processes that support successful volume ramp-ups and profitable growth.

What You Bring
• Bachelor’s degree in engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Business, or a related field; MBA or advanced technical or management degree preferred.
• 10+ years of progressive manufacturing, operations, or supply chain leadership experience, including leading managers and cross-functional teams.
• Required: Demonstrated direct leadership of Manufacturing Operations, Supply Chain, and Quality in a fast-paced electronics environment, with accountability for customer delivery, supplier performance, material availability, production execution, quality systems, corrective action, yield, and shipment performance.
• Strong knowledge of planning, purchasing, materials, inventory, manufacturing, quality, operating budgets, capacity planning, and resource planning.
• Required: Proven experience directly leading supply chain/materials and quality functions, not only partnering with or influencing those teams as peer organizations.
• Experience leading multi-site operations; U.S. and Asian manufacturing experience, particularly Vietnam, is preferred.
• Required: Deep, hands-on Surface Mount Technology (SMT) expertise and recent manufacturing operations leadership in electronics, semiconductor, industrial computing, memory, storage, or a closely related high-technology environment. Experience primarily in metal fabrication, machining, injection molding, medical-device manufacturing, or defense manufacturing without direct SMT/electronics operations experience does not meet this requirement.
• Working knowledge of ERP/MRP systems, Lean manufacturing, volume ramp-ups, and operational scaling.
• Track record of improving delivery, inventory, quality, productivity, cost, and working capital through measurable operating initiatives.
• Excellent customer-facing and executive communication, analytical judgment, and hands-on problem solving.
• Accountable, low-ego leadership style with urgency, sound judgment, follow-through, and the ability to develop strong managers and scalable systems.

Position Details
• Reports to: VP of Operations
• Location & Schedule: Full-time, onsite in Rancho Santa Margarita, CA, Monday–Friday
• Compensation: Total compensation package includes bonus eligibility in the range of $165,000 to $180,000
• Benefits: Medical, dental, vision, 401(k) match, paid time off, holidays, and additional employee perks.
• Additional Information: Candidates should live within a reasonable commuting distance. Relocation assistance and employment sponsorship are not available currently.

title: Radiology Tech
description:
Position Summary

The Radiologic Technologist is responsible for performing diagnostic imaging procedures to support accurate and timely patient diagnosis and treatment. This role ensures high-quality radiographic images while prioritizing patient safety, comfort, and dignity. The technologist collaborates with providers and care teams to deliver efficient, patient-centered services in both routine and emergency situations. This position also supports departmental operations, equipment maintenance, and scheduling functions to ensure continuity of care in rural healthcare. **Offering $10,000.00 sign on bonus**

Title: Radiology Technologist Job Code: 2944

Status: Full Time Night Shift Department: Radiology

Location: Share Medical Center Supervisor: Radiology Director

Required Skills

  • Demonstrate strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy in all imaging
  • Commitment to excellent customer service and support patient-centered care
  • Communicate effectively with patients, providers, and staff in a professional manner
  • Manage time effectively and prioritize tasks in a fast-paced environment
  • Proficiency in electronic health records (EHR) and radiology systems
  • Strong knowledge of radiation safety, patient positioning, imaging techniques and radiology equipment operation

Qualifications

  • Associate degree in Radiologic Technology from an accredited program
  • Current registration with the American Registry of Radiologic Technologists (ARRT)
  • Current BLS Certification (Must obtain within 90 days of hire)

Key Responsibilities

  • Perform radiographic procedures adhering to physician orders and department standards
  • Prepare and position patients accurately to obtain high-quality radiographic images
  • Practice radiation safety techniques to minimize exposure to patients, staff, and self
  • Maintain accurate and timely documentation in the electronic health record
  • Verifies orders, confirms patient identity and explains procedures to ensure patient understanding and comfort.
  • Operate and maintain radiologic equipment, ensuring proper function and reporting malfunctions
  • Manage inventory of radiology supplies, coordinating with central supply as needed
  • Maintain a clean, safe, and organized work area in compliance with infection control standards
  • Participate in weekend and evening on-call rotation, must be able to respond within 20 minutes for emergency imaging needs, staying onsite if needed.
  • Respond to emergency situations, including codes, and assist as needed
  • Collaborate with providers, nurses, and other departments to ensure quality of patient care
  • Assist with scheduling and coordination of imaging services for X-Ray, CT, MRI, Ultrasound and Mammogram based on patient needs and urgency
  • Confirm appointments and provide necessary pre-appointment instructions
  • Participate in continuing education and maintain required certifications and competencies
  • Monitor patient condition during procedures and respond appropriately to adverse reactions or emergencies
  • Ensure compliance with hospital accreditation standards, including utilization of SQSS (Strategic Quality Support System) for compliance tracking.
  • Adhere to all hospital policy and procedure, follow HIPAA guidelines, available for duty in the event of a disaster, completes all required educational training and performs other job duties as assigned.

Physical Requirements

  • Frequent standing and walking throughout clinical areas for extended periods.
  • Ability to assist with lifting, repositioning, transferring, or supporting patients.
  • Ability to lift, push, or pull up to 50 pounds occasionally and 25 pounds frequently.
  • Frequent bending, stooping, reaching, and kneeling while performing clinical tasks.
  • Manual dexterity and fine motor skills to operate medical equipment, and document care.
  • Ability to communicate clearly with patients, families, and healthcare team members.
  • Ability to visually read medical charts and operate clinical technology.
  • Ability to respond quickly in emergency situations.

Reasonable accommodations may be provided in accordance with ADA requirements

Potential Hazards

  • Exposure to hospital-related hazards including blood-borne pathogens, bodily fluids, infectious diseases, x-ray/electromagnetic energy, electric shock, and chemicals. Employees must adhere to all hospital safety protocols, including use of personal protective equipment (PPE) when necessary.

title: Director, AI/ML Engineering
description:
Optum Tech is a global leader in health care innovation. Our teams develop cutting-edge solutions that help people live healthier lives and help make the health system work better for everyone. From advanced data analytics and AI to cybersecurity, we use innovative approaches to solve some of health care's most complex challenges. Your contributions here have the potential to change lives. Ready to build the next breakthrough? Join us in making healthcare work better for everyone through people-led, responsible AI while Caring. Connecting. Growing together.

You'll enjoy the flexibility to work remotely * from anywhere within the U.S. as you take on some tough challenges. For all hires in the Minneapolis or Washington, D.C. area, you will be required to work in the office a minimum of four days per week.

Primary Responsibilities:

  • Lead the vision, architecture, and execution of the Prior Authorization AI/ML roadmap
  • Define and drive AI-native operating models across the authorization
  • Partner with business, clinical, operations, product, and technology leaders to identify high-value AI opportunities
  • Develop strategic investment plans, technical roadmaps, and delivery priorities aligned to business objective
  • Serve as the organization's senior technical authority for AI, Machine Learning, Generative AI, Agentic AI, and intelligent automation
  • Design and build scalable AI platforms and reusable services
  • Lead technical design reviews and ensure engineering excellence
  • Be actively involved in the design, development, and production deployment of AI solutions
  • Lead rapid experimentation, proof of concepts, pilots, and production releases
  • Own end-to-end delivery accountability from ideation through production support
  • Define standards for model governance, explainability, auditability, and transparency
  • Establish monitoring frameworks to evaluate accuracy, drift, bias, safety, and compliance
  • Ensure alignment with healthcare regulatory requirements and organizational AI governance policies
  • Create repeatable frameworks for safe deployment and operationalization of AI solutions
  • Mentor technical leaders and foster an AI-first engineering culture
  • Establish best practices around experimentation, model development, deployment, and continuous learning

You'll be rewarded and recognized for your performance in an environment that will challenge you and give you clear direction on what it takes to succeed in your role as well as provide development for other roles you may be interested in.

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, Data Science, or related discipline
  • 12+ years of software engineering experience
  • 7+ years leading AI/ML engineering teams
  • 5+ years delivering enterprise-scale AI solutions in production
  • Experience designing, building, and deploying solutions using Large Language Models (LLMs), Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), and agentic AI frameworks in production environments
  • Demonstrated expertise in AI platform architecture and engineering on cloud platforms such as Microsoft Azure and/or Amazon Web Services (AWS)
  • Proven ability to translate complex business challenges into technical solutions

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Healthcare, PBM, Utilization Management, Prior Authorization, or Clinical Operations experience
  • Experience building decision-support platforms in regulated environments
  • Knowledge of healthcare interoperability standards

*All employees working remotely will be required to adhere to UnitedHealth Group's Telecommuter Policy

Pay is based on several factors including but not limited to local labor markets, education, work experience, certifications, etc. In addition to your salary, we offer benefits such as, a comprehensive benefits package, incentive and recognition programs, equity stock purchase and 401k contribution (all benefits are subject to eligibility requirements). No matter where or when you begin a career with us, you'll find a far-reaching choice of benefits and incentives. The salary for this role will range from $176,700 - $302,900 annually based on full-time employment. We comply with all minimum wage laws as applicable.

Application Deadline: This will be posted for a minimum of 2 business days or until a sufficient candidate pool has been collected. Job posting may come down early due to volume of applicants.

At UnitedHealth Group, our mission is to help people live healthier lives and help make the health system work better for everyone. Together, we are shaping the future of healthcare by harnessing technology and innovation to make care simpler to navigate, more affordable and more connected for the people we serve. We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone feels welcomed, valued, heard and respected, empowering people to bring their authentic selves to work and strengthening our collective impact through diverse talents, backgrounds, experiences and perspectives.

UnitedHealth Group and its affiliated brands are an Equal Employment Opportunity employer under applicable law and qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, national origin, religion, age, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, or protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by local, state, or federal laws, rules, or regulations.

UnitedHealth Group and its affiliated brands are a drug-free workplace. Candidates are required to pass a drug test before beginning employment.

title: PACE Activities Coordinator
description:
Primary Accountability

The PACE Activities Coordinator is responsible for the coordination and planning of the therapeutic and recreational activities for participants in the FHCN PACE center. The PACE Activities Coordinator will also plan and develop individual and group recreation activities, including measurable goals for improvement.

Description of Primary Responsibilities

  1. Coordination of day center social programming and activity, including communicating current events and FHCN PACE organizational issues to participants in a culturally and linguistically appropriate manner.
  2. Work closely with the Center Manager to oversee activity in the day activity room, including unsafe conditions for participants or staff.
  3. Conduct initial and periodic assessments, at a minimum of every 6 months, for all participants. Assessments must be completed prior to scheduled team meetings.
  4. Establishes realistic and measurable goals and sets up individualized recreation therapeutic programs as part of the plan of care to include recreational and social activities.
  5. Communicate participant changes to team members.
  6. Provide participant and family education in coordination of 24-hour care delivery.
  7. Record, sign, and date “Progress Reports” in the participant’s medical record.
  8. Develop, implement, and supervise the Activity Program- to include both group and individual activities; ability to supervise recreation aides and volunteers.
  9. Ensure that the therapy being provided conforms to accepted industry practice standards and organizational/department standards.
  10. Demonstrate a thorough understanding of age-related characteristics, symptoms, and needs of participants served; explain activities and programming in an appropriate way; work with other therapists and primary care staff to enhance the day center experience of participants.
  11. Serve as a resource to staff and coordinate volunteer activities at the Center.
  12. Build relationships and coordinate with various community resources; coordinate performances by community organizations, including Holiday celebrations.
  13. Coordinate recreational and therapeutic outings into the community where possible.
  14. Build within the Center a sense of community and a warm, social atmosphere in which participants are able to identify a support system.
  15. Participate in QI activities as appropriate; lead participant discussions on FHCN PACE programming improvement.
  16. Participate as a member of the Interdisciplinary Team: attend staff meetings and take part in participant care planning.
  17. Responsible for adhering to the Attendance and Absenteeism Policy, recognizing that regular attendance is considered an essential function of all FHCN positions. Absenteeism is not being at work or failing to attend a paid workshop, training, or event unless the absence is protected by law.
  18. Ability to present to and work at any FHCN location, both at the beginning of a shift or during a shift, based on business need.
  19. Other projects and duties as assigned.

Description of Primary Attributes

Professional & Technical Knowledge:

Effective June 1, 2026, all individuals hired into the role must:

  1. Possesses proficiency in written and verbal communication, basic mathematics, computer applications, and technical systems frequently acquired through one of the following:
    1. Completion of a Bachelor’s Degree program in Recreational Therapy with an emphasis on recreation with special populations or senior populations or a related field and a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.5; or
    2. A combination of relevant experience and completion of a high school diploma with a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.5, or General Educational Development (GED) with a minimum overall score of 162.5, and healthcare-related knowledge frequently acquired through completion of a trade school, para-professional, or certificate type program.
    3. If an individual has completed a degree at a higher level than required by the role and had a stronger GPA in that program, they may provide proof of GPA from that degree in lieu of the high school diploma or Bachelor’s degree.
  2. Have a minimum of two years of experience working in a social or recreational program providing and coordinating services for frail or elderly populations.
  3. Good understanding of psychosocial problems of aging.
  4. Social activities, including arts/crafts and performance programming, tailored to the senior population.
  5. Basic computer skills and use of electronic mail.
  6. Able to work within an interdisciplinary team setting.
  7. Work effectively in a team environment.
  8. Be empathic and patient in attending to the needs of the frail elderly population.
  9. Communicate clearly and effectively to participants daily.
  10. Communicate effectively and openly with other Interdisciplinary Team members on participant status and needs.
  11. Only act within the scope of his/her authority to practice.
  12. Meet a standardized set of competencies for the specific position description established by FHCN PACE and approved by regulatory agencies before working independently.
  13. Be medically cleared for communicable diseases and have all immunizations up to date before engaging in direct participant contact.
  14. Pass a criminal background which will verify that the candidate is: not excluded from participation in Medicare and Medicaid programs; has not been convicted of criminal offenses related to their involvement in Medicaid, Medicare, other health insurance or health care programs, or social services programs under title XX of the Act; and have not been convicted of physical, sexual, drug or alcohol abuse.

Communications Skills:

  1. Job duties require the employee to effectively communicate, verbally and in writing, their opinions and extrapolations of information they collect and synthesize/analyze.
  2. Responsible for the resolution of conflicts that may arise because of disagreements between employees, between employees and customers/clients, or with the public, other legal entities or governmental authorities.
  3. Compiles, analyzes, and prepares information in an effective written form, including correspondence, reports, articles, or other documentation.
  4. Effectively conveys technical information to non-technical audiences.

Physical Demands and Work Environment:

The physical demands and work environment characteristics described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential functions.

Physical demands: Employee must be able to sit and stand for extended periods of time. The employee will also be an active member of the interdisciplinary team at the FHCN PACE center, engaged with employees, participants, and with staff. The employee is required to use hands and fingers, especially for typing on the computer and using the mouse. Employees must be able to talk and listen, particularly for daily interactions with staff and elderly participants. Must be medically cleared for communicable diseases and have all immunizations up to date before engaging in direct participant contact.

Work Environment: Employees must be able to project their voice clearly to participants in a large activity area. Employees must be able to work effectively within an interdisciplinary team model, interfacing and collaborating with a wide range of clinical and social services disciplines who work together to manage the FHCN PACE members’ care. The work setting is in an Adult Day Health Center and primary care clinic environment with moderate noise levels and controlled office temperatures.

Pay Scale:

Min Salary Rate: $25.25

Max Salary Rate: $30.30

title: Rotating Equipment Inspector
description:
Rotating Equipment Inspector – California, United States

Intertek, a leading provider of quality and safety solutions to many of the world’s top-recognized brands and companies, is actively seeking a Rotating Equipment Inspector to join our Technical Inspection Services team in the California, United States. This is a fantastic opportunity to grow a versatile career in Inspection Services!

What are we looking for?

The Rotating Equipment Inspector is responsible for performing visual inspection of materials and/or fabricated equipment at vendor shops or on-site fabrication or testing facilities. The ideal candidate must be well versed in quality control inspections and tests, including nondestructive testing techniques, mechanical testing, dimensional inspection, pressure testing and coating inspections. This position will travel at least 75% of the time.

About the Technical Inspection Services Team

Intertek Technical Inspection Services (TIS) is a partner to clients in diverse industries such as oil & gas, renewable energy, engineering, chemical, and transportation. Intertek supports our clients striving to meet the growing global infrastructure requirements and demands for secure and sustainable sources of energy through services such as inspection, expediting, technical auditing, and site construction support.

Job Title: Rotating Equipment Inspector

Location: California, United States

Salary & Benefits Information:

The hourly pay range for this position is $40.00 - $50.00. Individual compensation packages are based on a variety of factors unique to each candidate including skill set, experience, qualifications, and other job-related reasons.

Shift/Schedule:

All inspectors are utilized on an Adhoc basis and are not provided daily duties. All needs are based on our clients’ needs and we source inspectors based on availability, location, taxonomy approvals, and specific client requests.

What you’ll do:

  • Shaft Balance, Rotor Stack Balance, Rotor ERO/MRO, Residual Unbalance, and Rotor Final Balance
  • Perform inspections or audits and reviewing testing for conformance to Client specifications, industry standards, and approved procedures and reporting of results
  • Review material test reports to conformance with applicable codes and standards
  • Perform the follow-up of dispositions and corrective actions related to non-conformances
  • Document inspection activities in electronic formats
  • Evaluate and agree upon project quality procedures, standards, and specifications ensuring that all parties (engineering, procurement, manufacturing) are adhering to them
  • Review Inspection & Testing Plans to ensure a standardized minimum level of surveillance in accordance with the contractual requirements. Identify the critical inspections and tests to be witnessed by the Owner
  • Carry out inspection visits as per ITP’s either personally or through 3rd party resource

Type of Equipment:

  • Revamp of Existing Gas Compressor Package

This position outline is a general guideline and does not represent all encompassing details. The position assumes that the incumbent has both the mental and physical requirements to carry out the above defined duties.

Minimum Requirements & Qualifications:

  • Aramco Certified QM27 is preferred
  • High School Diploma or GED, Trade School, On-The-Job Training or University Diploma
  • 5+ years of third-party vendor inspection, expediting or auditing experience
  • Experience in quality control inspections and tests, including nondestructive testing techniques, mechanical testing, dimensional inspection, pressure testing and coating inspections
  • Technical training in subjects, such as, but not limited to quality, NDT, blueprint reading, industry standards, auditing, expediting, materials, welding, coatings, electrical components, instrumentation, pressure testing, well control, equipment operation and assembly
  • Must have experience with Mechanical/Pressure Vessels and lifting equipment
  • Must have basic knowledge of material properties
  • Possess clear understanding of basic procurement and fabrication processes with knowledge of relevant codes and specifications for the oil and gas industry
  • Ability to travel frequently throughout the continental US
  • Valid driver’s license and reliable driving record is required
  • Proficient in MS Office programs and Outlook

Preferred Requirements & Qualifications:

  • Valid Industry Certification preferred – Examples of such certifications include, but not limited to: AWS CWI, API 510, 570, SI, (Source Inspector), Electrical Journeyman License, NACE CIP 1, 2, 3, EMA (Expediting Management Association) Basic, Advanced, ASNT NDT Level II, III, and ASQ or IRCA Certified Auditor

Intertek: Total Quality. Assured.

Intertek is a world leader in the Quality Assurance market, with a proven, high-quality business model and a global network of customer-focused operations and highly engaged subject matter experts. With passion, pace, and precision we work to exceed our customers’ expectations, while engaging with our employees to be 10X in their performance and professional growth.

Intertek is a drug-free workplace. As a condition of employment, certain positions may be required to pass a pre-employment drug test based on the type of work that will be performed.

We Value Diversity

Intertek’s network of phenomenal people are our greatest assets, and the diversity they bring fuels our success. Intertek is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer that values inclusion and diversity. We take affirmative action to ensure all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, or other legally protected characteristics.

title: HSQE Advisor | Moranbah | 8:6
description:
HSQE Advisor – Moranbah | 8:6 Roster

Bring safety to life where it matters most.

We’re looking for an experienced and practical HSQE Advisor to join our team in Moranbah, QLD, supporting our remote accommodation operations across the Bowen Basin.

This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys being out in the operation, working alongside leaders and teams to strengthen safety practices, manage risk and build a positive, people-focused safety culture.

You’ll provide practical HSQE guidance across our villages, supporting operational teams to meet the requirements of Civeo’s Integrated Management System (IMS), maintain compliance, improve safety performance and ensure our systems, reporting and data remain accurate and effective.

Operating on 8 days on, 6 days off roster, the role will involve regular travel across our Queensland village operations.

Key Responsibilities

  • Operational HSQE Support: Partner with Village Managers, Supervisors and operational teams to support safe day-to-day operations.
  • HSQE Systems: Implement, maintain and continuously improve HSQE systems and processes across our remote accommodation villages.
  • Risk Management: Identify operational hazards and support effective risk assessments, controls and ongoing monitoring.
  • Incident Investigations: Facilitate incident and accident investigations, maintain accurate records and identify opportunities to prevent recurrence.
  • Inspections & Audits: Conduct workplace inspections and audits to support compliance with Civeo requirements, legislation and client standards.
  • Safety Procedures: Develop, implement and review safety procedures, work instructions and supporting processes.
  • Training & Coaching: Support inductions and HSQE training while coaching teams to strengthen safety awareness and capability.
  • Contractor Management: Assist operational teams with the effective management of contractors undertaking high-risk work.
  • Continuous Improvement: Support HSQE initiatives, safety campaigns and injury-prevention activities focused on key operational risks.
  • Reporting & Data: Maintain accurate HSQE information, reporting, records and safety performance data.

Qualifications & Experience

To be successful in this role, you will bring:

  • Certificate IV or equivalent in Workplace Health & Safety
  • Practical experience in incident investigation and risk management
  • Strong attention to detail across HSQE data, reporting and record keeping
  • The ability to build credible and positive working relationships with operational teams
  • A practical, collaborative approach to safety
  • High standards of confidentiality, honesty and integrity
  • Current Driver’s Licence

It would also be advantageous to have:

  • Internal Auditor qualification
  • Certificate IV in Training & Assessment
  • ICAM Lead Investigator qualification
  • Experience within workforce accommodation, resources, mining support or a similar operational environment
  • Understanding of ISO 9001 Quality, ISO 45001 OHS and ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems

About Us

Civeo Australia, a division of Civeo Corporation, provides workforce accommodation services globally. In Australia, Civeo has a national footprint of approximately 10,000 rooms across twelve villages in Queensland, New South Wales, and Western Australia. In addition, Civeo also operates approximately 16,500 rooms in client-owned properties in remote regions of Western Australia, South Australia and Queensland. With more than 40 years of experience, Civeo supports individuals who live and work away from home.

We're committed to fostering sustainable partnerships and inclusive opportunities in all the communities we operate in. By actively engaging with Traditional Owners and First Nations Businesses, we're not just operating accommodation villages, we're nurturing relationships that honour the rich cultural heritage of the land.

We're safe, welcoming, and proud to encourage Aboriginal & Torres Strait Islander people to join us.

title: Therapist (35129)
description:
Why You Will Love Working with Us!

Magnolia Creek treats women with eating disorders who also struggle with co-occurring disorders. Our evidence-based methods take a whole-person approach to achieve recovery. Magnolia Creek is peacefully situated on thirty-six wooded acres. The property has a private lake, walking trails, outdoor therapy areas, a firepit, and recovery garden. Our residents live in a comfortable, home-like environment where they feel safe and supported. Columbiana is commutable from Shelby, Calera, Chelsea, Montevallo, Alabaster, Pelham, and commute is against traffic from Birmingham area.

What We Offer

  • Collaborative environment dedicated to clinical excellence
  • Multiple Career Development Pathways
  • Company Supported Continuing Education & Certification
  • Multiple Health Plan Design Options Available
  • Flexible Dental & Vision Plan Options
  • 100% Company Paid EAP Emotional Well-Being Support
  • 100% Company Paid Critical Illness (with health enrollment plan)
  • 100% Company Paid Life & ADD
  • 401K with Company Match
  • Company-Sponsored HSA, FSA, & DSA Tax Savings Accounts
  • Generous Team Member Referral Program
  • Parental Leave

How You will Contribute

Responsible for providing individual and group psychological services and guidance for assigned clients and families of Magnolia Creek Treatment Center for Eating Disorders (MCTCED).

Relationships and Contacts

Within the organization: Maintains frequent and close working relationships with clients, families, Management, Clinical Director, facility leadership, peers and vendors.

Outside the organization: May initiate and maintain working relationships with clinical providers, referral partners, families and vendors as needed and directed

Essential Responsibilities

  • Responsible for the clinical management of his/her assigned clients and family.
  • Provide mediation-therapeutic intervention for clients and families, either in groups or individually.
  • Assists in identification of treatment/contract goals for clients and families.
  • Responsible for maintaining contact with the assigned clients referring/outpatient therapist, their Magnolia Creek therapist and the clients family.
  • Maintains client records and creates treatment plans for the family regarding the clients recovery.
  • Assists clients and families with setting goals and oversees the clients complete therapy program regarding the family.
  • Assists with completing a weekly privilege list and a bi-weekly treatment plan for clients/families.
  • Provides ongoing clinical documentation in the EMR for continued Utilization Review.
  • Meets with client or client and family at least once a week to help explore identified issues and behaviors in relationship to current symptoms and recovery.
  • Plans and attends family workshops to assist in the recovery of the client and their family.
  • Attends group meetings, meals and other activities in the milieu to better establish a relationship with clients.
  • Facilitates group sessions with clients and families regarding treatment goals, and recovery (up to 3 groups per week).
  • Provides comprehensive understanding of current behaviors and relational dynamics while using a variety of therapeutic modalities.
  • Attends the weekly team meetings and share observations, comments and important information about clients with the treatment team.
  • Responsible for proper charting and ensuring that all documentation is completed in an accurate and timely manner.
  • Assists in meal/snack supervision as assigned and attends special occasion activities for the clients.
  • Assists with discharge planning, including a written discharge summary and obtaining referral sources and necessary support systems for clients and families once the client is discharged.
  • May serve as a preceptor to graduate students while they are completing an internship at Magnolia Creek, depending on credentials and/or licensure.

title: Nuclear Reactor Operations Trainer
description:
Idaho National Laboratory is hiring a Nuclear Reactor Operations Trainer to work on our Materials and Fuels Complex (MFC) Reactor Training team. Our team works a 4x10 schedule located out of our MFC with every Friday off.

This position is located at our Materials and Fuels Complex, which hosts the core of the U.S. nuclear research and development capabilities with a diverse array of facilities designed for remote work on highly irradiated fuels and materials. A new fuel idea can be designed, fabricated, tested, and analyzed at MFC to better understand the effects of irradiation. Many groups, such as universities, industry partners, other national laboratories, international research organizations, and other federal agencies are working at MFC.

You will conduct training for certified nuclear reactor operators. Utilize operational and technical knowledge and experience, develop, and implement training to meet DOE Order requirements utilizing the Systematic Approach to Training (SAT) principles. You will conduct classroom training, on the job training, simulator activities, and performance standards (written exams, walk-throughs, oral boards, etc.) and facilitate drills.

Essential Job Functions and Responsibilities: (Knowledge, skills, and behaviors required for this position.)

  • Develop and implement technical facility-specific training and qualification programs.

  • Develop learning objectives, lesson plans, training support materials, evaluation standards, and written/oral examinations to ensure staff are qualified to perform their duties in accordance with regulations and procedures. Design training to obtain high levels of proficiency and retention.

title: Senior Workday Analyst, HRIS
description:
Senior Workday Analyst, HRIS

100% Remote within California, Must reside in California

We are seeking a Senior Workday Analyst, HRIS to join FoundationCCC in its mission of benefiting, supporting, and enhancing the California Community Colleges—the largest and most diverse system of higher education in the nation. Together, we are building stronger communities by getting students and colleges the resources they need to succeed and expanding pathways to economic and social mobility across California. Join us as we continue this important work to uphold the value of community colleges in building a brighter future.


What You’ll Do

This position within Business Systems is responsible for the domain design, configuration, and continuous optimization of Workday as the Foundation's enterprise HRIS platform, spanning HCM, Recruitment, Onboarding, Time Tracking, job classifications, benefits administration, data integrations (I/O), reporting, and payroll.

This position works in close partnership with the Foundation's HRIS team, which provides frontline user education and mid-level functional support. This position serves as the escalation point for complex issues involving major loss of functionality, and as a cross-functional mentor and subject matter expert to the HRIS team, building its capability over time through knowledge transfer. Within the HRIS domain, this position is accountable for platform-level responsibilities: security administration, worktags, data management, vendor tenant access, escalated testing, and vendor and tenant engagement. It partners with Business Systems counterparts on cross-domain items such as worktags. The Foundation's Workday Platform Architect holds full, platform-wide system oversight across HCM and Finance; this position escalates cross-domain or platform-wide architecture decisions to that role rather than carrying them directly.

Under general direction, this position serves as a subject matter expert and internal consultant, exercising independent judgment and discretion to evaluate platform capabilities, determine appropriate technical approaches, and advise HRIS and Business Systems leadership on system design, risk, and roadmap decisions. This position does not supervise staff, but it carries significant cross-functional influence and depends on strong consensus-building skills to align HRIS, IT, and Business Systems stakeholders around shared solutions. Because Workday HRIS touches sensitive employee, compensation, and payroll data across the entire organization, this person must be skilled at building alignment across teams with competing priorities and earning trust without formal authority over the teams whose processes the platform supports.


  • Workday HRIS Platform and Domain Design
    • Deep, hands-on expertise in Workday HCM (or a comparable top-tier enterprise HRIS/HCM platform), including recruitment, onboarding, job classifications and position management, benefits administration, reporting, and payroll.
  • Escalation, Testing, and Team Enablement
    • Leads feature updates and functionality testing, provides troubleshooting and escalation support to the Payroll and Finance teams
    • Serves as a cross-functional mentor and subject matter expert to HRIS support staff, advising on Workday best practices and troubleshooting techniques, supporting resolution of escalated issues, and leading knowledge transfer that builds and maintains internal subject matter expertise, reducing the volume of escalations over time.
  • Security, Data, and Vendor Management
    • Builds and maintains complex integrations (e.g., Workday Studio, EIBs, core connectors) within the HCM domain, built to the integration and security standards set by the Workday Platform Architect, supporting HR, benefits, and payroll data flows.
  • Digital Transformation and Stakeholder Engagement
    • Ability to translate complex technical concepts for HRIS and Payroll support staff and non-technical stakeholders.
    • A consensus-building advisor able to work across HR, IT, and Business Systems, aligning stakeholders with competing priorities and earning trust without direct authority.

Attributes for Success

  • Bachelor's degree in business, information systems, human resources, or a related field, OR an equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • 7+ years of experience administering, configuring, or designing Workday HCM (or a comparable top-tier enterprise HRIS/HCM platform), including demonstrated experience operating at an advanced configuration level.
  • Experience with a net-new Workday HCM implementation, or a significant re-engineering of an existing Workday HCM tenant, is strongly preferred.
  • Demonstrated experience across multiple HR functional areas (HCM, recruitment, onboarding, benefits administration, payroll, reporting).
  • SHRM-CP, SHRM-SCP, PHR, or another HR certification is preferred but not required.
  • Project Management certification (e.g., PMP, CAPM) is a plus but not required.
  • Experience in an education or nonprofit environment is a plus.
  • FoundationCCC blends the impact of a non-profit, the culture of an entrepreneurial start-up, and the scale of a state agency
  • We’re recruiting for mission-driven, passionate, equity-minded individuals with a strong desire to impact and change people’s lives for the better

  • Innovation, creativity, collaboration, and entrepreneurship are encouraged as employees work to achieve organizational goals

title: Senior Scientist, Bioinformatics / Computational Biology
location: Cambridge, Massachusetts, United States of America
description:
Are you ready to harness multi-omics, comparative genomics, and agentic AI to accelerate vaccines and immune therapies from discovery to the clinic? In this role, you will transform complex human and pathogen datasets into clear, decision-driving insights that shape antigen design, patient stratification, and translational strategy across high-priority programs.

Based in Cambridge, MA you will work in a collaborative, multidisciplinary environment alongside immunologists, molecular biologists, and data scientists. If you thrive at the intersection of computation and experiment—designing reproducible pipelines on HPC and cloud platforms while partnering closely with the lab to iterate rapidly—this role offers the opportunity to influence study design, guide go/no-go decisions, and help advance novel immune-based therapies toward patients.

Accountabilities

  • You will design, implement, and deliver robust analyses across genomics, bulk and single-cell transcriptomics, and multi-omics to answer program-critical questions with statistical rigor. You will assemble genomes, call variants, and perform comparative genomics and phylogenetic analyses on bacterial and viral pathogens to inform antigen selection and surveillance strategy.
  • You will apply machine learning and statistical modeling to discover biomarkers, stratify patients, predict antigen immunogenicity, and forecast treatment response, translating model outputs into actionable program recommendations. You will also build, optimize, and maintain reproducible workflows using HPC schedulers and AWS to scale analyses, reduce turnaround time, and ensure traceability.

In addition, you will design and integrate LLM-powered agentic workflows for literature mining, data extraction, and pipeline orchestration to accelerate discovery and improve developer productivity. Working closely with experimental scientists, you will propose computationally informed experiments, interpret results, and refine study designs to improve confidence and reduce cycle time.

You will generate translational insights through differential expression, pathway enrichment, and functional annotation, connecting molecular signals to biological mechanisms and clinical hypotheses. You will produce publication-quality visualizations and reports, present findings clearly to cross-functional stakeholders, and champion version control, workflow managers, and reproducible research practices to strengthen code quality and method sharing across programs.

Finally, you will stay current with emerging tools in bioinformatics, AI/ML, and agentic AI, piloting new approaches, sharing learnings, and scaling successful methods across the portfolio.

Essential Skills and Experience

  • You should have a PhD in Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, Genomics, Molecular Biology, Computer Science, or a closely related quantitative discipline, with 2–5 years of industry experience.
  • Alternatively, you may have an MS in a relevant discipline with 4–6 years of industry experience in bioinformatics, computational biology, or genomics.
  • A demonstrated track record of independent research through publications, conference presentations, or successful project delivery is expected.
  • You should bring proficiency in R and/or Python for genomic data analysis, statistical computing, and data visualization, including tools such as ggplot2, Bioconductor, tidyverse, pandas, and scikit-learn.
  • Hands-on experience with NGS data analysis is required, including alignment tools such as STAR, BWA, and Bowtie2; quantification tools such as Salmon, featureCounts, and HTSeq; and variant calling tools such as GATK and bcftools.
  • You should be familiar with RNA-seq analysis workflows, including differential expression methods such as DESeq2, edgeR, and limma, as well as pathway analysis and gene set enrichment approaches such as ssGSEA and MSigDB. Experience working in Linux/Unix environments and with HPC job schedulers such as SLURM, SGE, or PBS, and/or cloud computing platforms such as AWS or GCP, is important.

You should also have working knowledge of Git/GitHub and reproducible research practices, including Nextflow or similar workflow managers. A solid understanding of molecular biology fundamentals, genome annotation, and public bioinformatics databases such as NCBI, Ensembl, UniProt, and PDB is required, along with foundational knowledge of machine learning concepts and applied statistics relevant to biomarker discovery and genomic data.

Success in this role will also require strong analytical thinking, creative problem-solving, and the ability to translate complex datasets into actionable biological insights. You should have excellent written and verbal communication skills, a collaborative mindset, intellectual curiosity, and the ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver results within timelines.

Desirable Skills and Experience

Experience in at least one therapeutic area—infectious diseases, oncology, or inflammatory disease—would be valuable.

We also welcome experience with comparative genomics and microbial or viral genome analysis, including pangenome methods, AMR gene detection, and phylogenetics.

Additional desirable experience includes building predictive and prognostic models using supervised and unsupervised machine learning methods on clinical or preclinical omics data; familiarity with deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch and TensorFlow; and exposure to biological foundation models such as ESM, EvolutionaryScale, scGPT, TranscriptFormer, and Evo.

We also value experience with or strong interest in agentic AI workflows for bioinformatics, including LLM-orchestrated pipelines, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for scientific literature, and tool-using AI agents that interact with databases and analysis tools. Proficiency with AI-assisted coding tools such as Claude Code or GitHub Copilot is a plus.

Exposure to single-cell RNA-seq tools such as Seurat, Scanpy, and CellRanger; knowledge of structural biology tools, protein modeling, or antigen/antibody design; and experience with containerization and infrastructure-as-code would also be beneficial. Familiarity with LLM APIs and prompt engineering for scientific applications, including structured output generation and multi-agent system design, is also desirable.

Why AstraZeneca

At AstraZeneca, ambitious science meets everyday collaboration. Here, bioinformaticians, immunologists, clinicians, and engineers come together to share knowledge openly, challenge ideas constructively, and learn from setbacks as they work toward better solutions. You will contribute across diverse therapy areas, with visibility into decisions that matter and support from leaders who encourage experimentation and innovation.

We pair rigorous scientific standards with creativity and value kindness alongside ambition. Most importantly, we connect each individual’s contribution to a clear purpose: translating insights into medicines that can change patients’ lives.

If you are ready to turn data, models, and modern AI into faster, smarter decisions for patients, we encourage you to apply and show us how you can make an impact from day one.

INSIDER THREAT PROGRAM ANALYST

SpaceX is seeking a dynamic and driven individual with a demonstrated ability to work independently and as a member of a team in a fast-paced, high-tech environment. Our goal is to protect some of the world’s most advanced technologies including rockets, Dragon capsules for human transport, inter-planetary transport vehicles, the world's largest satellite communications network, etc. As an industry leader, we are a target of adversaries, both foreign and domestic, focused on slowing us down and accessing our proprietary technology. The work we do will literally safeguard mankind becoming an interplanetary species.

You will be responsible for the research, analysis, production, and dissemination of information relevant to protecting the safety and security of personnel, brand, global assets, intellectual property, and operations at SpaceX. This role will triage anomalous event data and analyze insider threat program datasets to respond to threats posed to SpaceX. You will use comprehensive understanding of various collection methods and platforms to explore new data sources, build effective queries, and combine information from disparate sources.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Conduct comprehensive investigations and analysis in support of SpaceX intellectual property and security
  • Uphold investigation and analytic tradecraft standards including confidentiality, objectivity, lawfulness, timeliness, and use of all available sources of information
  • Collect and analyze available program data to evaluate insider threat risk to SpaceX infrastructure, programs, and operations
  • Triage anomalous event data associated with indicators of data exfiltration, data destruction and other key indicators of concern
  • Conduct internal investigations working with Information Security, HR, Legal, Government Security, Physical Security, and external partners based on information derived from internal and external sources
  • Utilize network monitoring, data analytic, and other tools (DLP/SIEM/UEBA) to identify anomalous activity, initiate investigations and decipher underlying trends
  • Extract and organize insider threat program data to build metrics, reports and case studies addressing mission requirements and timelines
  • Communicate findings in a timely and accurate manner to team members, management, and relevant stakeholders
  • Support employee training and briefings for internal and external audiences
  • Liaise with external industry and government partners to benchmark insider threat program, share threat intelligence, and further investigations
  • Continuously identify and help implement program improvement methods
  • Manage and safeguard sensitive information, including case files, employee PII, and intelligence reports

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor's degree and 2+ years of professional experience in internal investigations, information security, or counterintelligence; OR 4+ years professional experience in information security, internal investigations, or counterintelligence in lieu of a degree

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • 1+ year using a SIEM and/or conducting digital forensic investigations in a government or corporate environment
  • Working level understanding of insider threat program missions, internal stakeholders, and manifestations of insider threats
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Purview for eDiscovery
  • Experience performing business process automation or constructing data pipelines
  • Familiarity with risk-based alerting, detection, and tuning concepts for insider risk
  • Experience conducting preliminary assessments, determining scope, investigation planning, evidence collection/handling, interviewing and reporting findings to internal and external stakeholders
  • Ability to conduct interviews on short notice according to established internal guidelines.
  • Excellent written and oral communication skills, with the ability to produce clear and concise reports
  • Highly organized with a strong attention to detail
  • Ability to adapt to changing priorities and deadlines
  • Can swiftly adapt to new technical environments and workflows
  • Ability to exercise discretion when conducting confidential investigations

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Must be able to work extended hours and weekends as needed to support critical efforts and operations
  • Must be willing to travel ad hoc
  • Active TS/SCI clearance, or ability to obtain one. With an active clearance, candidates will be subject to pre-employment screening including background check and drug/alcohol test as well as random drug and alcohol testing during employment

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

Pay Range:
Level 1: $85,000 - $110,000
Level 2: $100,000 - $135,000

Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.

Base salary is just one part of your total rewards package at SpaceX. You may also be eligible for long-term incentives, in the form of company stock or long-term cash awards, as well as potential discretionary bonuses and the ability to purchase additional stock at a discount through an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. You will also receive access to comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage, access to a 401(k) retirement plan, short and long-term disability insurance, life insurance, paid parental leave, and various other discounts and perks. You may also accrue 3 weeks of paid vacation and will be eligible for 10 or more paid holidays per year. Employees accrue paid sick leave pursuant to Company policy which satisfies or exceeds the accrual, carryover, and use requirements of the law.

Those with an active clearance will receive a 10% differential, up to an additional $20,000 annually, once officially briefed into a classified program.

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

  • To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

title: Nuclear Reactor Operations Trainer
description:
Idaho National Laboratory is hiring a Nuclear Reactor Operations Trainer to work on our Materials and Fuels Complex (MFC) Reactor Training team. Our team works a 4x10 schedule located out of our MFC with every Friday off.

This position is located at our Materials and Fuels Complex, which hosts the core of the U.S. nuclear research and development capabilities with a diverse array of facilities designed for remote work on highly irradiated fuels and materials. A new fuel idea can be designed, fabricated, tested, and analyzed at MFC to better understand the effects of irradiation. Many groups, such as universities, industry partners, other national laboratories, international research organizations, and other federal agencies are working at MFC.

You will conduct training for certified nuclear reactor operators. Utilize operational and technical knowledge and experience, develop, and implement training to meet DOE Order requirements utilizing the Systematic Approach to Training (SAT) principles. You will conduct classroom training, on the job training, simulator activities, and performance standards (written exams, walk-throughs, oral boards, etc.) and facilitate drills.

Essential Job Functions and Responsibilities:

  • Utilize highly specialized operational and technical knowledge and experience to implement DOE Order and company compliant Systematic Approach to Training (SAT)-based facility-specific training and qualification programs for the Category B Reactor Facilities at the Materials & Fuels Complex (MFC). Areas covered include nuclear theory, reactivity controls, facility operating characteristics and principles, operating limits (safety limits, limiting control settings, and limiting conditions for operation) and their bases, and integrated plant knowledge. Implement nuclear facility training programs by classroom instruction and on-the-job training using lesson plans, OJT checklists, training checklists, and other training materials, procedures, and processes.

  • Instruct Operations and Operations Support personnel in the theory and operation of existing and future nuclear facilities. Some of the existing facilities include the Transient Reactor Test Facility (TREAT), Neutron Radiography Reactor (NRAD), and the Demonstration of Microreactor Experiments (DOME). Some of the future Advanced Reactor Demonstration projects include Project Pele, Microreactor Applications Research Validation and Evaluation (MARVEL), Space Reactor 1 (SR-1), Versatile Autonomous Lightweight Kilowatt-class Reactor Experiment (VALKRE), Kaleidos Demonstration Unit (KDU) and the UNITY Pilot Reactor.

  • Develop performance-based initial and continuing training programs, using the systematic approach to training for nuclear facilities operator training programs, as well as other assigned operations support programs.

  • Develop and facilitate operational drills.

  • Present Simulator training and conduct simulator evaluations for Nuclear Reactor Operator personnel in the Glass Top Simulator, Basic Reactor Operator Simulator and reactor specific simulator/emulator/digital twin.

  • Maintain an in-depth understanding and knowledge of the systems, operating practices, procedures, and policies associated with nuclear facilities. May be required to maintain Senior Reactor Operator (SRO) level of knowledge.

  • Ensure assigned training programs comply with the requirements of program documents, company procedures, training implementation matrices, and training program plans.

  • Establish and maintain examination question banks for nuclear facility operations and operations support personnel. Develop, schedule, administer, grade, and evaluate written and oral examinations.

  • May be responsible for instruction of Technical Safety Requirements, reactor operating principles and characteristics, and control manipulations as well as systems operating principles and standards.

  • Analyze, design, develop, and evaluate specific training programs.

  • Training programs are equivalent to both licensed and non-licensed training programs in the commercial nuclear power industry.

  • Other duties as assigned.

Required:

  • Level 3: Bachelor’s degree and 5 years’ experience and applicable years’ experience for level or equivalent combination of operations and training experience. Master’s and 2 years of experience. PhD and 2 years of experience.

  • Level 4: Bachelor’s degree and 9 years’ experience and applicable years’ experience for level or equivalent combination of operations and training experience. Master’s and 6 years of experience. PhD and 4 years of experience.

  • This position requires the ability to obtain and maintain a Department of Energy “L" clearance, which requires US Citizenship.

  • Experience in operation or training at a research laboratory reactor, Commercial Reactor or US Navy Reactor.

  • Experience consistent with the material being presented.

Ideal Candidate Will Have the Following:

  • Current or prior Reactor Operator (RO) or Senior Reactor Operator (SRO) certification/license at a research laboratory reactor, Commercial Reactor or US Navy Reactor. (Navy Engineering Watch Supervisor (EWS) and Engineering Officer Of the Watch (EOOW) also considered)

  • Prior experience developing and facilitating drills.

  • Able to certify Reactor Operator or Senior Reactor Operator.

Physical Requirements:

While performing the duties of this classification, the employee is frequently required to stand, walk, sit, stoop, kneel, and bend. The job requires hand/finger dexterity to keyboard or type. The job requires operation of job-related equipment. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 35 pounds. Sufficient visual acuity and hearing capacity to perform the essential functions and interact with the public is required. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Job Information:

  • The pay range for this position is: Level 3($95,256 - $195,288)/Level 4 ($114,360 - $234, 336). At Idaho National Laboratory compensation decisions are determined using factors such as education, relevant experience, and other credentials.
  • TDP: This is a testing designated position; you will be required to submit to a pre-employment drug screen and periodic drug testing throughout the term of your employment.
  • Multi-Level: This is a multi-level posting and you will be placed at the appropriate level dependent on depth and breadth of proven experience and skills.

title: Senior Program Manager - Clinical Innovation
description:
This is a hybrid position and must be located within 100 miles of a Mayo Clinic campus for occasional on-site expectations based on business needs.

The Senior Program Manager works collaboratively with stakeholders to develop strategic initiatives, manage the execution of such initiatives. Identifies, evaluates and advances innovation care delivery, digital health and operational transformation opportunities aligned with Mayo Clinic's strategic priorities. The Senior Program Manager participates in gap identification and assessment to drive prioritization of work and may lead contract negotiations with external collaborators for activities within their assigned programs. Develops and manages strategic relationships with industry partners, technology vendors and internal stakeholders to supports evaluation, pilot implementation and scaling of innovative solutions. Initiates, actively manages, and maintains positive working relationships with internal and external groups. Acts as a mentor for direct and indirect report team members. The Senior Program Manager works independently, assuming primary responsibility for planning, directing, coordinating and delivering initiative and project activities through the entire project life cycle (from initiation to completion) that are major/complex/business critical. Leads complex healthcare technology, clinical operations and digital transformation initiatives involving multidisciplinary stakeholders. The Senior Program Manager is responsible to lead project objectives and completion on time, on budget, and in conformance to Mayo Clinic project management methodologies and standards. Accountable for achieving intended clinical, operational, financial and experience outcomes through effective implementation, adoption and sustainment program objectives. Responsible for generating and managing the overall budget (as applicable) within their assigned collaborations and for related projects. Leads and provides direction in the development and tracking of project budgets. This position requires significant capacity to manage multiple competing objectives, to prioritize, and to communicate complex information in clear and unambiguous terms to management and leadership. Uses data to define success metrics, evaluate outcomes, identify risks and support executive decision-making. This individual may support leadership in strategic planning processes. Serves as a strategic advisor by developing business cases, evaluating opportunities and providing recommendations to advance organizational priorities. Presents project requests to internal and external committees and oversight bodies to receive approval and project direction and input. Independently leads problem-solving and decision-making activities, within the scope of their assigned collaborations and related projects and change management processes taking reasonable and prudent actions to accomplish agreed upon project objectives. Leads change management efforts that drive stakeholder alignment, adoption and sustainable transformation. Leverages years of experience to manage stakeholder relationships and extensive projects and is highly competent in the implementation of project results. Uses advanced negotiation skills that are characterized by innovative thinking. Manages a portfolio of interconnected initiatives, balancing competing priorities, shared resources and strategic objectives across multiple stakeholders. Must have strong business acumen with the ability to work with people from diverse functional backgrounds and build relationships across the organization. Serves as a trusted advisor to senior leaders through executive presentations, governance participation and influence across matrixed organizational structures. May require matrix supervision and evaluation of staff from other departments and divisions, individuals from their assigned external collaborations, and/contractor/vendor resources. title: Data platform engineer
description:

At Ninety One, the vision for data is for trustworthy, discoverable and timely information to be at everybody’s fingertips. Data is our number one technology priority and foundational in our journey to become an AI-centred organisation.

Their mandate is to deliver high quality, business value solutions, while assuring the highest standards of speed, accuracy, stability and security.

Better data - by improving the quality, trustworthiness, traceability and ownership of data Faster data - by continuously reducing the time between data sourcing and information delivery More data - by expanding the contextual, historical and domain content available and making it discoverable

We believe in the power of technology to enable our vision and are looking for passionate, committed individuals to join us on our journey.

In this role you will have a unique opportunity to work in a blended role requiring Data Engineering, Azure Cloud Infrastructure and Dev Ops practices to keep Ninety One's Databricks environment reliable, secure and well governed while building automation, common tooling and self-service for platform users.

In this role you will: Work across both the data engineering and infrastructure/platform spaces to design, build and maintain solutions at the platform layer: Python solutions for platform and automation. Common shared libraries/modules used by data engineers and analysts across the platform. Pipelines/processes that support overall platform management (e.g. for purposes such as cost tracking, governance, provisioning, monitoring). CI/CD pipelines (Dev Ops/Git Hub Actions) for platform and application deployments Terraform Ia C for Azure services and Azure Databricks (e.g. Unity Catalog, workspaces, networking, compute policies) Collaborate with a wide ranging scope of teams including data engineers, analysts, security and infrastructure teams to translate requirements into capabilities. Provide platform support to engineering teams and platform users including assisting with issues, ranging from code, platform and infrastructure. Contribute to platform documentation, patterns and best-practice standards You should consider applying if you have: BSc Computer Science or equivalent Minimum 7 years technology experience, with at least 3 years’ experience in the cloud platform/data platform roles Intermediate Databricks engineering experience Intermediate knowledge of Microsoft Azure infrastructure Proficiency in Python and/or SQL;. NET is a plus Azure Dev Ops and/or Git Hub Actions Terraform (Ia C) experience, ideally in a multi-environment setup Understanding of Platform Governance, Security Experience in Data Modelling, Data Contracts and exposure to Fin Ops/cost attribution practices Some of the attributes we look for in a person are: The ability to build and maintain meaningful relationships The ability to 'approach and own' and continuously look for opportunities to develop A client focused and collaborative approach High conviction and be comfortable sharing opinions A curiosity about technology and its potential to drive innovation

title: Senior Endpoint Management Engineer (KACE/BigFix/Application Packaging)
description:

Opportunity:

Key Responsibilities:

Software Packaging and Deployment
