title: AI Agent Engineer
description:
What makes us Qlik?

A Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ Leader for 16 years in a row, Qlik helps teams get more out of AI with trusted data products, a powerful analytics engine, and AI agents. This helps teams reduce risk and operating costs, while scaling AI responsibly.

Used by 75% of the Fortune 500, Qlik works with the systems organizations already use, maintaining flexibility without lock-in.

The Agentic AI Engineer Role

Most AI programs stall between the build and the business. Someone architects something impressive, and then it sits — ungoverned, unadopted, and underperforming. The Agentic AI Engineer exists to make sure that never happens at Qlik.

This role has a clear mandate: scale and run the AI agent program that transforms how we serve 35,000 customers. You'll design the agents, define where they act, govern their quality, and bring our frontline teams along for the ride. No handoffs between 'the builder' and 'the operator' because you are both.

What makes this role interesting?

  • You’ll own the full lifecycle of an AI agent program from building the reasoning logic to governing how agents perform across 35,000 customer accounts. There’s no template for this; you’re defining it.
  • You’ll work at genuine technical depth (LLMs, n8n, RAG, APIs, Salesforce integrations) while also shaping strategy by deciding where agents should act, how quality is governed, and how frontline teams adopt AI as a co-pilot.
  • The impact is direct and measurable – reduction in formal escalations, automation of routine tasks for Cohort Leaders, and real-time visibility into every customer interaction across the book of business.
  • The challenge: this is a greenfield program in an environment defining its own processes. You’ll need to be equally comfortable in a terminal and in a cross‑functional planning meeting.

Here’s How You’ll Be Making An Impact

  • AI Agent Architecture & Development - You will primarily architect and integrate AI agent systems end-to-end, from concept through deployment.
  • Design and build AI agents from use case scoping and system prompt engineering through deployment and handoff to operational workflows
  • Develop automation pipelines using tools like n8n, integrating with core systems such as Salesforce to trigger the right interventions at the right moments
  • Define and implement data pipelines that feed agents the right context at the right time — including ingesting Value Erosion signals and translating them into automated Action plays
  • Build technical diagnostic logic to detect Value Erosion in real time, including automated identification of product defects and cases exceeding 5–10 support touchpoints without resolution
  • Collaborate with IT and the AI Practice on LLM, RAG, and API integrations into the Intelligent Front Door (IFD)
  • Instrument agents for observability — building in the feedback loops and evaluation criteria needed to measure quality and determine automation readiness
  • Execute rigorous testing to ensure all agents meet defined Confidence Gates before graduating to autonomous operation
  • Produce clear technical documentation and runbooks to support smooth handoffs and operational continuity
  • Contribute to roadmap planning by identifying new agentic use cases within the COI org Journey Orchestration & Experience Governance Beyond the build, you will own how agents are deployed and how the customer experience is governed
  • Define the precise insertion points across the customer journey where AI agents should act to automate adoption tasks and multiply Cohort Leader capacity
  • Lead the “Delight Audit” — reviewing human and agent interactions across the full account base to surface product, support, and experience improvement opportunities
  • Analyze audited touchpoints to identify Value Creation opportunities, specifically where improvements in education and knowledge can turn a neutral interaction into a delightful one
  • Own the Agent Health Dashboard, tracking universal KPIs (Accuracy, Adoption) and usecase specific KPIs (Value Enhancement Score, Time-to-Resolution) Change Management & Enablement
  • Lead the rollout of AI agents to frontline CSMs and Support teams, enabling them to confidently co‑pilot with AI
  • Translate audit findings into actionable feedback loops for Product, Support, and Data Intelligence teams
  • Drive the automatic drafting of Knowledge Base articles from resolved cases, closing documentation and education gaps in real time

What We Offer

A comprehensive onboarding experience paired with mentorship from seasoned professionals to ensure a strong start. Our supportive and inclusive culture fosters curiosity, creativity, and personal growth, while providing exposure to career paths across sales, marketing operations, and analytics.

Team members have access to a variety of professional development tools, training programs, and networking opportunities. In addition, we provide a competitive salary and benefits package to support your overall well‑being and success.

We’re Looking For a Teammate With

  • Proven experience building and deploying AI agents or intelligent automation systems in a customer‑facing environment
  • Strong operational instincts — you can define where and when agents act, not just how they work
  • A quality‑first mindset with a track record of building governance frameworks, testing protocols, or audit processes for AI systems
  • Hands‑on experience building with LLMs including prompt engineering, tool/function calling, and agentic design patterns
  • Familiarity with workflow automation platforms such as n8n, Make, or similar
  • Ability to work with APIs and webhooks — comfortable pulling and handling data from CRM systems like Salesforce
  • Strong systems thinking — you design for reliability and edge cases, not just the happy path
  • Comfortable operating in ambiguity — this team defines processes as it builds them
  • Collaborative — you work across functions and can translate technical decisions for non‑technical stakeholders

The location for this role is:

Ottawa, Canada

More About Qlik And Who We Are

Find out more about ‘Life at Qlik’ on social: Instagram, LinkedIn, YouTube, and X/Twitter, and to see all other opportunities to join us and our values, check out our Careers Page.

What else do we offer?

  • National Capital Region's 2026 Top Employers in Canada: https://reviews.canadastop100.com/top-employer-qliktech
  • Genuine career progression pathways and mentoring programs.
  • Culture of innovation, technology, collaboration, and openness.
  • Flexible, diverse, and international work environment.

Giving back is a huge part of our culture. Alongside an extra “change the world” day plus another for personal development, we also highly encourage participation in our Corporate Responsibility Employee Programs

title: Graduate Engineer, System IP Engineering - Systems
description:
We’re looking for a graduate engineer to join our growing hardware development team at a world-leading technology company. Please note that the expected start date for this role is from April 2027 onwards.

What you could be doing as a Graduate:

You’ll support the development of new hardware platforms used for prototyping Arm’s latest IP. You'll collaborate with experienced engineers across Software, SoC, Characterisation, and Verification teams, building your technical expertise while contributing to innovative hardware platforms. Your responsibilities may include:

  • Helping define specifications for new hardware platforms
  • Supporting the design and delivery of development boards based on Arm’s custom SoCs and FPGAs
  • Collaborating with platform architects and design teams to meet engineering goals
  • Learning how to work with external partners such as ODMs and CEMs

We are looking for individuals who:

Hold (or are on track to hold) a degree by the programme start date. This can be a Bachelors or Masters in Electrical/Electronic Engineering, Computer Science or a related field.

  • Basic understanding of compute architectures and system-level design

  • Enthusiasm for learning about high-speed digital design, PCB layout, and signal integrity
  • A collaborative approach, strong communication skills, and enthusiasm for working with diverse teams

Qualities that will help your application stand out:

We encourage early applications as we review them on a first come/first served basis.

Please note that relocation support is available for this role for domestic moves within the country and regional moves within Europe. Visa sponsorship support is also available for candidates who require it.

title: Billing & Collections Specialist
description:
The Billing and Collections Specialist manages billing, payment tracking, collections, reconciliation, and cash application for customer receivables.


This role owns the operational flow from signed agreements, through invoice submission, payment follow-up, reconciliation, and cash application.


This role works closely with the Sales department and other members of the Finance department to ensure that sales are billed accurately, payments are collected on time, records remain complete, and exceptions are resolved through the appropriate channels.


This is a hands-on role for a highly organized, detail-oriented professional who is comfortable working with contract and financial data and confident managing professional business-to-business payment communications.


Key Responsibilities

  • Review approved financing documentation for completeness, accuracy, and alignment with transaction requirements.
  • Maintain organized records for invoice requirements, payment schedules, remittance information, and related approvals.
  • Confirm that the required documentation is complete before billing.
  • Identify missing, inconsistent, or unclear contract and financial information and route exceptions to the appropriate department.

  • Track invoice acceptance, submission status, milestones, due dates, and payment commitments.
  • Coordinate with stakeholders to resolve billing questions and prevent avoidable delays.

  • Monitor aging balances, scheduled payments, overdue items, and unresolved invoice or remittance issues.
  • Conduct timely, professional follow-up with customers regarding invoice status, payment timing, missing remittance details, disputes, and past-due balances.
  • Coordinate customer-related questions and collection matters through the appropriate departments and maintain ownership through resolution.

  • Research unapplied cash, short payments, discrepancies, duplicate payments, and other exceptions.
  • Ensure that reconciliations are documented, and completed within required reporting or close timelines.
  • Maintain schedules, aging views, and supporting documentation needed for operational visibility and audit readiness.
  • Maintain clear ownership of every assigned invoice, balance, commitment, and next step until the item is resolved.

title: Project Manager – New Construction
description:
Stabbert Marine & Industrial is a family-owned company specializing in vessel repair, construction, and industrial solutions. With two full-service shipyards, in Ballard and Anacortes, and a commitment to quality, safety, and innovation, we deliver reliable marine services that keep the maritime industry moving forward.

POSITION SUMMARY:

The Project Manager is a dedicated, single-project role responsible for the new construction of SMI’s own semi-submersible barge at our Anacortes shipyard. Unlike our other project management roles, which support multiple outside clients at once, this position owns one internal build from start to finish and is the primary point of accountability for delivering the barge on schedule, within budget, and to specification. Because SMI is both the builder and the owner, the Project Manager is expected to bring the same cost and schedule discipline an outside owner would demand. The Project Manager uses Primavera P6 and earned value metrics, including the Schedule Performance Index (SPI) and Cost Performance Index (CPI), to build and maintain the project baseline, track costs and progress day to day, and drive production decisions on the yard. This is a hands-on role based in an active, outdoor shipyard environment.


ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS AND MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES (This list is not intended to detail all aspects of the assigned work but is representative of the job’s overall responsibilities):

· Own the overall execution of the semi-submersible barge newbuild, from project kickoff and engineering through construction, testing, and delivery.

· Develop, baseline, and maintain the integrated project schedule in Primavera P6, including the work breakdown structure, activity logic, critical path, resource loading, and regular progress updates.

· Build and manage the project budget, tracking labor hours, material, subcontract, and equipment costs against the baseline on a daily basis.

· Use earned value management to measure performance, applying SPI and CPI, along with schedule and cost variance, to identify negative trends early, forecast estimate at completion (EAC), and drive corrective action.

· Translate schedule and cost data into daily production priorities; work directly with superintendents, foremen, and leads to sequence work, set targets, and remove obstacles to production.

· Walk the job daily to verify reported progress against physical completion, confirm work quality, and keep schedule updates grounded in actual conditions on the ground.

· Coordinate engineering, planning, procurement, and production so that drawings, materials, and long-lead equipment arrive in time to support the build sequence.

· Manage scope and design change control: document, estimate, and track every change and its impact on cost and schedule, and secure leadership approval before changed work proceeds.

· Serve as the primary link between the shipyard and company leadership on the build, and coordinate with classification society surveyors and regulatory inspectors as applicable.

· Prepare and deliver daily and weekly progress, cost, and schedule reports to the General Manager and senior leadership, including earned value metrics, look-ahead schedules, risks, and recovery plans.

· Identify, assess, and manage project risks, escalating issues to the appropriate management channels with recommended solutions in time for leadership to act.

· Manage subcontractor and vendor scopes, schedules, and performance, and review invoices against verified progress.

· Support the shipyard’s safety program by ensuring safety and quality requirements are planned into work packages and are not traded off for schedule.

· Conduct checkpoint inspections and coordinate testing, trials, and final delivery documentation.

· Capture lessons learned and actual cost and schedule data to strengthen estimates and planning for future newbuild projects.


JOB SCOPE:

The role operates within established company standards and project requirements, with significant latitude for independent judgment in day-to-day project decisions. As part of the OpT staff, the Project Manager is accountable for the cost, schedule, and quality performance of the newbuild. This is a single, high-value capital project funded by the company, so slippage in schedule or cost lands directly on SMI. Without an outside customer enforcing a contract, the Project Manager is responsible for holding the line on scope, controlling informal changes, and recognizing negative trends early enough to act on them.


INTERPERSONAL CONTACTS:

The Project Manager works daily with production superintendents, foremen, and leads, as well as engineering, planning, procurement, safety, and finance. The position interacts regularly with senior leadership on project status and financial performance. Externally, the role represents the Company with vendors, equipment suppliers, subcontractors, and classification and regulatory inspectors. Face-to-face meetings on the yard occur daily throughout construction.


KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES:

· Advanced, hands-on proficiency in Primavera P6, including baseline development, schedule updates, critical path analysis, resource loading, and reporting.

· Strong working knowledge of earned value management, with demonstrated use of SPI, CPI, variances, and EAC to manage cost and schedule performance.

· Ability to turn schedule and cost data into clear production direction, with the credibility to hold craft leadership accountable to targets.

· Working knowledge of steel vessel or barge construction, including hull fabrication, modular/block construction, outfitting, and build sequencing.

· Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, specifications, and technical publications.

· Knowledge of cost tracking, labor reporting, material procurement, work orders, and change order management.

· Strong leadership and team-management skills, with the ability to set clear expectations and follow through.

· Clear, direct written and verbal communication with production crews, vendors, and senior leadership alike.

· Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills; able to spot technical and schedule issues early and develop practical solutions.

· Well-organized, detail-oriented, and self-motivated, with the ability to prioritize and follow tasks through to completion under pressure.

· Strong commitment to a team environment, with the ability to contribute expertise and follow leadership direction as appropriate.

· Proficiency in MS Office, particularly Excel; working skills in AutoCAD and Adobe DC preferred.


EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:

· High School Diploma or GED Certificate is required. BA/BS degree in engineering, construction management, naval architecture, or a related field is preferred; equivalent work experience will be considered.

· Minimum five (5) years of project management experience in shipbuilding, ship repair, or heavy industrial construction. New construction experience is strongly preferred.

· Demonstrated experience building and managing project schedules in Primavera P6 is required.

· Demonstrated experience using SPI and CPI to budget, schedule, and track project costs is required.

· PMP or similar project management certification is a plus.


WORKING CONDITIONS AND PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:

· Regular schedule is 7:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. at the Anacortes shipyard. Additional hours may be required to support critical milestones, testing, or schedule recovery.

· This position spends a significant portion of each day in outdoor production areas and must be able to work outside in all weather conditions, including rain, wind, cold, and heat.

· Work is performed in an active shipyard with exposure to noise, dust, fumes, welding and grinding operations, overhead lifts, moving equipment, and uneven or wet walking surfaces. Required PPE must be worn at all times in production areas.

· Must be able to walk to and from job sites and around the yard and vessel for extended periods.

· Must be able to climb inclined stairways and vertical ladders, enter confined spaces and tanks, and work at heights.

· Must be able to lift up to 20 pounds.

· There may be local and out-of-town travel (including air travel) up to 5% of the time with notice.


COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

Salary range: $110,000 – $120,000 per year, depending on experience. This is a full-time, exempt salary position. Benefits include:

· Medical, dental, and vision insurance

· Paid time off (PTO)

· Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

· 401(k) retirement plan with employer match options

· Bonus opportunities

title: Test Engineer

title: Localisation Quality Coordinator
description:
As a leading game localization company, we offer integrated text, audio localization, and localization QA for all regions, languages and platforms, ensuring a fully authentic offering for players worldwide.

Our global footprint across Asia, Oceania, Europe, and the Americas enables us to run 24-hour follow-the-sun workflows, allowing our professional translators and game developers continue to work on your project around the clock and delivering on even the most challenging timelines.

The team at Keywords Studios handles media localization and translation services for any project size, from indie to AAA games. We help you speak to global audiences by translating your games for your target language and dialect, and ensure expert quality control throughout the game development and translation process through both technology solutions and human oversight.

Job Summary

The Quality Management team ensures that localized content consistently meets the highest standards of accuracy, creativity, and player experience. We achieve this by evaluating performance, driving continuous improvement initiatives, enabling linguists and vendors through training and feedback, and partnering with stakeholders to prevent issues before they reach the player. Our work spans resource evaluation, process optimization, and tool enhancement, ensuring quality is embedded at every stage of the localization workflow.

The Localization Quality Coordinator supports Localization teams across Keywords in implementing and upholding quality processes, ensuring that content meets client expectations, style guidelines, and franchise-specific requirements. This role combines data-driven analysis with linguistic expertise, acting as a bridge between Project Management, Resource Management, and external vendors.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Collaborate with Localization Managers and Project Managers to assess risk & create quality plans, reviewing them regularly and making sure they are effective.
  • Analyze and present timely, actionable reports on quality performance against set standards, identifying risks and recommending corrective or preventive measures.
  • Champion quality standards and processes across Localisation teams, promoting a consistent approach across projects and languages.
  • Define, deliver, and continuously improve training sessions and guidance materials for internal linguists, external vendors, and other stakeholders on quality processes.
  • Validate, arbitrate, and finalise quality evaluations, ensuring consistent application of scoring frameworks and fair dispute resolution.
  • Support PMs in delivering constructive, actionable feedback to external resources.
  • Collaborate on tool and process improvements, including the Quality Evaluation Portal, translation quality evaluation systems, and automated QA checks, suggesting enhancements based on recurring trends or workflow bottlenecks.
  • Contribute to root cause analysis for quality incidents and client complaints, helping define preventive actions and assess their effectiveness.
  • Assist in onboarding and testing processes for new linguists, ensuring alignment with quality standards before integration into live projects.
  • Leverage Generative AI tools (such as Gemini) to optimize daily workflows, streamline data analysis, and assist in drafting quality reports and CAPAs.

Requirements

  • Based in an Asian timezone with the ability to work closely with regional teams and vendors.
  • Minimum 2 years’ experience in a related role within the localisation industry.
  • A degree in Translation, Linguistics, or a related field.
  • Ideally, a native speaker of Korean, Japanese, or Chinese, with excellent proficiency in English.
  • Excellent communication and negotiation skills, with the ability to provide clear, actionable feedback.
  • Demonstrated ability to work effectively with distributed, multicultural teams.
  • Intermediate to advanced Excel skills; ability to extract, process, and interpret data for decision-making.
  • Familiarity with translation quality evaluation systems, frameworks (e.g., MQM), and CAT tools.
  • Experience with linguistic arbitration or dispute resolution in a professional setting is desirable.
  • Strong analytical mindset with the ability to identify patterns, prioritise issues, and propose process improvements.
  • Knowledge of localisation quality control processes and industry best practices.
  • Ability to adapt quickly to new tools and workflows, with demonstrated hands-on experience using using generative AI (specifically Gemini) for day-to-day productivity, process improvement, and problem-solving.
  • Ideally, a familiarity with Audio Localization processes.

title: Lead Product Manager - Ethernet Network (Remote, US)
description:
Lumen is the trusted network for the AI‑powered world, connecting people, data, and applications through our expansive fiber network and connected ecosystem. We enable secure, high‑performance connectivity across cloud, edge, and AI workloads for enterprises, governments, and communities.

At Lumen, you’ll work on infrastructure customers rely on today and build for what’s next, where performance, security, and resilience matter.

This is a high accountability environment where bold ideas drive real innovation for our customers, partners, and industry. The work is challenging, expectations are clear, and trust is built into how we operate. If you’re ready to take ownership, deliver meaningful impact, and help shape the future of AI‑ready connectivity, join us today.

The Role

The Lead Product Manager – Ethernet Network owns the strategy, roadmap, delivery, go-to-market execution, and lifecycle performance of Lumen’s Ethernet network product. This role serves as the accountable business voice for the product within its Agile Release Train (ART), translating customer needs, market opportunities, product-line priorities, and network strategy into a clear, prioritized feature backlog that engineering teams can execute. The Lead Product Manager partners across architecture, engineering, operations, sales, marketing, finance, legal, and regulatory teams to evolve the Ethernet network, improve customer outcomes, and deliver sustainable revenue and margin growth. The role requires strong technical and commercial judgment, disciplined product leadership, and hands-on Agile Product Manager accountability within Lumen’s SAFe operating model.

The Main Responsibilities

  • Own the Ethernet network product vision, strategy, roadmap, objectives, and key results across the full lifecycle—from concept and investment through launch, growth, optimization, and retirement.
  • Act as the voice of the customer by analyzing customer needs, market trends, competitive alternatives, sales insights, and operational data to define differentiated product capabilities and priorities.
  • Develop and maintain a 12–24 month product roadmap aligned with Lumen’s network evolution, business strategy, transformation priorities, and related product portfolios.
  • Own, maintain, and prioritize the product’s feature backlog, ensuring features have clear business outcomes, requirements, acceptance criteria, dependencies, and readiness for engineering execution.
  • Write and prioritize features in close partnership with Product Owners, System Architects, engineering teams, and other delivery partners; decompose higher-level capabilities and strategic direction into executable increments of value.
  • Represent the product in SAFe planning and delivery activities, including PI Planning, roadmap and vision reviews, backlog refinement, PO Sync, System Demos, and outcome reviews.
  • Track and manage product-level risks, assumptions, dependencies, impediments, and trade-offs in Jira, escalating decisions that require broader product-line or leadership alignment.
  • Partner with Technical Program Managers and delivery leaders to coordinate cross-team dependencies and maintain transparency on scope, sequencing, milestones, and delivery health.
  • Lead product-level business planning, including business cases, pricing inputs, investment and resource needs, revenue and margin opportunities, and ongoing measurement of ROI, KPIs, OKRs, and backlog health.
  • Coordinate go-to-market and launch readiness across engineering, network operations, marketing, sales, customer success, support, finance, legal, and regulatory stakeholders.
  • Enable sales and solution teams with clear positioning, customer benefits, competitive differentiation, roadmap guidance, and assessment of qualified feature or customization requests.
  • Maintain accurate, current product documentation and communications, and provide clear updates on strategy, roadmap, delivery progress, product performance, and decisions.
  • Build subject-matter expertise in Ethernet services, network capabilities, customer use cases, and the applicable competitive and regulatory environment.
  • Influence and align cross-functional teams without direct authority, using data, customer insight, and sound product judgment to drive decisions and accountability.

What We Look For in a Candidate

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent education and relevant experience.
  • Five or more years of experience in product management, technical product ownership, or a related discipline within telecommunications, networking, software, platform, or technology services.
  • Demonstrated end-to-end ownership of a product or major feature area, including strategy, roadmap development, requirements, delivery, launch, and performance management.
  • Experience translating customer and business needs into well-defined features, requirements, and acceptance criteria in partnership with engineering teams.
  • Working knowledge of Ethernet services and network technologies, with the technical aptitude to evaluate product, platform, API, operational, and architectural trade-offs.
  • Experience operating in an Agile or SAFe delivery environment, including backlog prioritization, PI Planning, and cross-functional delivery coordination.
  • Demonstrated ability to use customer insight, market analysis, financial data, and performance metrics to make product investment and prioritization decisions.
  • Experience developing business cases and supporting pricing, go-to-market, launch-readiness, and sales-enablement activities.
  • Strong written, verbal, presentation, and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with technical teams, business partners, and senior leaders.
  • Proven ability to lead through influence, manage competing priorities, resolve ambiguity, and deliver results in a fast-paced matrixed organization.
  • Hands-on proficiency with Jira and Microsoft Excel; familiarity with APIs, product analytics, and roadmap or portfolio-management tools is preferred.

title: Vær med til at sikre rent vand i hanen og havet – bliv driftsleder hos AquaDjurs
description:
Vil du stå i spidsen for en drift, hvor ny teknologi, AI og datadrevne løsninger får en stadig større rolle? Og søger du samtidig en arbejdsplads med stærkt sammenhold, gode udviklingsmuligheder og plads til livet ved siden af jobbet?

Hos AquaDjurs får du mulighed for begge dele. Vi søger en driftsleder, der vil lede og udvikle driften af vores renseanlæg og samtidig være med til at sætte retningen for fremtidens spildevandsrensning.

En hverdag med ledelse teknologi og udvikling

Som driftsleder får du ansvar for den daglige drift af AquaDjurs’ 10 renseanlæg og bliver leder for et erfarent og engageret team.

Du kommer tæt på både mennesker og drift. Din vigtigste opgave som leder bliver at skabe gode rammer for medarbejderne, sætte retning og sikre, at faglighed, samarbejde og nye idéer bliver omsat til en stabil og effektiv drift.

Samtidig står AquaDjurs midt i en spændende udvikling. Spildevandsrensningen skal i stigende grad centraliseres på Fornæs Renseanlæg, og nye teknologier skal være med til at gøre driften mere intelligent, energieffektiv og robust.

Her får du en central rolle

Du bliver blandt andet involveret i arbejdet med automatisering, online målinger, hydrauliske modeller og AI-baserede værktøjer. Målet er at bruge data og teknologi endnu bedre til at optimere renseanlæg, pumpestationer og bassiner og samtidig være på forkant med fremtidens miljøkrav.

Du kommer også til at arbejde med nye renseteknologier og løsninger inden for blandt andet ressourcegenvinding, energieffektivitet og håndtering af nye miljøfremmede stoffer.

Du får ansvar men står ikke alene

Du bliver en del af den daglige ledelse og får et tæt samarbejde med kolleger på tværs af AquaDjurs.

Dine vigtigste opgaver bliver at:

· lede, udvikle og skabe gode rammer for driftsteamet

· sikre en stabil, sikker og energieffektiv drift

· bruge procesdata og analyser til at finde forbedringer

· drive udviklingen mod mere automatiseret og datadrevet drift

· være med til at vurdere og implementere nye rense- og procesteknologier

· samarbejde på tværs af organisationen om fremtidens løsninger.

Hvem er du

Vi forestiller os, at du har en teknisk eller naturvidenskabelig baggrund – eksempelvis som biolog, kemiingeniør, miljøingeniør, maskinmester eller tilsvarende. Det er en fordel, hvis du har erfaring med spildevandsrensning eller andre procesanlæg.

Du har erfaring med ledelse og trives med at være synlig og tæt på dine medarbejdere. Du behøver ikke selv have alle svarene. Til gengæld skal du være nysgerrig, kunne sætte retning og give medarbejderne plads og ansvar.

Fagligt har du forståelse for biologiske og kemiske processer og arbejder analytisk med drift og procesoptimering. Samtidig interesserer du dig for digitalisering og ny teknologi og kan se mulighederne i automatisering, data og AI – og være med til at omsætte dem til løsninger, der fungerer i praksis.

En arbejdsplads med plads til ambitioner og hverdagsliv

title: Bliv vores nye driftsleder i BAUHAUS Valby
description:
Er du en leder, der får struktur, mennesker og resultater til at gå hånd i hånd? Hos BAUHAUS Valby søger vi en driftsleder, der tager ansvar, skaber overblik og får tingene til at ske - hver dag.

Som driftsleder bliver du en del af varehusets ledelsesteam og får ansvaret for driften sammen med dit driftsteam. Sammen sikrer I, at butikken står skarp, effektiv og salgsklar - og at kunderne får en god oplevelse, hver gang.

Din rolle og hverdag

Du samarbejder tæt med varehuschefen, salgschefen og logistiklederen og refererer til Driftschefen. Du har fokus på at skabe et effektivt samspil mellem lager, butik og kundeservice.

Dine opgaver

  • Lede, motivere og udvikle driftsteamet i det daglige
  • Sikre, at butikken er salgsklar, trimmet og opfyldt efter BAUHAUS’ koncept
  • Planlægge og følge op på drift, bemanding og opgavefordeling
  • Sikre korrekt håndtering af varer, min/max-lokationer og lagerstyring
  • Koordinere med logistikken om varemodtagelse, opfyldning og ordrer

Hvem er du?
Du er en naturlig leder, der trives med at tage ansvar og skabe struktur. Du har overblik, følger op og motiverer andre gennem tydelig kommunikation og faglig respekt.

Vi forestiller os, at du:

  • Har ledererfaring fra detail, byggeri eller logistik

  • Har forståelse for drift, sikkerhed og struktur
  • Trives i et miljø med tempo og variation
  • Er engageret, løsningsorienteret og en kollega, man kan regne med

Det får du hos os

Hos BAUHAUS får du en lederrolle med stor betydning for både medarbejdere og kunder – og mulighed for at præge hverdagen.
Vi tilbyder:

  • Ordnede forhold og fast vagtplan - weekendvagt hver 4. uge
  • Medarbejderrabat, sundhedsforsikring og pensionsordning
  • Gode udviklingsmuligheder - både fagligt og personligt
  • En arbejdsplads, hvor vi hjælper hinanden og går op i at gøre tingene ordentligt

Klar til næste skridt?
Send din ansøgning og CV hurtigst muligt - vi holder samtaler løbende og ansætter, når vi har fundet den rette kollega.

Har du spørgsmål, er du velkommen til at kontakte Driftschefen Jacob, som gerne fortæller mere om rollen.

Vi glæder os til at høre fra dig!

title: Experience Technical Architect, Innovation & Emerging Technologies
description:
Job Description:

The Experience Technical Architect, Innovation & Emerging Technologies is a hands-on, full-stack technical architect who owns the technical architecture and implementation of AI and agentic prototype solutions within Horizon's committed-build phase, bringing deep experience building rapid proofs-of-concept and shipping at speed under compressed timelines.


This role translates solution architectures into working, tested code spanning custom integrations and programming languages/frameworks, data pipelines, and agentic automation, with a track record of threading custom development into platforms across the Adobe ecosystem (i.e., AEM, GenStudio, Firefly, CX Enterprise CoWorker, Adobe Experience Platform, and adjacent Adobe products).


Balancing velocity with code quality in an agile, iterative delivery model, the Experience Technical Architect establishes and applies coding standards, drives prototypes to production readiness under compressed timelines, and maintains the patterns and documentation that make knowledge transfer possible.


Key Responsibilities

The responsibilities below reflect core needs for this role.

  • Lead sprint execution, breaking solution architecture into testable, shippable increments across two-week sprints.
  • Build custom integrations, data pipelines, custom interfaces, and agentic automation, including fine-tuned AI models, wiring GenStudio, Firefly, CX Enterprise CoWorker, AEP, and AEM into customer systems via APIs.
  • Design and implement custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) connectors that enable seamless integration between Adobe’s AI/agentic solutions and client enterprise systems, accelerating prototype time-to-value and reducing manual data handoffs.
  • Architect third-party connector strategies and build integration patterns that extend Adobe capabilities into client data ecosystems, knowledge bases, and operational systems while maintaining data governance and security standards.
  • Lead AI hardening and production readiness validation for emerging capabilities and custom builds, identifying edge cases, failure modes, and mitigation strategies before client pilot launch.
  • Define data schemas, lineage, and governance frameworks that support experimental AI use cases, ensuring data quality and traceability as prototypes move from innovation labs into production pilots.
  • Write and ship production-quality code hands-on across the stack (e.g., JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, Java, Node.js, React) and operate within agile build/deploy cadences, including CI/CD pipelines, feature branching, and frequent iterative releases.
  • Establish coding standards, run code reviews, and work closely with other developers to align on technical patterns, quality practices, and integration best practices.
  • Work with solution architects to stress-test technical feasibility and feed implementation learnings back into architecture decisions.
  • Partner with the Lead Architect, Product Manager, and Innovation Strategy Lead to clearly document integration approaches, configuration decisions, and known issues, so future teams can sustain and extend the build.
  • Track technical dependencies and coordinate with customer infrastructure teams to secure timely access to the staging and production environments you need to build, test, and ship.
  • Partner with QA to execute test plans and validate releases before they ship.

Required Qualifications

  • 8+ years of software engineering or technical architecture experience, including hands-on development across backend, front-end, and data integration technologies.
  • 3+ years of hands-on experience developing or integrating solutions within the Adobe ecosystem, with experience across one or more Adobe solutions and extending platform capabilities through APIs and custom development.
  • 3+ years of experience designing and building API-based integrations, data pipelines, or event-driven architectures connecting enterprise platforms and customer-experience applications.
  • 2+ years of hands-on experience building AI-enabled applications or solutions, including experience with AI-assisted coding, prompt engineering, agent/LLM configurations, fine-tuning, or custom AI model integration.
  • Hands-on proficiency in at least 3 relevant programming languages/frameworks, such as JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, Java, Node.js, React, and SQL.
  • 5+ years working in agile software development environments, including Scrum/Kanban, 1-2 week sprints, CI/CD deploy pipelines, feature branching, and frequent iterative releases.
  • Demonstrated experience taking at least 2 rapid proofs-of-concept or prototypes through implementation or production/pilot readiness, ideally within compressed timelines and ambiguous, rapidly changing requirements.
  • Demonstrated experience defining technical patterns and coding standards, conducting code reviews, and working with other developers to maintain code quality.
  • Strong problem-solving skills and demonstrated ability to operate effectively in emerging-technology environments with minimal guardrails.

Additional Information

The annual base salary range for this position is $136,000 - $190,000. Placement within the salary range is based on a variety of factors, including relevant experience, knowledge, skills, and other factors permitted by law. Additionally, this position is eligible for discretionary incentive compensation.


Benefits available with this position include:

· Medical, vision, and dental insurance

· Life insurance

· Short-term and long-term disability insurance

· 401k

· Flexible paid time off

· At least 15 paid holidays per year

· Paid sick and safe leave

· Paid parental leave

Job Summary

The Quantitative Biosciences Institute (QBI) at UCSF brings together researchers across the biomedical, physical, and computational sciences to address complex problems in biology and human disease. QBI supports large, multi-investigator programs that integrate quantitative proteomics, structural biology, genetics, and advanced computational and AI methods, and works extensively with academic, government, and industry partners in the United States and internationally. Based at Byers Hall on the UCSF Mission Bay campus, QBI provides a highly collaborative, interdisciplinary environment in which computational scientists work directly alongside experimental groups to translate large-scale biological data into mechanistic understanding and therapeutic hypotheses.

Custom Scope

Functions as a recognized expert in computational bioinformatics, AI/machine learning, and structural biology, with responsibility for developing and directing advanced computational approaches used across multiple major QBI research programs and collaborations. Applies expert knowledge to highly complex, novel problems in protein-protein interaction prediction, structural modeling, scientific AI, and large-scale biological data integration where established approaches may be inadequate or nonexistent.

Provides computational leadership across multi-investigator research programs involving researchers from multiple UCSF schools, departments, and research centers, as well as domestic and international academic institutions and other external collaborators. Current work supports major QBI collaborative initiatives, including the ARIA-funded autism program and research collaborations involving institutions such as Gladstone Institutes, NYU Langone Health, Johns Hopkins University, and the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, as well as research supported through federal programs including NIH and DARPA.

Serves as a senior technical authority who shapes computational strategy, establishes and advances technical standards and reproducibility practices, develops computational methods and resources intended for reuse across research teams, and provides authoritative consultation to scientists and computational professionals. Represents QBI and UCSF computational expertise through collaborative publications, presentations, methods, and resources shared internally and externally. title: Program Officer
description: ABOUT THE DAVID AND LUCILE PACKARD FOUNDATION Founded in 1964 by David and Lucile Packard, The David and Lucile Packard Foundation (the Foundation) is a family philanthropy dedicated to supporting leaders and organizations around the world working to invest in children and families, protect and restore the natural world, and create just and inclusive societies. For more than six decades, the Foundation has advanced scientific innovation, championed reproductive health and rights, conserved and restored our natural world, and invested in the well-being of children and families. The Foundation’s goals today include: • Build Just Societies: support a strong civil society and inclusive institutions and governance to build just and equitable societies for all people. • Protect and Restore Our Natural World: champion bold climate solutions, an ocean that sustains us, and scientific innovation and discovery to secure the health and future of people and planet. • Invest in Families and Communities: prioritize the importance of children having a healthy start and promoting resilient and vibrant communities where children and families thrive, so they have the power to shape their lives. To achieve lasting change, the Foundation also strives to address root causes of longstanding problems, including building a thriving, resilient U.S. democracy; advancing racial justice in the United States and gender equity globally; and supporting a strong civil society around the globe. Inclusive collaboration is the heart of the Foundation’s approach, with the belief that actively listening to and learning from people with a wide range of views is the best way to create solutions that match the scale and urgency of the challenges we face. The Foundation is dedicated to supporting community-based solutions shaped by the knowledge and experience of the people whose lives are most affected and informed by data, recognizing that meaningful solutions require patience, urgency, and supporting the conditions for transformational change. The Foundation is committed to addressing complex issues over the long term while making tangible progress today. The Foundation’s Vision, Mission, and Values are as follows: • Vision: A just and equitable world where both people and nature flourish. • Mission: We work with people and communities to create enduring solutions for just societies and a healthy, resilient natural world. • Values: Equity, Integrity, Belief in Individual Leadership, Thinking Big, Respect, and Effectiveness. U.S. RACIAL JUSTICE INITIATIVE As the Packard Foundation advances its goal to “Build Just Societies,” essential to supporting thriving families, strong communities, and a sustainable natural world, it is clear that advancing racial justice in the United States is essential—both in its own right and to a healthy democracy, where the full participation, representation, and protection of all communities are safeguarded. The U.S. Racial Justice initiative aims to accelerate progress toward just and equitable outcomes for Black people and communities, creating ripple effects that expand opportunity, improve social and economic outcomes, and build a more just society for everyone. We advance this goal through grantmaking across three interconnected portfolios: • Strengthening the leadership and voices of those most affected by injustice in the U.S. South, so they can help shape our collective future. • Investing in efforts to defend the constitutional and legal rights guaranteed to all. • Catalyzing big ideas that propel us toward a more just and equitable future. Together, these efforts contribute to a nation more fully aligned with its highest ideals. THE PROGRAM OFFICER ROLE Located within the Just Societies goal area and reporting to the Director of the Racial Justice Initiative, this Program Officer will lead a grantmaking portfolio focused on defending and advancing constitutional and civil rights as a core strategy for racial justice. They need to bring strong knowledge of civil rights, particularly the 14th Amendment framework, and the ability to translate theory, application, and strategy into clear, actionable grantmaking approaches. They will be able to identify which legal strategies create meaningful opportunities to advance racial justice and shape funding partnerships that advance the work. The Program Officer will design and manage a portfolio that supports work across litigation, enforcement, community leadership, and public narrative. They will build relationships with legal experts, advocates, and community leaders, and collaborate with colleagues and funding partners to extend the reach and impact of the portfolio. They will partner with grantees and seek out new grantees, recommend grants, and serve as a resource and connector for grantees in the execution of program strategies. The ideal candidate is a strong analytical thinker who is comfortable navigating complexity and change. They bring a clear commitment to equity and racial justice, communicate effectively, and center the perspectives of impacted communities in their work. They will also bring a nonpartisan, innovative, creative approach to this work, and will stay abreast of emerging trends, synthesizing information across a dynamic field, to inform strategy. THE OPPORTUNITY Grantmaking and Strategic Leadership In partnership with the Director, lead the development and implementation of the strategy for one or more portfolios within the Racial Justice initiative. Lead all aspects of annual grantmaking, assessing opportunities, recommending new grants, managing relationships with grantee partners, and evaluating the impact of investments. Empower and enable grantee partners to achieve meaningful impact through specific policy and programmatic objectives, providing expertise/technical assistance as needed. Clearly and consistently communicate with grant recipients, staff, and other partners in a transparent, timely, and respectful manner. Partner with other Foundation staff, consultants, and grantees to ensure effective grantmaking and that deadlines and budgets are met or readjusted as needed. Manage the grant proposal process and contribute to the shaping of proposals. Manage complex processes and projects involving multiple institutions and cross-functional Foundation teams. Review and resolve legal, financial, and technical issues raised by specific grants and grant reports. Produce high quality and timely materials for senior leadership and the Board, including quarterly Board docket materials, strategy documents, updates, dashboards, and other materials as needed. Strategic and Field Leadership Organize foundation-sponsored convenings of grantees and field experts, including legal experts, advocates, movement leaders, and peer funders. Research, analyze, identify, and cultivate new opportunities for investment in the civil rights and racial justice landscape, translating into funding strategies. Integrate strategic communications and monitoring and evaluation into the portfolio's grantmaking strategies, maintaining a dynamic learning environment for grantees and staff where lessons learned are regularly synthesized and shared. Collaborate with key internal and external stakeholders to provide strategic leadership, identify gaps, and develop effective solutions across the field. Effectively represent the Foundation and the U.S. Racial Justice Initiative externally with credibility and clarity across a wide range of audiences, including meeting with current and potential grantees, giving presentations and attending public forums and conferences on topics of relevance, and when interacting with nonprofit, intergovernmental and private sector leaders, elected officials, academics, collaboratives and journalists. Contribute to broader field building efforts through writing, collaboration, and other forms of thought leadership.

title: Program Manager
description:
About Ascent

Ascent Global Logistics, headquartered in Belleville, Michigan, is a leading global provider of expedited, time-critical logistics solutions and other direct transportation services. The company connects customers to its extensive carrier network, internal ground fleet and airline via its proprietary, digital PEAK freight marketplace, which provides robust carrier capacity and transparent pricing, backed by 24/7/365 logistics experts. Ascent’s offerings include air charter and ground expedited solutions as well as truckload, less-than-truckload, global forwarding, brokerage, and managed transportation services. The experienced Ascent team solves customers’ most challenging logistics needs by providing industry-leading service and top-tier satisfaction.

Our Guiding Principles


At the core of Ascent's culture is a strong commitment to excellence, driven by the passion and dedication of every team member. We're equally dedicated to going above and beyond for our customers, ensuring this commitment extends beyond our team and brings exceptional value to those we serve. We aim for perfect execution in everything we do and ‘play hard’ by creating an environment where tasks are performed with a can-do attitude from start to finish. We ‘play smart’ by delivering on our commitments in an honest, fair, and ethical manner. We treat every person with whom we interface with the utmost dignity and respect. We understand that our teammates are our most valuable assets, so we ‘play together’ by making every effort to provide a professional and enjoyable experience, enabling careers to flourish and personal growth to be achieved.

What You’ll Do

The Program Manager owns the program of related technology initiatives for a single business domain. For this position, the domain is two shared programs: Ascent's customer-facing shipment visibility platform, which serves every business unit, and the final-mile business unit and its operating application. The Program Manager aligns that work to the domain's strategic objectives and carries it from framing through delivery and benefits realization. It is a strategic, hands-on role: the Program Manager is the connective owner across the domain's initiatives, the primary partner to its business sponsors, and the internal IT subject-matter expert for the domain's applications, with agentic AI as primary leverage. The core of the role is translating business needs into a clear, sequenced program roadmap that product owners and delivery teams can build against.

Program Ownership and Strategic Alignment

  • Own the domain's portfolio of related initiatives as a single program; align it to the business area's objectives and shape sequencing and roadmap.
  • Frame major project outcomes with the business and translate them into a coherent program plan.
  • Serve as the internal IT subject-matter expert for the domain's applications, maintaining deep knowledge of how those systems work and how the business uses them.
  • Maintain one integrated roadmap for the shared customer visibility platform with its product owner, so requests from every business unit are sequenced in a single plan.

Business Need to Program Roadmap

  • Understand how the business units operate and how the platforms are used by employees and customers, so requests are evaluated against how the work is done.
  • Work with the business to define the current state, the target state and the process change in between before a build begins, so requirements reflect the real workflow rather than assumptions.
  • Turn business needs into outcome statements, scope and sequencing on the program roadmap; make the trade-offs visible and get them decided.

Cross-Initiative Coordination and Dependencies

  • Manage interdependencies across the domain initiatives and across the IT delivery teams, so the program advances.
  • Coordinate timing, handoffs, and sequencing across initiatives; surfacing conflicts early.
  • Governance and Reporting
  • Run the program's governance and cadence: decisions, transparency, and status to sponsors and leadership.
  • Champion PMO methodology and standards to ensure consistency across the program.

Benefits Realization

  • Determine the business value of program initiatives based on defined outcomes.
  • Provide visibility into progress toward program outcomes and value delivery

Business UAT Engagement (major and higher-risk projects)

  • Identify, recruit, and engage business UAT testers.
  • Responsible for UAT schedule and milestones; UAT team owns validation protocols and sign-off.

Stakeholder and Program Risk

  • Own the sponsor and stakeholder relationship for the domain and keep expectations aligned as the program evolves.
  • Manage program change management communication to promote clear, timely messaging about what is changing and when.
  • Track program-level risks and issues and escalate to the appropriate level with context, options, and a recommendation.

Agentic AI

  • Use AI to draft plans, status, and reporting, accelerate program documentation, and reduce routine coordination overhead.

What You’ll Bring

  • 7+ years managing programs or large, cross-functional initiatives, ideally within a PMO.
  • Strong command of program governance, dependency management, and benefits realization.
  • Experience partnering with senior business stakeholders to align technology outputs with business outcomes.
  • Strong executive communication skills: able to brief senior leaders concisely, present options and recommendations, and communicate key decision points for leaders to act on.
  • Proven ability to translate business needs into program roadmaps: outcome statements, scope, actionable plans for sequencing and trade-offs that product owners and delivery teams.
  • Strong experience in logistics or supply chain, including time spent in or supporting an operation’s role and its business processes.
  • Working knowledge of Agile and structured delivery methods.
  • Demonstrated fluency using AI tools to accelerate program and reporting work.
  • Bachelor's degree in a related field; PMP, PgMP, PRINCE2, or similar certification preferred.

title: Part Time Specimen Processor I
description:
Overview

A Specimen Processor I prepares and handles specimens received for testing. Specimen Processors will work with management and quality team members to ensure laboratory activities are defined, documented, and completed to support inspection readiness. They will also ensure compliance is maintained through procedures, training, and documentation.

Responsibility

  1. Works under the direct supervision of an employee or supervisor who is trained and competent in all relative procedures and processes pertaining to accessioning as well as other assigned processes.
  2. Prepares and handles specimens for testing:
    1. Assigns specimens an internal tracking number (accession ID).
    2. Compares and verifies identifiers on specimens match test order.
    3. Ensures specimens are labeled appropriately.
    4. Communicates important information pertaining to testing.
    5. Looks for and documents problems with specimens.
    6. Scans, files, and electronically saves paperwork received with specimens.
    7. Files and temporary stores specimens until test release.
    8. Transports specimens to testing labs.
    9. Packages specimens for return, or external/internal lab send out.
    10. Performs other duties as assigned.
  3. Complies with and maintains competency in all assigned laboratory policies and procedures.
  4. Observes all compliance and regulatory requirements, particularly those associated to data security and patient confidentiality.
  5. Actively participates in and maintains accepted laboratory standards for continuing education.
  6. Maintains ethical standards in the performance of testing and in interactions with co-workers and other staff.
  7. Plays an active role within the team and helps to create a positive work environment. This includes participating in team building events and communicating positively with others.
  8. Arrives to work on time and is regular in attendance.
  9. Meets productivity and quality standards/rates set by the department and lab operations.
  10. Works with team members to resolve department problems and help implement improvement projects.
  11. Supports leadership by providing feedback to better support the team and needs of the department. This includes responding to department and company surveys.

Qualifications

  1. High school diploma or GED equivalent required.
  2. Data entry experience preferred.
  3. Excellent organizational, communication, multitasking and teamwork skills.
  4. Detail oriented with the ability to multitask.
  5. Basic computer knowledge needed.

Physical Requirements

Lifting Requirements: Medium work or exerting up to 50 pounds of force occasionally, 20 pounds of force frequently, and 10 pounds of force consistently.

Physical Requirements: Stationary positioning, moving, operating, ascending/descending, communicating, observing, reaching, and repetitive motion. Use of equipment and tools necessary to perform essential job functions.

Hazards and Atmospheric Conditions: Exposure to fumes, dust, extreme temperatures, wet and/or humidity, noise, vibration, mists or gases, mechanical hazards, chemical hazards, electrical hazards, and radiant energy hazards.

OSHA Category I: Duties performed routinely requires exposure to blood, body fluid, and tissue.
