title: UN Women - Social Policy Consultant (Home-based)
description:
Background:

UN Women, grounded in the vision of equality enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations, works for the elimination of discrimination against women and girls; the empowerment of women; and the achievement of equality between women and men as partners and beneficiaries of development, human rights, humanitarian action and peace and security.

UN Women, grounded in the vision of equality enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations, works for the elimination of discrimination against women and girls; the empowerment of women; and the achievement of equality between women and men as partners and beneficiaries of development, human rights, humanitarian action and peace and security.

Globally, care work is central to social protection, economic resilience, gender equality and sustainable development. Yet unpaid care and domestic work remain largely invisible in policy, budgets and labour markets, despite women’s disproportionate responsibility for childcare, eldercare, care for persons with disabilities, household management and community support. SDG Target 5.4 calls for the recognition and valuation of unpaid care and domestic work through public services, infrastructure and social protection policies, and the promotion of shared responsibility within households and families. SDG Indicator 5.4.1, on the proportion of time spent on unpaid domestic and care work by sex, age and location, provides an essential measure for evidence-based policy reforms.

Regional commitments also provide an important normative basis for advancing comprehensive care systems. The Tlatelolco Commitment reinforces the need to guarantee the right to care, recognize care as a public good and a shared social responsibility, and promote care systems that are universal, comprehensive, rights-based, gender-responsive, intersectional, intercultural and co-responsible between the State, households, communities, the private sector and society as a whole. In this context, Jamaica’s National Care Systems Assessment will support the generation of evidence and recommendations to inform an integrated national approach to care, aligned with the 6Rs of decent care work: recognize, reduce, redistribute, reward, represent and resource care work.

In Jamaica, care policy is closely linked to social protection reform, women’s economic empowerment, labour force participation, decent work, poverty reduction and resilience. Existing evidence points to persistent gender gaps in social protection and care, including women’s heavier unpaid care workload, the concentration of women among beneficiaries and family representatives of social assistance programmes, the gendered implications of conditionalities, and the need for more responsive services for children, older persons, persons with disabilities, caregivers and care workers. Jamaica’s social protection system, including the Programme of Advancement through Health and Education (PATH), provides an important platform for strengthening shock-responsive, inclusive and gender-responsive care-related policy and programming.

Jamaica’s national policy framework provides a strong basis for this assessment. Vision 2030 Jamaica, the country’s long-term national development plan, articulates the national vision of making Jamaica “the place of choice to live, work, raise families and do business” and emphasizes the importance of family well-being, equitable access to education and health care, social protection, poverty reduction, support for vulnerable populations, and the integration of older persons and persons with disabilities within society with access to appropriate care and support services. The Vision 2030 Gender Sector Plan further treats gender as a cross-cutting development issue and provides a basis for mainstreaming gender equality across all national development priorities, including social protection, labour, family life, health, education and community development.

The National Policy for Gender Equality also provides an important policy anchor for the National Care Systems Assessment. It commits Jamaica to gender mainstreaming within a human rights-based framework across State institutions and partnerships with the private sector, non-governmental organizations and civil society. Its focus on transforming gender relations, eliminating discrimination, advancing equal access to opportunities, resources and rewards, addressing poverty and vulnerabilities among women, and ensuring that women and men can participate fully in national development is directly relevant to care policy. These national commitments support the assessment’s focus on unpaid and paid care work, the redistribution of care responsibilities, access to support services, gender-responsive social protection, poverty reduction, and the strengthening of care systems for children, older persons, persons with disabilities, caregivers and care workers.

Jamaica’s climate and disaster policy architecture is also directly relevant to the assessment. The Comprehensive Disaster Risk Management Policy and Strategy 2020–2040 sets out Jamaica’s long-term vision for “A Safe and Resilient Jamaica” and calls for disaster risk management to be mainstreamed across national policies and sectoral planning, including the integration of disaster risk reduction with climate change adaptation. The Climate Change Policy Framework for Jamaica provides a national basis for coordinating adaptation and mitigation across sectors, including human settlements and infrastructure, water resources, agriculture and fisheries, tourism, health, biodiversity, disaster risk financing, land-use planning, communication, public awareness and support to vulnerable populations. These frameworks should inform the assessment’s analysis of how care systems can remain functional before, during and after shocks, and how public services, infrastructure, financing and community systems can reduce the unpaid care burden during climate- and disaster-related disruptions.

The Jamaica Gender and Climate Change Strategy and Action Plan 2022–2025 further strengthens the rationale for linking care systems to climate resilience. It identifies the need for gender-responsive climate action that addresses gender-differentiated needs and capacities, supports equitable participation in climate-related decision-making, and promotes equitable access to the benefits of climate investments. For the National Care Systems Assessment, this means examining how women, men and diverse groups experience climate risks differently; how climate shocks increase unpaid care and domestic work; and how care-related services, such as childcare, eldercare, disability support, health, social protection, WASH and shelter, can be designed as part of Jamaica’s resilience infrastructure.

The assessment must also address the nexus between climate change, disasters and care. As a small island developing state, Jamaica is exposed to climate-related hazards that disrupt care infrastructure, livelihoods, schools, health services, water and sanitation, housing and social protection delivery. Hurricane Melissa underscored how disasters intensify pre-existing gender inequalities and increase unpaid care burdens, particularly for women and girls, caregivers, women-headed households, older persons, persons with disabilities and people living in rural or hard-to-reach communities. The storm’s impacts on displacement, school disruption, housing damage, service access, protection risks, livelihoods and psychosocial well-being demonstrate the need for care systems that are climate-resilient, shock-responsive and grounded in gender equality and human rights.

Within this context, UN Women is seeking to contract a Social Policy Expert to support the Ministry of Labour and Social Security with undertaking a National Care Systems Assessment for Jamaica. Given the gender policy and mainstreaming remit of the Bureau of Gender Affairs, close coordination with the Bureau of Gender Affairs is necessary. The assessment will generate evidence on Jamaica’s care architecture, identify gaps and opportunities across policy, legislation, services, financing, data, governance and implementation, and provide actionable recommendations to inform the development of a national care policy, system or roadmap that advances gender equality, decent care work, climate resilience and inclusive social protection.

Under the overall supervision of the UN Women MCO - Caribbean Representative and directly reporting to the Deputy Representative, the Social Policy Expert will lead the design and implementation of a National Care Systems Assessment for Jamaica in collaboration with and with guidance from the Ministry of Labour and Social Security and in coordination with the Bureau of Gender Affairs. The consultant will assess the current care ecosystem, including unpaid and paid care work, social protection, labour and family-friendly policies, childcare, eldercare, disability care, health and community-based care, domestic work, care infrastructure, care services, disaster response and climate resilience dimensions; and women´s participation in the policy and decision-making processes.

The consultant will apply a gender-responsive, rights-based, intersectional and life-course approach, ensuring alignment with the SDGs, including SDG 5.4 and SDG Indicator 5.4.1; the Tlatelolco Commitment; CEDAW; relevant ILO standards on decent work, social protection, maternity protection, domestic work and care work; and regional and international good practices on comprehensive care systems.

Description of Responsibilities /Scope of Work

The consultant will be responsible for the following areas of work:

  • Policy, legislative and institutional review: Review Jamaica’s policy, legislative, institutional and service delivery frameworks relevant to care, social protection, labour, gender equality, child and family services, health, ageing, disability inclusion, disaster risk management and climate resilience.
  • Care systems mapping: Map the actors, services, programmes, financing mechanisms, coordination arrangements and data systems that shape formal and informal care provision in Jamaica.
  • Gender and intersectional analysis: Analyse how care responsibilities and access to care services differ by sex, age, disability, income, geographic location, household composition, employment status and exposure to disaster risk.
  • Climate change and disaster resilience lens: Analyse the gendered impacts of climate-related shocks, including Hurricane Melissa, on care needs, care infrastructure, social protection access, livelihoods, education, health, WASH, shelter, protection risks and unpaid care burdens, and identify entry points for gender-responsive, inclusive and equitable climate action.
  • 6Rs Framework: Assess opportunities to recognize, reduce, redistribute, reward. represent and resource care work through policies, services, labour protections, financing, social dialogue and institutional reforms.
  • Stakeholder engagement: Design and facilitate inclusive consultations with government ministries and agencies, civil society, women’s rights and women-led organizations, care workers, caregivers, organizations of persons with disabilities, older persons’ representatives, employers’ and workers’ organizations, private sector actors, academia and development partners.
  • Recommendations and roadmap: Develop actionable recommendations and a proposed roadmap for strengthening Jamaica’s national care system and related policies, including through integrated governance, financing, implementation, monitoring and accountability mechanisms and links to climate resilience and shock-responsive social protection.

Expected Deliverables

Deliverables Expected completion time Percentage Payment
Submit an Inception report outlining methodology, analytical framework, workplan, stakeholder map, consultation plan, ethical considerations and proposed outline for the National Care Systems Assessment. Within 10 working days of contract start 5%
Complete a Desk review and report on Jamaica’s policy, legislative, institutional, financing, service delivery and data context on care, including Vision 2030 Jamaica, the Vision 2030 Gender Sector Plan, the National Policy for Gender Equality, the Jamaica Social Protection Strategy, the Comprehensive Disaster Risk Management Policy and Strategy 2020–2040, the Climate Change Policy Framework for Jamaica, the Jamaica Gender and Climate Change Strategy and Action Plan 2022–2025, relevant disaster response and recovery plans, sector policies and legislation, social protection, labour, gender equality, childcare, eldercare, disability care, health, education, social services, disaster risk management, climate resilience and unpaid care work measurement, including SDG 5.4.1. Within 20 working days of contract start 14%
Complete a Care Systems Mapping that identifies key actors, programmes, services, coordination mechanisms, financing arrangements, data gaps and existing entry points for a comprehensive national care system. Within 25 working days of contract start 10%
Draft qualitative tools for focus group discussions and key informant interviews, including tailored instruments for caregivers, care workers, women’s organizations, men and boys, older persons, persons with disabilities, youth, employers, workers’ organizations, including domestic workers’ unions/networks, service providers and government stakeholders. Within 25 working days of contract start 14%
Prepare a summary report from stakeholder consultations and qualitative data collection, including analysis of care needs, unpaid care burdens, paid care work, social norms, access barriers, climate and disaster-related care pressures, and the impact of Hurricane Melissa on care systems and caregivers. Within 40 working days of contract start 14%
Draft a National Care Systems Assessment for Jamaica, including situational analysis, policy and legislative gaps, institutional and financing analysis, care service mapping, climate and disaster resilience analysis, and recommendations structured around the 5Rs of decent care work. Within 45 working days of contract start 15%
Prepare a presentation highlighting draft findings to UN Women and the leadership of the Ministry of Labour and Social Security, Bureau of Gender Affairs and other national stakeholders Within 50 working days of contract start 10%
Jointly facilitate, with Ministry of Labour and Social Security, a validation consultation and preparation of a short validation summary detailing the outcomes of the consultation. Within 50 working days of contract start 10%
Prepare a Final National Care Systems Assessment for Jamaica incorporating feedback, with an executive summary, prioritized recommendations and proposed roadmap for policy, programme, financing, governance, monitoring and accountability actions. Within 60 working days of contract start 8%
TOTAL 100%

Consultant’s Workplace and Official Travel

This is a home-based consultancy. As part of this assignment, the Consultant will be expected to conduct virtual consultations and may be required to support in-person stakeholder consultations in Jamaica, subject to confirmation by UN Women and the availability of resources.

Competencies :

Core Values:

  • Integrity;
  • Professionalism;
  • Respect for Diversity.

Core Competencies:

  • Awareness and Sensitivity Regarding Gender Issues;
  • Accountability;
  • Creative Problem Solving;
  • Effective Communication;
  • Inclusive Collaboration;
  • Stakeholder Engagement;
  • Leading by Example.

Please visit this link for more information on UN Women’s Values and Competencies Framework:

Functional Competencies:

  • Strong social policy, gender analysis and care economy expertise.
  • Demonstrated ability to conduct policy, legislative, institutional and service delivery assessments.
  • Excellent qualitative research, facilitation and stakeholder consultation skills.
  • Strong understanding of gender-responsive social protection, unpaid and paid care work, decent work and labour rights.
  • Familiarity with SDGs, including SDG 5.4.1, the 5Rs framework, the Tlatelolco Commitment, CEDAW and relevant ILO standards.
  • Ability to analyse the links between climate change, disaster risk, humanitarian response, social protection and care systems.
  • Excellent written and oral communication skills, including the ability to present complex analysis and recommendations clearly to policy and technical audiences.

Required Qualifications

Education and Certification:

  • A Master’s degree in Social Policy, Public Policy, Social Sciences, Economics, Gender and Development, Development Studies, Public Health, Labour Studies or a related field is required.

OR

  • A first-level university degree in combination with two additional years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

  • At least (7) five years of progressively responsible experience in social policy, gender equality, social protection, care economy, labour policy, disability inclusion, child and family policy or related fields nine (9) years' experience with a Bachelor’s degree is required.
  • Demonstrated experience conducting national assessments, policy analyses, institutional reviews, qualitative research or stakeholder consultations is required.
  • Experience working on care systems, unpaid care work, paid care work, family-friendly policies, childcare, eldercare, disability care or domestic work is required.
  • Experience integrating gender-responsive, intersectional and rights-based approaches into policy and programme design is required.
  • Experience working in Jamaica or the Caribbean region is highly desirable.
  • Experience analysing climate resilience, disaster risk management, humanitarian response or shock-responsive social protection from a gender perspective is desirable.
  • Prior experience working with government institutions, UN agencies, civil society, women’s organizations, workers’ organizations or employers’ organizations is desirable.

Languages:

  • Fluency in written and oral English is required.

title: Logistics Clerk- Inventory Property Control
description:
Stratolaunch is a technology accelerator that engineers operationally realistic testing at Mach 5+. Our air-launched, Talon testbeds are reusable, cost-effective platforms that enable routine access to the hypersonic environment. We deliver flight data critical to validating system performance and achieving rapid technology deployment. Together with our customers, we drive innovations that are imperative to advancing national security.

We are seeking a detail-oriented Logistics Clerk to accurately track and manage our carrier aircraft inventory. In this role, you will ensure materials and supplies are properly received, stored, and issued while maintaining precise records that support efficient operations. This position is vital to the supply chain, helping safeguard stock integrity, enabling production and operations teams, and driving continuous improvement in inventory management practices.

ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Establish, maintain, and audit a compliant Property Control System for all company assets (storage, tracking, security, and accounting).
  • Implement and manage inventory recording and control systems; coordinate the movement of parts, equipment, and supplies across organizations.
  • Analyze work in area, determine priorities and sequence work based on customer requirements.
  • Develop, document, and continuously improve processes and procedures for inventory and logistics operations.
  • Receive, verify, and log incoming shipments; investigate and resolve discrepancies.
  • Maintain accurate inventory levels and support kitting and material distribution planning.
  • Manage shop supply needs, including ordering, receiving, and proper storage.
  • Support project management activities such as scoping, scheduling, resource planning, and contract coordination.
  • Prepare and execute audit plans; resolve compliance issues related to property and inventory.
  • Safely handle and store hazardous materials in accordance with applicable regulations.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Minimum 1 year of experience in warehouse or logistics operations.

title: Ekstern lektor indenfor formueret
description:
En stilling som ekstern lektor inden for Formueret ved CBS Law er ledig til besættelse den 1. januar 2027.

Som ekstern lektor har du mulighed for at anvende din viden til at uddanne unge mennesker og give dem et indblik i dine praktiske erfaringer. På CBS er de eksterne lektorer et vigtigt supplement til forskernes undervisning. Funktionen som ekstern lektor giver dig desuden mulighed for at opdatere din teoretiske viden, diskutere med ambitiøse studerende og blive del af et internationalt fagligt miljø.

Der er tale om en midlertidig deltidsstilling, som er tidsbegrænset for tre år, med mulighed for forlængelse inden for rammerne af lov om tidsbegrænset ansættelse.

Stillingen omfatter (eksempler)

  • Tilrettelægge og gennemføre undervisning i formueret.
  • Online undervisning – blended learning.
  • Vejledning af de studerende.
  • Udarbejdelse af undervisningsmateriale og eksamensopgaver.
  • Gennemførelse af eksaminer og andre evalueringer.

Kvalifikationer

Kvalifikationskravet er kandidatniveau og ansættelse som ekstern lektor forudsætter:

  • Relevant praksiserfaring på højt niveau, der ikke er opnået gennem en universitær, videnskabelig ansættelse, eller
  • Ansættelse i en videnskabelig hovedstilling på et andet universitet (En hovedstilling er en ansættelse som adjunkt/forsker, lektor/seniorforsker eller professor/professor MSO).
  • En ekstern lektor, som ansættes i kraft af sin relevante praksiserfaring, skal have indgående, aktuel viden om fagets/fagområdets anvendelsesmuligheder. Det opnås/er opnået gennem beskæftigelse inden for faget/fagområdet.
  • Derudover forudsætter ansættelse som ekstern lektor, at undervisningsmæssige kvalifikationer indgår i bedømmelsen af ansøgere til et eksternt lektorat.

Dine øvrige kompetencer

  • Ud over relevant kandidateksamen, lægges der vægt på specialisering samt faglig kompetence inden for de respektive kursers indhold.
  • Som person har du gode samarbejdsevner og evner at bidrage til et godt arbejdsmiljø.
  • Undervisning og vejledning skal kunne gennemføres på dansk. Undervisning og vejledning kan efter aftale skulle ske på engelsk.

Stillingsindhold og kvalifikationskrav er yderligere beskrevet i bekendtgørelse om stillingsstruktur for videnskabeligt personale ved universiteter.

Ansættelsesforhold

Løn og ansættelse sker i henhold til Aftale om Eksterne lektorer ved universiteter m.fl. under Uddannelses- og Forskningsministeriet. Antallet af arbejdstimer er max 500 timer pr. studieår og kan variere efter behov i de enkelte semestre. Timetallet fastsættes to gange om året og aflønning sker på baggrund heraf.

I forbindelse med ansættelse som ekstern lektor skal du gennemgå et pædagogisk introduktionskursus til universitetspædagogik arrangeret af CBS.

Du vil blive tilknyttet en forsker på instituttet som vil være din faglige kontaktperson. Du forventes at deltage i faglige arrangementer med relevans for den undervisning, du varetager, og du vil desuden blive en del af instituttets netværk af eksterne undervisere.

Rekrutteringsprocessen

Copenhagen Business School inviterer alle kvalificerede kandidater til at søge stillingen. Et ansættelsesudvalg vil vurdere ansøgningerne og indkalde et udvalg af kvalificerede kandidater til samtale.

Et af CBS’ strategiske mål er at fremme mangfoldighed og diversitet i vores organisation. Derfor bestræber vi os på en ansættelsesproces, der mindsker potentiel bias. Vi opfordrer derfor ansøgere til ikke at inkludere foto eller unødvendige oplysninger om personlige forhold i ansøgningen.

Yderligere oplysninger

Hvis du vil vide mere om stillingsindholdet, er du velkommen til at kontakte Professor Kim Østergaard på kos.bhl@cbs.dk eller telefon 2912 6077.

Din ansøgning

Du søger stillingen online, hvor du udfylder ansøgningsformularen samt vedhæfter:

  • Motiveret ansøgning
  • CV
  • Eksamensbevis
  • Undervisningsportfolio
  • Publikationsliste, hvis relevant for stillingen

Du kan finde yderligere information om CBS og instituttet på .

WE TRANSFORM SOCIETY WITH BUSINESS

CBS er et globalt anerkendt businessuniversitet med dybe rødder i den nordiske, socioøkonomiske model. Vi har et bredt fokus på erhvervslivets og samfundets udfordringer i det 21. århundrede. Derfor har vi en samlet portefølje af tværfaglig forskning og uddannelse af høj kvalitet, der har styrket generationer af fagfolk og ledere i den private sektor og andre steder.

Universitetet ligger på Frederiksberg og har ca. 20.000 fuldtids- og deltidsstuderende, 800 fuldtidsansatte videnskabelige medarbejdere, 200 ph.d.-studerende og 700 administrative medarbejdere samt en portefølje af bachelor-, kandidat-, MBA/EMBA-, ph.d.-og efter-/videreuddannelser udbudt på både dansk og engelsk.

Med vores globale profil følger en forpligtelse til at bidrage til udviklingen af transformative kompetencer hos studerende, kandidater og virksomhedsledere gennem vores uddannelsesaktiviteter og muligheder for livslang læring. Komplekse udfordringer kræver en fælles indsats, og derfor fokuserer vores strategi på at styrke nuværende og starte nye partnerskaber med andre videnskaber, erhvervslivet, myndigheder og civilsamfundet.

CBS arbejder kontinuerligt med at blive en mangfoldig og inkluderende organisation, og vi opfordrer alle uanset kønsidentitet og -udtryk, alder, etnicitet, religiøs overbevisning, LGBT+-status, kulturel baggrund m.m. at søge.
Kontakt os, hvis du har brug for assistance i søge- eller ansættelsesprocessen, hvis der er noget vi skal vide, eller hvis du som person med handicap ønsker at gøre brug af din fortrinsret.

title: Lead Substation Engineer
description:
AECOM is seeking a Lead Substation Engineer to join our growing Energy practice in a remote role based anywhere in the United States. This position offers the opportunity to lead the design and delivery of critical transmission, distribution, renewable energy, and grid modernization projects while working alongside some of the industry's top engineering professionals.

As a technical leader within AECOM's Power Delivery team, you will play a key role in helping utilities and energy clients navigate an evolving energy landscape by delivering innovative, reliable, and resilient substation solutions.

Whether supporting grid expansion, renewable energy integration, or infrastructure modernization, you'll have the flexibility of a remote work environment while contributing to impactful projects across North America.

The Opportunity

As a Lead Substation Engineer, you will provide technical leadership for the planning, design, and delivery of utility-scale substation projects. Working with multidisciplinary teams, clients, and project managers, you will support projects from concept development through construction while ensuring technical excellence, quality, and client satisfaction.

This role is ideal for an experienced engineer who enjoys solving complex technical challenges, mentoring others, and building strong client relationships while contributing to the continued growth of AECOM's Energy business.

What You'll Do

Technical Leadership

  • Lead the engineering and design of transmission and distribution substation projects for utility, renewable energy, and industrial clients
  • Provide technical guidance and oversight for substation physical design, protection and control integration, grounding systems, equipment layouts, and power delivery infrastructure
  • Support the development and review of one-line diagrams, protection schemes, equipment specifications, construction packages, and design documentation
  • Apply engineering expertise throughout project phases including planning, conceptual design, detailed design, procurement, and construction support
  • Support engineering studies and analyses related to grounding, equipment sizing, fault current evaluations, and substation design considerations
  • Stay current with evolving technologies, industry standards, and utility practices related to substations, grid modernization, and power delivery systems
  • Build standards across processes and practices

Project Delivery

  • Lead engineering tasks and coordinate multidisciplinary project teams to deliver high-quality work on schedule and within budget
  • Support project planning, resource coordination, technical reviews, and project execution activities
  • Provide technical oversight for substation upgrades, expansions, brownfield modifications, and greenfield projects
  • Collaborate with project managers to identify and mitigate risks while maintaining project objectives and client expectations
  • Support construction activities through technical consultation, design clarifications, and resolution of field issues

Client Engagement & Business Development

  • Build strong relationships with utility, renewable energy, and industrial clients
  • Participate in client meetings, technical workshops, presentations, and project reviews
  • Support proposal development, scope definition, cost estimates, and pursuit efforts
  • Identify opportunities to expand services and strengthen long-term client partnerships
  • Collaborate with regional and national teams to support strategic growth initiatives

Collaboration & Mentorship

  • Mentor engineers and designers while supporting technical development and knowledge sharing
  • Collaborate with civil, structural, transmission, protection and control, and program management teams
  • Contribute to engineering best practices and continuous improvement initiatives across the Energy practice
  • Foster a culture of technical excellence, innovation, safety, and collaboration

Why AECOM

AECOM is the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, delivering professional services throughout the project lifecycle. Our Energy practice helps clients modernize the electric grid, integrate renewable energy resources, improve reliability, and support the transition to a more sustainable future.

As part of AECOM, you'll enjoy:

  • Remote/hybrid work flexibility
  • Opportunities to work on industry-leading energy projects
  • Access to a global network of technical experts
  • Career growth, leadership development, and professional training opportunities
  • Competitive compensation and comprehensive benefits
  • A collaborative culture focused on innovation, inclusion, and technical excellence

Join AECOM and help deliver the next generation of energy infrastructure.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or a related discipline with +10 years of experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education
  • Professional Engineer (PE) license
  • Experience supporting transmission and distribution substation projects
  • Experience with electrical engineering principles, utility infrastructure, and power delivery systems
  • Experience leading engineering tasks, reviewing technical deliverables, and coordinating project teams
  • Experience and knowledge working with industry standards and codes such as IEEE, NESC, and NEC
  • Experience with industry-standard engineering and design software such as AutoCAD, MicroStation, ETAP, Aspen, CAPE, or similar tools
  • Willingness to travel periodically for project, client, and team needs

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Advanced degree in Engineering or a related technical field.
  • Strong communication, leadership, and client relationship skills.
  • Experience supporting utility, renewable energy, grid modernization, or energy transition projects.
  • Experience mentoring engineers and contributing to technical leadership initiatives.
  • Familiarity with substation physical design, protection and control systems, SCADA integration, or related power system applications.
  • Visa Sponsorship is not available for this role, now or in the future
  • Relocation is not available for this role

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

About AECOM

AECOM is proud to offer comprehensive benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Depending on your employment status, AECOM benefits may include medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, disability benefits, paid time off, leaves of absences, voluntary benefits, perks, flexible work options, well-being resources, employee assistance program, business travel insurance, service recognition awards, retirement savings plan, and employee stock purchase plan.

AECOM is the global infrastructure leader, committed to delivering a better world. As a trusted professional services firm powered by deep technical abilities, we solve our clients’ complex challenges in water, environment, energy, transportation and buildings. Our teams partner with public- and private-sector clients to create innovative, sustainable and resilient solutions throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm that had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. Learn more at aecom.com.

What makes AECOM a great place to work

You will be part of a global team that champions your growth and career ambitions. Work on groundbreaking projects - both in your local community and on a global scale - that are transforming our industry and shaping the future. With cutting-edge technology and a network of experts, you’ll have the resources to make a real impact. Our award-winning training and development programs are designed to expand your technical expertise and leadership skills, helping you build the career you’ve always envisioned. Here, you’ll find a welcoming workplace built on respect, collaboration and community—where you have the freedom to grow in a world of opportunity.

As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we believe in your potential and are here to help you achieve it. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

Work with Us. Change the World.

At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the worldâs most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.

There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

title: Portfolio Manager, GRC Risk Operations
description:
Job Summary:

WHO ARE WE?

Live Nation Entertainment is the world’s leading live entertainment company, comprised of global market leaders: Ticketmaster, Live Nation Concerts, and Live Nation Media & Sponsorship. Ticketmaster is the global leader in event ticketing with over 620 million tickets sold annually and approximately 10,000 clients worldwide. Live Nation Concerts is the largest provider of live entertainment in the world promoting more than 50,000 events annually for nearly 7,000 artists in 40+ countries. These businesses allow Live Nation Media & Sponsorship to create strategic music marketing programs that connect more than 1,200 sponsors with the 145 million fans that attend Live Nation Entertainment events each year. For additional information, visit .

WHO ARE YOU?

Passionate and motivated. Driven, with an entrepreneurial spirit. Resourceful, innovative, forward thinking and committed. At Live Nation Entertainment, our people embrace these qualities, so if this sounds like you then please read on!

THE ROLE

The Portfolio Manager, GRC Risk Operations is a hands-on player-coach responsible for the end-to-end operational health and delivery of an assigned Risk Operations portfolio. This role combines direct risk assessment execution, first-line quality assurance, intake and workload management, business engagement, reporting, project delivery, and people leadership.


The Portfolio Manager will directly manage risk analysts and oversee AI agents that support portfolio execution, creating a blended human-and-AI delivery model. The Portfolio Manager remains actively involved in the work, including completing assessments, QAing analyst deliverables, managing stakeholder communications and escalations, and driving projects and operational improvements. The role is accountable for ensuring work is prioritized, completed with quality, communicated clearly, and continuously improved in alignment with program requirements and broader security, privacy, compliance, and business priorities.


WHAT THIS ROLE WILL DO

  • Own day-to-day operational delivery and overall health of an assigned portfolio, including intake, prioritization, workload allocation, backlog, cycle time, service levels, remediation, escalations, and stakeholder responsiveness.
  • Personally perform third-party risk assessments across the full assessment lifecycle, including standard, complex, Critical/High, expedited, fast-track, and escalated reviews as needed; review supplier documentation and evidence, identify risk, document findings, develop remediation requirements, support exceptions, and communicate assessment conclusions.
  • Perform first-line QA of analyst-completed assessments for completeness, accuracy, evidence quality, consistency, risk judgment, and adherence to standards; provide actionable feedback and coaching, identify recurring quality trends, and escalate work requiring independent final approval in accordance with program governance.
  • Manage, coach, and develop team of risk analysts, including work assignment, capacity planning, performance support, skill development, and guidance on complex assessments, remediation, exceptions, and stakeholder issues.
  • Lead portfolio intake support by reviewing incoming requests, confirming completeness, assessing urgency and complexity, aligning work to analyst capacity and expertise, and resolving or escalating intake issues that create delays or duplicate effort.
  • Serve as a primary operational point of contact for business leaders, internal stakeholders, and external suppliers; provide portfolio-level updates, manage escalations, clarify next steps and timelines, and translate requirements into clear business-facing communications.
  • Develop, gather, validate, and communicate portfolio metrics, dashboards, and status reporting, using data to monitor SLA achievement, backlog health, cycle time, workload, remediation, quality trends, stakeholder experience, and emerging portfolio risks; provide clear portfolio-health updates and recommended actions to leadership and business stakeholders.
  • Lead or support projects and workstreams by defining scope, timelines, deliverables, owners, dependencies, risks, action items, and status; maintain project plans and schedules, coordinate cross-functional execution, translate operational needs into actionable requirements, and drive adoption of new processes, tools, controls, and program initiatives.
  • Manage AI agents used to support portfolio operations by identifying appropriate use cases, directing and monitoring AI-enabled work, reviewing output quality, defining human-review and escalation requirements, and measuring operational value. Partner with the Technical Administrator and governance resources on agent configuration, integrations, controls, and technical enhancements while retaining accountability for how agents are used within the portfolio.
  • Drive continuous improvement across assessment workflows, intake, reporting, communications, quality, and automation by identifying recurring friction, rework, capacity constraints, stakeholder pain points, and control gaps and translating those findings into practical operational improvements that improve portfolio health and scalability.

WHAT THIS PERSON WILL BRING

  • 8+ years of experience in third-party risk management, information security, compliance, operational risk, audit, vendor risk, or a related risk discipline.
  • 3+ years of experience in portfolio management, program/project management, business engagement, or operational leadership, with demonstrated ability to manage multiple workstreams and competing priorities.
  • 2+ years of people leadership or direct management experience, including coaching, workload management, performance support, and development of analysts or comparable risk professionals.
  • Hands-on experience conducting third-party risk assessments and evaluating supplier evidence, control environments, findings, remediation plans, exceptions, and ongoing due diligence.
  • Experience reviewing or QAing risk assessment work and providing clear, consistent feedback that improves quality and analyst capability.
  • Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, including the ability to translate risk concepts for technical and non-technical audiences and provide clear portfolio-level reporting and escalation updates.
  • Strong project management skills, including experience managing scope, schedules, dependencies, risks, action items, and cross-functional delivery; experience with tools such as Asana, Jira, Smartsheet, or similar is preferred.
  • Experience using metrics, dashboards, reporting platforms, workflow automation, or AI-enabled tools to improve operational visibility, efficiency, and scalability; experience overseeing AI-supported workflows or agent-based automation is preferred.
  • Working knowledge of common security, privacy, and compliance frameworks and requirements such as NIST, ISO 27001, PCI, SOX, and GDPR.
  • Ability to exercise sound judgment in a fast-paced global environment, balance hands-on execution with leadership responsibilities, and manage sensitive or confidential information with discretion.
  • Relevant certifications such as CTPRP/CTPRA, CRISC, CISA, CISM and PMP, CAPM, Certified ScrumMaster, or comparable risk/project management credentials are preferred.

If the above description sounds like you and fits your background, apply online at to join the Live Nation Entertainment team today!


Applicants for employment in the U.S. must possess work authorization which does not require sponsorship by the employer for a visa.

title: Manufacturing Programmer
description:
Company Overview

The Montague Company is a proud family-owned manufacturer with a rich history dating back over 150 years. Renowned for its commitment to quality craftsmanship and innovative design, the company specializes in producing high-end commercial cooking equipment that meets the needs of professional kitchens worldwide.

Job Overview

We are seeking a dynamic Manufacturing Programmer to join our team and drive excellence in our manufacturing processes. In this role, you will develop, optimize, and implement CNC (Computer Numerical Control) programs for various machining operations, ensuring precision and efficiency. Your expertise will help us maintain our tradition of superior quality while embracing modern manufacturing techniques.

Duties

  • Develop and write CNC programs for multi-axis CNC milling machines, including 5-axis CNC machines, using CAM software and CAD (Computer-Aided Design) tools such as AutoCAD, SolidWorks, and CATIA.
  • Interpret mechanical blueprints, schematics, and engineering drawings to determine machining requirements and tooling specifications.
  • Set up machining tools and fixtures on CNC lathes, mills, and other equipment like Fanuc-controlled machines to ensure accurate production runs.
  • Optimize machining processes through lean manufacturing principles to reduce waste and improve throughput.
  • Conduct precision measurements using calipers, bore gauges, micrometers, coordinate measuring machines (CMM), and other measurement instruments to verify part accuracy.
  • Troubleshoot programming issues and machine malfunctions promptly to minimize downtime.
  • Collaborate with engineering teams on CAD design modifications and ensure manufacturing processes align with design intent and GD&T (Geometric Dimensioning & Tolerancing) standards.
